title: legalize accepts overlapping or out-of-bounds placements as clean
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] finding 2. legalize.rs nearest_free checks origin-to-origin distance using unrotated extents, while rules.rs placed_box applies back-flip, rotate_local, quarter-turn swaps, and origin_offset. Reproduced clean report with RV1/SW1 overlapping by 5.07mm and with excessive travel on a 40mm board. Also check ring-search board bounds and missing footprint facts; acceptance should use placed_box plus gap_between >= -TOLERANCE_MM.
close_reason: Fixed nearest_free candidate acceptance so legalization only accepts spots that both avoid placed-box collisions and satisfy this part's physical rules. Added regression for occupied edge target choosing an off-board ring-search candidate. Verified cargo fmt --check, cargo test -p legion-of-bom-core legalize, cargo test -p legion-of-bom-core, and cargo clippy -p legion-of-bom-core --all-targets -- -D warnings.

title: Panel cutouts silently stack when 3U controls overflow vertical band
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] finding 1. min_panel_hp_for sizes 3U panels by width only, so a column of panel controls can exceed the 105.5mm vertical band. Overflow is clamped to the same y coordinate, producing coincident cutouts and self-overlapping Edge.Cuts. Reproduced with 8-10 Thonkiconn jacks at 4HP. Fix should make panel sizing/checking account for vertical pitch capacity and fail or widen before duplicate cutouts are emitted.
close_reason: Already fixed in current tree: 3U min_panel_hp_for sizes by required columns, derive_panel_for balances columns, and duplicate cutout regression tests pass. Verified with cargo test -p legion-of-bom-core a_crowded_panel.

title: legalize creates the overlap it was repairing around: nearest_free ignores rotation and origin_offset
description:
Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] item 2. FIXED 2026-08-12.

nearest_free's clash test compared placement ORIGIN to ORIGIN with UNROTATED extents. The
checker it must satisfy, rules::placed_box, applies the back-flip, rotate_local, the
quarter-turn extent swap AND origin_offset. An Alpha pot's origin is pin 1, ~5.35mm from its
body centre, so the two disagreed by that much on every Eurorack board. Legalization would
declare a spot free, move a part there, and hand back a clean report on interpenetrating
bodies.

MEASURED, and the fixture had to be FOUND rather than reasoned out — two hand-built guesses
did not reproduce it. New examples/legalize_probe.rs sweeps rotation x both x positions:

  BEFORE  rot 0, pot_x 38, sw_x 28: RV1 moved 22.100mm -> overlap margin -5.065
  AFTER   rot 0, pot_x 38, sw_x 28: RV1 moved  3.100mm -> overlap margin +0.435

Note the travel as well as the overlap: 22.1mm down to 3.1mm. The old code was escaping a
PHANTOM keep-out — the wrong geometry told it the nearby spots were taken — which is what broke
the module's stated minimum-disturbance contract. Every rotation-0 case in the sweep is now
clear; the four still flagged are ones legalize was never asked to repair (no Overlap rule
supplied, edge rule already satisfied) and are the probe's own check, not a defect.

WHY IT WAS AT ROTATION ZERO, not 90 as I first assumed: at 90 the offset rotates out of the
line between the two parts. It is origin_offset that bites, not the rotation. Worth knowing —
I built two fixtures on the rotation theory and both passed.

FIX: nearest_free now asks the geometry question the way the rule asks it —
gap_between(placed_box(..), placed_box(..)) < -TOLERANCE_MM. placed_box, gap_between and
TOLERANCE_MM became pub(crate). The tolerance matters for the same reason rules needs it:
escape_target returns precisely the touching distance, so an exact tie is the COMMON case and
the two sides reach it by different summation orders. placed_box also now uses
board::quarter_turns rather than its own inline copy ([[legion-of-bom-4t9]]).

SECOND DEFECT in the same function, also fixed: a part with no measured facts short-circuited
to Some(target) — moved with NO collision check at all. It now treats itself as a POINT and
still checks against parts it does know. Callers legitimately pass an empty facts map and rely
on the rule's own repair target, and that keeps working.

TEST legalize_does_not_create_an_overlap_while_repairing_an_edge, on the measured fixture. My
first version of it was a TAUTOLOGY and I caught it only because it passed: it asserted
report.is_clean() against rules::assess over the same rule list legalize computes  from,
so it could not fail however wrong the placement was. The rules are now deliberately split —
only the edge rule goes in, the overlap is checked afterwards — and the precondition that RV1
actually moved is asserted.

STILL OPEN from z8c item 2: the ring search has no board-bounds check and can return a point
outside bounds. Untouched here.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: Typo from shell backtick expansion when filing: the test paragraph should read "...over the same rule list legalize computes its stuck list from". The word was eaten. Second time this session — bd descriptions filed from a shell should avoid backticks entirely.

title: Panel cutouts silently stack: min_panel_hp_for sizes a 3U column by width only
description:
Split from the robustness-audit holding bead. FIXED 2026-08-12 in the same session; recording it as its own bead because the holding bead is a pen, not a record.

min_panel_hp_for's 3U branch sized the panel by widest + 2*EDGE_MM — WIDTH ONLY. A 3U panel is
a COLUMN, and nothing checked the column of pitches against the ~105mm vertical band. The
overflow was absorbed by derive_panel_for's .clamp(avail_bot, avail_top), which pins every
control past the end of the column to exactly avail_bot.

REPRODUCED to three decimals: 8 Thonkiconn jacks at 4 HP put J7 AND J8 both at
(10.160, 12.000). 10 jacks give 3 coincident pairs. min_panel_hp_for returned 3, so the CLI's
'widened to N HP' line never fired — nothing anywhere said a word.

It reached the manufactured artifacts: write_dxf emitted two identical CIRCLE entities and
panel_to_kicad_pcb two identical inner Edge.Cuts loops — a self-overlapping outline the panel
shop resolves however it likes, and one jack with no hole at all. eurorack_trial_build also
anchored two jacks at one point.

FIX: the 3U branch now sizes for the COLUMNS the stack needs, as the exact inverse of
derive_panel_for's fits_wide — which is what makes the two agree, since the width it asks for
is by construction a width that fits those columns. The usable height depends on the margins,
which depend on HP, which is what is being solved for; there are only two margin buckets and
each pass only widens, so it settles at once, bounded at 4 passes anyway.

Also added a debug_assert at the end of the 3U branch: two cutouts at one point means sizing
and layout have disagreed again. Debug-only — a release build should not abort a derive. The
clamp stays as a floor with a comment saying it is not a layout strategy.

TEST a_crowded_panel_never_puts_two_controls_in_one_place, over 8/10/14 jacks at 4 HP: no two
cutouts coincide, the emitted HP is at least the stated minimum, and everything is on the
panel. It failed before the fix with exactly the reproduced coordinates.

NO REGRESSION on real work: slew_limiter still derives 6 HP in a single column.
close_reason: Closed

title: [holding] Robustness audit 2026-08-12 — 14 findings, most reproduced against the crate; split into real beads
description:
HOLDING PEN, to be split. Filed as one bead so 14 verified findings survive; each numbered item below deserves its own. [R] = the auditor executed it against the crate, not inferred.

1. [R] P0-ish PANEL CUTOUTS SILENTLY STACK. panel.rs:1256, root cause :1045-1053 and :1223.
   min_panel_hp_for's 3U branch sizes by WIDTH ONLY (widest + 2*EDGE_MM); nothing checks the
   column of pitches against the 105.5mm vertical band. Overflow is absorbed by
   clamp(avail_bot, avail_top), pinning every control that does not fit to the SAME point.
   Executed: 8 Thonkiconn at 4 HP -> J7 and J8 both at exactly (10.160, 12.000); 10 jacks give
   3 coincident pairs. min_panel_hp_for returns 3 so the 'widened to N HP' message never fires.
   write_dxf then emits two identical CIRCLEs and panel_to_kicad_pcb two identical inner
   Edge.Cuts loops — a self-overlapping outline the panel shop resolves however it likes, and
   one jack has no hole. eurorack_trial_build anchors two jacks at one point.

2. [R] LEGALIZE ACCEPTS INTERPENETRATING BODIES AND REPORTS CLEAN. legalize.rs:160-161 vs
   rules.rs:687-702. nearest_free's clash test uses placement origin to origin with UNROTATED
   extents; the checker it must satisfy (placed_box) applies back-flip, rotate_local, the
   quarter-turn swap and origin_offset. An Alpha pot's origin_offset is ~5.35mm and
   control_rotation emits 90 deg for pots, so both discrepancies are live on every Eurorack
   board. Reproduced: report is_clean()==true while RV1 and SW1 overlap by 5.07mm; and the same
   fixture reports clean after 44.095mm of travel on a 40mm board, destroying the module's
   minimum-disturbance contract. Two more in the same function: the ring search has no
   board-bounds check and can return a point outside bounds; facts.get(refdes) missing ->
   return Some(target) teleports the part with zero collision checking.
   NOTE: the auditor confirms the 1e-14 refusal IS fixed — TOLERANCE_MM=1e-6 (rules.rs:457) is
   applied and inherited correctly everywhere. This is the repair PRODUCER, one layer down:
   legalize.rs:161 makes an independent accept/reject with a bare '<' against a threshold summed
   in a different order than escape_target computed the target with, and escape_target returns
   precisely the touching distance, so an exact tie is the COMMON case. Fix: nearest_free should
   call gap_between(placed_box(..), placed_box(..)) >= -TOLERANCE_MM.

3. AN ERC THAT NEVER RAN REPORTS CLEAN. validate.rs:14-34. read_to_string().ok() swallows a read
   failure into passed; an EMPTY erc file matches no prefix so the stage returns passed plus an
   affirmative Finding::info. out/daisy_demo, out/dfm_fanout, out/patch_sm_demo, out/mpn_probe,
   out/daisy_panel_demo all hold 0-byte .erc files RIGHT NOW. skidl.rs:214 guards the sibling
   case ('exited 0 but produced no netlist'); the next line does not.

4. lob fab PUTS EVERY THT PART BACK IN THE ASSEMBLY BOM ON A PARSE FAILURE. cli/main.rs:1437-1445.
   guide::parse_board(...).map(...).unwrap_or_default() — an Err yields an empty hand_soldered set
   and jlc_bom_csv filters nothing. Silent both ways: 'if !hand_soldered.is_empty()' also
   suppresses the summary line, so the operator sees neither the withheld count nor an error.
   This is MY code from this session. Pairs with [[legion-of-bom-g5a]].

5. A SOCKETED OP-AMP OR ANY JFET IS DELETED FROM THE SPICE DECK AND THE SIM STILL REPORTS NUMBERS.
   spice.rs:421-438 used at :330. is_electrical_noop skips a part before model resolution if its
   footprint contains 'socket' — DIP-8_W7.62mm_Socket is the normal DIY op-amp mounting and exists
   in the KiCad library we resolve against — or if its refdes starts with 'J', which is the
   standard designator for a JFET. It never reaches the 'no SPICE model' error, so the AC sweep is
   a measurement of a circuit with its active device removed.

6. SIMULATOR FAILURE RETURNS A PASSING STAGE — the StageOutcome/StageError contract inverted.
   cli/main.rs:548-551 and :656-665: Err(e) => StageOutcome::passed(...).with(Finding::warning).
   Every StageError (ToolNotFound, ToolFailed, 'produced no transient data points') becomes a pass
   and lob run exits 0. Also bypasses check_channel_crosstalk's own vacuous-pass guard. Root cause:
   nothing in production implements trait Stage, so nothing type-forces the distinction.

7. A NON-USD MOUSER PRICE IS SILENTLY 100x WRONG AND PRINTED WITH A '$'. mouser.rs:226-231.
   parse_price keeps only ASCII digits and '.', so '1,48 EUR' -> '148' -> 148.0.
   PriceBreak.currency is captured at :198 and NEVER READ anywhere in the workspace. Flows to
   Bom::total() and is formatted as ${v:.2}.

8. A DRC REPORT THAT ISN'T ONE PARSES AS CLEAN AND lob fab SHIPS ON IT. drc.rs:21-32, 81-83,
   127-129. All three vectors are #[serde(default)], so ANY JSON object deserializes to zero
   violations and is_clean()==true — enshrined by the test at :237 (from_json("{}") -> clean).
   A truncated write or a renamed key in a newer kicad-cli prints 'DRC: 0 error(s)' and the
   package is written. Same shape as the stale-file bug drc.rs:141-145 already defends against.

9. [R] GERBER APERTURE PARSING panics and misreads legal D-codes. gerber.rs:285-292 slices by the
   length of the REPARSED number, not the digit run consumed. '%ADD*%' -> PANIC (start byte index
   1 out of bounds), reachable from web/src/render.rs:330 on a user-supplied directory.
   '%ADD010R,2.0X1.0*%' (leading zeros are legal RS-274X) -> a 2.0x1.0mm rect pad renders as a
   2.0mm CIRCLE, silently.

10. [R] EXCELLON READER: zero-diameter tools, inch files read as mm, dropped holes. gerber.rs:651,
    :655, :666-672, :696. 'T01C0.800F00S00' (Altium/DipTrace/older KiCad) fails parse() and
    unwrap_or(0.0) gives a 0.0mm hole — reproduced — while the hole COUNT stays right. 'metric'
    defaults true and only the literal words METRIC/INCH switch it; M71/M72 are ignored, so an inch
    file lands every hole at 1/25.4 of true position. Modal single-axis lines are dropped.

11. [R] lob edit PANICS on a lob.toml the manifest reader accepts. edit.rs:113 and :131,
    .as_table_mut().expect("repo is a table") — Item::as_table_mut matches only Item::Table, and an
    INLINE table is Item::Value(Value::InlineTable). Both reproduced. Manifest::from_toml accepts
    both files. find_circuit_mut handles the analogous case gracefully with '?'.

12. [R] IMPORTED CPL ROWS DROPPED AND COORDINATES TRUNCATED WITH NOTHING RECORDED. import.rs:183-204.
    Reproduced on a 3-row CPL: 2 rows survive (blank-X row vanishes) and U3 with '1,234.5' parses as
    x = 1.0. ImportedBoard::skipped exists for exactly this — its doc says 'kept so the caller can
    report an incomplete import rather than a silent one' — and the row parsers never touch it.

13. [R] A SECOND CSV IN A FAB PACKAGE SILENTLY REPLACES THE FIRST. import.rs:241-245 assigns inside a
    loop. Reproduced: board-bottom-pos.csv (C9,C10) + board-top-pos.csv (R1) -> result ['R1'],
    skipped: []. The entire bottom side of the board vanishes with no report.

14. THE DASHBOARD REPORTS 'broken: 0' ON A BOARD WITH A PART OFF THE EDGE. web/src/render.rs:107-115.
    build_facts(...).ok() -> facts: None -> derive_in generates NEITHER the edge-clearance rule NOR
    the overlap rule, and separation rules fall back to a (0,0) origin offset. Trigger: lob serve on
    ANY Linux host, since kicad_footprint_dir() knows only KICAD9_FOOTPRINT_DIR and /Applications.
    The CLI refuses in the same situation; the web surface degrades silently.

ALSO CONFIRMED, one bead each: fab.rs:130/209/595 read kicad-cli output back from fixed temp paths
never cleared first (export_cpl worst — a stale CPL becomes the shipped pick-and-place), the exact
bug drc.rs:141-145 documents. fab.rs:626-628 drops CPL rows with <7 fields silently. layout.rs:320-327
an unrunnable DRC removes the 100x error penalty so an unchecked attempt can win. package.rs:223 DIP
body fencepost (DIP-16 -> 20.92mm vs JEDEC 18.7-19.7) on a life-size sheet. easyeda.rs:107 takes the
qty-5000 break and ranks it against Mouser qty-1 as 'cheaper'. bom.rs:193 to_csv writes unquoted
fields while fab.rs:695 has a correct helper. eagle.rs:290-317 drops nets with <=1 real pin.
sexpr.rs:203 recurses without a depth bound.

CHECKED AND CLEARED, do not re-audit: board.rs:2279, board.rs:1150, layout.rs:402, panel.rs:1442,
main.rs:614-618, panel.rs:854, board.rs:959, layout.rs:170, placement.rs:165, rules.rs:655,
eagle.rs attribute scanner, layout.rs:283. No remaining ==/!= on any coordinate; all rotation
quantisation uses the safe (deg/90.0).round() form; float->int casts saturate.
close_reason: Split holding-pen robustness audit into 22 concrete child beads (numbered findings plus extra confirmed findings).

title: All 8 PathfinderRouter tests pass if PathfinderRouter is aliased to GridRouter; 7 pass with the obstacle-blind MstRouter
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 by stubbing and running, not by reading.

  impl Router for PathfinderRouter { fn route(&self,n,o){ GridRouter.route(n,o) } }
    -> all 8 tests pass (route.rs:1712-1968)
  stub with MstRouter (which never emits conflicts at all)
    -> 7 of 8 pass; only pathfinder_routes_around_an_obstructing_pad catches it

So the negotiated-congestion router — the whole PathFinder implementation, McMurchie &
Ebeling — has no test that distinguishes it from the greedy router it replaced.

WHY: GridRouter returns 0 conflicts on BOTH fixtures, so every assertion of the form
conflicts.is_empty() or pf.conflicts.len() <= grid.conflicts.len() reduces to 0 <= 0.

BOTH FIXTURES ARE BROKEN, independently:

corridor_board (route.rs:1758) HAS NO CORRIDOR. The wall is built with pad(), which
defaults to PadLayer::Front, so the back is an open field. Measured routes: both nets go
(100,98)->F.Cu, ->B.Cu, ->F.Cu with 2 vias, never touching the y=100 gap. There is no
contention to negotiate. Second defect in the same fixture: the wall is one RouteNet with
12 pads, so pads.len() >= 2 makes it a ROUTABLE NET, not an obstacle — PathfinderRouter
dutifully wires the wall together with 11 tracks. Compare
no_net_pad_forces_traces_to_route_around_it (route.rs:1603), which correctly models
obstacles as one single-pad net each. The auditor tried the obvious repair (PadLayer::Both,
one obstacle pad per net) and it jumps straight to grid=2, pf=2, impossible=2 — no regime in
between. This fixture needs redesigning, not patching.

channel_board (route.rs:1808) states its own invariant in its doc comment: 'if GridRouter
ever passes it, the board has stopped being a discriminating case and the test is
worthless.' MEASURED: GridRouter clears it with 0 conflicts. The condition the author wrote
down as fatal is true today and no assertion notices.

ALSO: pathfinder_reports_rather_than_emitting_shorted_copper (route.rs:1899) asserts
routed.contains(idx) || complained.contains(idx) — an OR that holds however the router
behaves. Its stated premise ('one round is not enough to negotiate anything') is false:
max_iters:1 on the corridor gives 0 conflicts and routes both nets.

FIX: build a fixture where GridRouter is ASSERTED to leave >=1 conflict and Pathfinder 0 —
write assert!(!grid.conflicts.is_empty(), "fixture no longer discriminates") down, so the
suite fails the day it stops being a real test. Also pick a board where
unroutable_by_placement() > 0 so 'got <= impossible' is a non-trivial bound.

HISTORY: this bead's subject was already caught vacuous once this cycle. The response then
was to WEAKEN the assertion so it passed. That is why [[legion-of-bom-69v]] exists.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
FIXED 2026-08-12. There is now a board the ordering search cannot solve, and the suite fails if it ever stops being one.

FINDING A DISCRIMINATING FIXTURE TOOK MEASUREMENT, and the two obvious ideas were both dead
ends — recorded here because the next person will try them:

  • A single narrow gap does not work AT ANY WIDTH. Swept 0.6..2.9mm with a both-layer wall
    (new examples/channel_sweep.rs): both routers clear every width. The cost model is
    Manhattan, so a great many routes tie and nothing pushes two nets onto the same cell.
    There is no contention to negotiate.
  • Narrowing until contention exists goes straight from 'both route' to 'impossible for
    both'. The auditor found the same cliff independently.
  • First sweep returned all zeros for a different reason worth recording: my wall spanned
    y 90..110 inside bounds of 88..112, so both nets just walked around the end of it. A wall
    that stops short of the edge is a pillar. Same class of error as the fixture being fixed.

WHAT WORKS: diffuse congestion — exactly what the module docs always claimed the advantage
was for. crossbar_board() is 4 nets across an 8mm span, left pad i wired to right pad 3-i, so
every pair must cross, on through-hole pads so there is no empty back layer to escape to.
Measured, deterministic across runs: GridRouter 2 conflicts, PathfinderRouter 0, 0 impossible
by placement. The sweep found 19 discriminating configurations; this is the smallest.

REMEMBER GridRouter IS NOT NAIVE. It does rip-up-and-reroute over net orderings. That is why
every 2-net fixture failed to discriminate — reordering solves them. This bead's premise held.

THE NEW TEST kills the exact mutant the audit used: with PathfinderRouter aliased to
GridRouter, pathfinder_routes_a_board_the_ordering_search_cannot FAILS and the other eight
still pass — reproducing the audit's result and confirming it is the only one that
discriminates. It asserts its own preconditions:
  • unroutable_by_placement must be empty, or 'pathfinder routed it' is luck
  • GridRouter must actually FAIL, with a message telling the reader to make the board harder
    rather than delete the assertion
channel_board carried that second requirement IN PROSE — 'if GridRouter ever passes it, the
test is worthless' — and GridRouter passed it for months. Prose is not an assertion; that is
the lesson.

THE OTHER SEVEN, all fixed rather than left:
  • pathfinder_is_never_worse_than_the_grid_router — added the crossbar (the only board where
    'worse' is expressible) plus a guard that fails if every board is trivially routable, so
    it can never silently return to comparing 0 <= 0.
  • pathfinder_routes_everything_the_placement_allows — same, the bound is now non-trivial.
  • pathfinder_reports_rather_than_emitting_shorted_copper — moved to the crossbar, because
    its stated premise ('one round is not enough to negotiate anything') was measurably FALSE
    on the corridor. Added an assert that something IS left unrouted, and turned the OR into
    OR-plus-NOT-BOTH: a net reported as unroutable must not also have copper emitted, which is
    the knowingly-shorted case the test is named for.
  • pathfinder_clears_a_contested_corridor -> pathfinder_routes_both_signals_through_one_gap.
    Nothing about it was contested. Honest name, kept as a correctness test.
  • corridor_board's wall was ONE RouteNet with 12 pads, so pads.len() >= 2 made it a net to be
    ROUTED — the routers wired the wall together, 11 tracks down x=106. Now one single-pad net
    per pad, like no_net_pad_forces_traces_to_route_around_it always had it.
  • corridor_board and channel_board doc comments rewritten to say what they measurably are.

examples/channel_sweep.rs is kept: it is how the fixture was found and how to find a harder
one when this stops discriminating.

Gates: 424 core + 21 web + 4 cli, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean.

title: [epic] Tests that cannot fail — the suite is green for the wrong reasons
description:
A dedicated audit (2026-08-12) checked the suite against the standard 'would this test still pass if the function under test were stubbed out?' and verified its answers EMPIRICALLY, by linking legion-of-bom-core from a scratch binary and running the fixtures. The numbers in the children are measured, not argued.

Headline: 446 tests pass, and a meaningful number of them would pass against a no-op. The most important router tests in the repo pass with the router deleted.

This matters more here than in most codebases because the pipeline emits manufacturing data. A green suite is currently weak evidence, and we have been treating it as strong evidence — including me, closing beads on it.

Children cover: the PathfinderRouter suite, the skip-on-missing-tool escape hatches, modules with zero executed coverage, and the individual no-op-passing tests.

Precedent this is not new: 'pathfinder_clears_a_contested_corridor' was ALREADY caught being vacuous once this cycle, and the response at the time was to WEAKEN the assertion rather than fix the fixture. The audit shows the fixture is still broken. Fixing a test by making it easier to pass is the specific habit this epic exists to break.

title: Router models a rotated pad's copper untransposed — a 90-degree SOIC pad is routed as if it were 1.95mm wide, not 0.6
description:
VERIFIED 2026-08-12 by reading all three call sites. Three code paths answer 'how wide is this pad once the footprint is turned' and they give three different answers.

  board.rs:1815-1826  pad_bb and PadPoint: place_point() rotates the pad CENTRE, then
                      w_mm: pad.w, h_mm: pad.h are passed through UNROTATED.
  board.rs:2537       turn_pad_with_footprint: writes the rotation into the pad's
                      absolute 'at' angle, so KiCad draws it turned (effectively swapped).
  guide.rs:826-833    parse_board: explicitly swaps pw/ph on an odd quarter turn, with a
                      comment saying 'A 90 degree turn also swaps the pad's own width/height'.

So the emitted board is right, the guide is right, and the ROUTER's obstacle model is wrong.
A SOIC pad is 1.95 x 0.6mm; at 90 degrees the router sees 1.95 wide x 0.6 tall where the
copper is actually 0.6 x 1.95. The auto-outline's pad bounding box (board.rs:1816-1819,
feeding 1889-1891) has the same defect.

WHY IT BITES NOW: SeededPlacer emits 90-degree poses for SMD (board.rs:997) and for every
pot (control_rotation, board.rs:288), both landed in the recent placement work. Before
that, rotation was rare enough to hide this. It is the same family as the absolute-pad-angle
bug fixed in [[legion-of-bom-j54.25]] — that fix corrected EMISSION only, and this is the
half that was left.

FIX: one shared placed_pad_box(placement, pad) -> (w, h) that swaps on quarter_turns % 2,
called by board.rs (both sites), route.rs and guide.rs. Do not re-derive it a fourth time —
rules.rs:178-181 already documents that there must be exactly one such transform.

Found by the DRY/divergence audit; this was its #1 finding and I confirmed it by reading
the three sites rather than taking the report.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
FIXED 2026-08-12, TDD — failing test first, then the fix, then a mutation check.

THE TEST: board.rs a_rotated_footprint_turns_its_pads_copper_too. A synthetic footprint
(two 2.0 x 0.5mm pads) written to a temp .pretty dir, placed once at 0 deg and once at 90 by a
fixed test Placer, with a probe Router capturing the PadPoints the router is actually handed.
Asserts the extents SWAP between the two poses. Deliberately:
  • no KiCad dependency — the fixture is a file the test writes, so this does not join the
    14 tests that silently return when KiCad is absent ([[legion-of-bom-69v]])
  • asserted as a swap between two poses, not against hard-coded numbers, so it cannot drift
  • the non-square precondition is ASSERTED, so a future fixture change cannot make it vacuous
Before the fix it failed with exactly the bead's claim: 'pad 2: 2x0.5 turned 90 deg is 0.5x2 of
copper, router was told 2x0.5'.

THE FIX: new board::place_pad_extent(placement, w, h) — the other half of place_point, which
only ever moved the pad's CENTRE. Used at both board.rs sites (the PadPoint handed to the
router, and pad_bb which feeds the auto-outline). Also added board::quarter_turns as the ONE
spelling of the odd-quarter-turn test; guide.rs now imports it instead of defining its own, and
PartFacts::keepout_at_rot uses it instead of an inline copy. The bead counted four spellings;
there are now fewer, and route.rs needs none because it consumes the corrected PadPoint.

SCOPE, HONESTLY: this corrects the router's MODEL. On the slew limiter it did not change the
outcome — 0 DRC errors and 0 unconnected before and after — only the routing itself, 492 -> 494
tracks, because the router now sees the real pad shapes. So this is not 'it fixed a broken
board'; it is 'the router was measuring the wrong obstacle and now is not', which matters most
for the dense boards where we are currently blaming the router ([[legion-of-bom-kcq]]) and for
anything with rotated fine-pitch parts.

NOT DONE, deliberately: the DRY audit's related items — guide::courtyard_bbox re-deriving what
board::courtyard_extent already does, and the mechanical/standoff check at board.rs:1780 using
the UNROTATED keep-out. Both are real; both are their own change. Gates: 424 core + 21 web +
4 cli, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean.

title: 4 HP is blocked by the PLACER, not by geometry — the board is 45% full and we silently widen to 6
description:
The user asked for 4 HP from the start. tus.11 records the target as "Compact 4-6HP". They were told it could not be done, it became 5 HP, and the tooling now silently builds 6. MEASURED 2026-07-28, that refusal is wrong.

DOES IT ACTUALLY FIT? Part keep-out area against board area, from build_facts:

  4 HP (20.32 x 128.5): front 1164 mm2 = 44.6% of one side, back 361 mm2 = 13.8%
                        total 1525 mm2 = 29.2% of the two-sided area
  6 HP (30.48 x 128.5): 29.7% front, 9.2% back, 19.5% two-sided

A 4 HP board is LESS THAN HALF OCCUPIED on its busiest side. The panel fits too: the widest control is the Alpha pot at 14.0mm envelope, +2 x 1.0mm edge = 16.0mm = 3.15 HP, comfortably inside 4 HP (20.32mm). Six controls stack vertically with room.

WHAT ACTUALLY REFUSES. board::minimum_hp increments the width until SeededPlacer can place all 23 parts, and returns 6. Everything downstream trusts it:
  - declared_panel_staleness rejects any panel narrower than it: "4 HP, but the PCB needs 6 HP"
  - effective_panel then SILENTLY substitutes a 6 HP derived panel and builds that
So an explicit 4 HP panel is accepted, rejected, and replaced without the build failing. That is the chain that turned 4 HP into 5 into 6, and it never once tried and failed honestly — it declined to try.

ALSO CIRCULAR: `lob panel derive --hp 4` derives cutouts FROM THE BUILT BOARD, where controls sit at x=15.2mm because the board is 6 HP. 15.2 + 7 = 22.2mm overflows 4 HP, so it concludes 4 HP cannot fit — using the 6 HP board as evidence that 6 HP is needed. An idealised centred column at 4 HP puts them at x=10.16 and fits.

WANTED: find out what SeededPlacer actually fails on at 4 HP and fix that, rather than widening. 29% occupancy says the answer is packing strategy, not area. Related: [[legion-of-bom-tsy.10]] (4.63mm dead strip on the right at 6 HP) and the byte-identical placements at 6/8/10/12 HP recorded in [[legion-of-bom-qng]] — the packer does not respond to width at all, which is the same symptom from the other end.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
MEASURED AND ROOT-CAUSED, 2026-07-28. The bead is half right: 4 HP was never
honestly tried, and four real placer/emitter defects were hiding behind that.
But with all four fixed, 4 HP with the RANGE switch is still refused — and by
the circuit, not by the packer. Every number below is the real puget-hardware
board (LOB_PARTS_DIR=~/src/puget-hardware/.lob/parts), derived panel.

WHAT ACTUALLY FAILS AT 4 HP. New harness crates/core/examples/place_probe.rs
(+ LOB_PLACE_TRACE=1 inside SeededPlacer) says it exactly: 2 of 23 parts go to
the off-board overflow lane — C5 (14mm film cap, front THT) and U1 (LM13700,
back SOIC, 8.90 x 11.49mm). Placement order: U2 is placed FIRST (highest pull
to the anchors), U1 is placed third and finds nothing.

WHY "44.6% OCCUPIED" IS THE WRONG PICTURE. The front is one vertical column of
6 panel controls, and their THROUGH-HOLE PADS ARE COPPER ON BOTH LAYERS. The
three Thonkiconn jacks' pads sit at x 8.70..11.62 — dead centre of a 20.32mm
board — so from y 67 to y 114 the back is two 5.70mm slivers. A SOIC is 8.90mm
wide. So the back is not a sheet with 17% on it; it is a stack of horizontal
bands between control pad groups. Measured band heights, clear of every pad on
both layers:
  7.2, 6.2, 1.2, 3.5, 1.2, ~0, ~0 mm ... and 11.3mm at the bottom
Exactly ONE band can hold a body 8.9mm or wider. Three parts need it: U1, U2,
and C5 (whose THT pads pierce through to the back).

IT IS NOT THE ORDER. Added a fail-first repack (re-pack with whatever could not
be placed moved to the front). Measured all three orderings — greedy, U1-first,
U2-first: every one leaves exactly 2 parts homeless. Whoever gets the bottom
band, the other two have nowhere.

DECISIVE: DROP THE RANGE SWITCH AND 4 HP BUILDS CLEAN TODAY.
Stripping SW1, C4, C5 from the netlist and re-running:
  with the switch:    board::minimum_hp = 6 HP; a 4 HP trial build is
                      21 KiCad DRC errors (9 unconnected, 8 copper_edge_clearance)
  without the switch: board::minimum_hp = 4 HP; a 4 HP trial build is DRC CLEAN
                      (hp_search, real place -> route -> KiCad DRC)
That is exactly what the memory dual-slew-limiter-is-the-product predicted:
"C5 is 14mm wide and is what pushed the board past 4 HP". It is a product
decision, not mine to take — but it is now measured rather than argued.

FOUR DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED ALONG THE WAY (see the per-bead comments):
1. crates/core/src/board.rs turn_pad_with_footprint — a rotated footprint's
   pads did not carry the rotation. This is [[legion-of-bom-j54.25]]'s open
   root cause and the reason the placer was forbidden from ever turning SMD,
   which is what makes a SOIC unplaceable in a 20mm board.
2. The free-part rotation was a one-shot width heuristic, decided before the
   search and never revisited; a part that fit nowhere in that pose was thrown
   off the board. Both quarter turns are now tried first.
3. The power header was laid out by footprint ORIGIN as if that were its
   keep-out centre. A 2x5 header's origin is pin 1, 5.08mm from its body
   centre, so J3's copper sat 3.58mm OFF THE LEFT EDGE at every width this
   project has ever built.
4. With (3) fixed the header lands exactly on the 1.5mm edge line, and the
   placer and the rule reach that number by different summation orders —
   2.8e-14mm apart. That read as a broken Tier::Physical rule and REFUSED the
   8 HP fab package outright.

BEFORE/AFTER, my five edits toggled in an otherwise identical tree:
  lob fab slew_limiter @6 HP   0 DRC / 19 warn  ->  0 DRC / 15 warn
  lob fab slew_limiter @8 HP   REFUSED ("J3 hangs 0.0mm past the board's
                               1.5mm edge clearance")  ->  0 DRC / 10 warn,
                               fab package written
  lob fab slew_limiter @4 HP   silently widened to 6  ->  unchanged

STILL OPEN, and it is the other half of this bead: effective_panel still
accepts a 4 HP spec, rejects it and substitutes a derived 6 HP panel without
the build failing. It does print a loud warning with the reason, but it does
not stop. Changing that is a product-behaviour call — say the word and it
becomes an error.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
CLOSED OUT 2026-08-12. Both silent-substitution paths are now hard failures, and the 4 HP question has an answer.

THE REFUSAL (crates/cli/src/main.rs, effective_panel). A declared panel that does not
fit the PCB now STOPS the build instead of warning and building against a derived
substitute. Panel and PCB are ordered from different vendors weeks apart, so nothing
downstream ever gets the chance to notice they disagree — this is the only place that
can. New PanelStaleness enum {Missing, TooNarrow} replaces the stringly reason, and
panel_mismatch() builds the error: both HP numbers, why it is fatal, three concrete
fixes, and the promise that the author's file was left untouched. The substitute is
still DERIVED (so '--panel out/<n>/<n>_auto_panel.toml' is a real escape hatch that
exists on disk) — it is just no longer BUILT.

WHAT THIS IMMEDIATELY CAUGHT, which is the point. puget-hardware's declared
slew_limiter panel was wrong in TWO independent ways, and lob had been building past
both:
  • hp = 5 while the PCB needs 6 — the mismatch the user hit as 'why is the panel /
    pcb mismatched?'
  • NO CUTOUT FOR SW1. The RANGE switch was added to the circuit and the panel never
    followed. That panel ordered as-is is a module with no hole for its switch.
Fixed the spec to 6 HP + SW1, keeping the author's deliberate jack order (IN, OUT,
CV IN — the deriver wants CV IN, IN, OUT) and the deriver's spacing. Rebuilt: 492
tracks, 31 vias, clean. Round-trip verified — 'lob panel derive' off the new board
returns J1 IN @ (15.2, 52.3), the exact position now declared.

THE CIRCULARITY, also fixed and WORSE than this bead recorded. 'lob panel derive --hp 4'
reads cutouts off the built board by default (correct — the board is master). But
panel_from_board takes its hp FROM THE BOARD OUTLINE, so the requested width was
discarded entirely, and the code then printed 'widened to 6 HP — 4 HP can't fit the
control hardware'. That verdict was never tested; it was the 6 HP board asserting its
own width. Now: an explicit --hp that differs from the built board sets the board aside
and lays out from scratch, saying so. Measured — 'derive --hp 4' emits a real 4 HP
column at x=10.2 (exactly what this bead predicted), and the default path is unchanged.
Also suppressed the follow-on 'no built board at ...' line, which was a plain untruth
when a board existed and had been deliberately ignored.

DOES 4 HP HAPPEN? No, and not because of the packer. The prior comment measured it:
with SW1/C4/C5 the packer leaves exactly 2 of 23 parts homeless in EVERY ordering
(greedy, U1-first, U2-first) because the front column's through-hole pads are copper on
BOTH layers, leaving the back as bands of 7.2/6.2/1.2/3.5/1.2/~0/~0mm plus 11.3mm at the
bottom — one band fits a body >=8.9mm and three parts need it. Strip SW1/C4/C5 and 4 HP
builds DRC clean. The user has since chosen to keep the switch ('it adds to the
features') and moved the product to the dual, so 4 HP is decided, not blocked.

Tests: a_panel_narrower_than_the_pcb_stops_the_build (pure, no KiCad needed) and
a_panel_wider_than_the_pcb_is_left_alone (42 HP for one jack is the author's business).
CLI tests 1 -> 3. Gates: 422 core + 21 web + 3 cli, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean.

title: Two divergent board artifacts: lob guide and lob fab produce different boards, and the dashboard renders the ungated one
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-28, ~/src/puget-hardware/out/slew_limiter:

  slew_limiter.kicad_pcb        written by lob GUIDE   6.0 HP   2 footprints with copper OUTSIDE the outline (U1 +6.5mm, C2 +0.5mm)
  fab/slew_limiter.kicad_pcb    written by lob FAB     6.0 HP   0

Same circuit, same panel, two different placements. lob fab runs the Tier::Physical gate and refuses an illegal board. lob guide runs no gate at all and writes its board straight to out/<name>/<name>.kicad_pcb (cli/src/main.rs, guide_cmd).

AND THAT IS THE ONE EVERYONE LOOKS AT. web/src/render.rs board_path() resolves out/<name>/<name>.kicad_pcb, so the dashboard's PCB view, the layout view and the gerber view all render the guide's ungated board. It is also the obvious file to open by hand. The user spotted an IC hanging off the side from the dashboard; the shipping board does not have that IC hanging off.

This is worse than a bad board: it means nobody can trust what they are looking at. It cost most of a session — I twice reached a confident conclusion (once 'fab-ready', once 'the gate has a hole') from whichever of the two files I happened to open.

WANTED, in order of preference:
  1. ONE board artifact. The guide should render the board the fab package contains rather than generating its own, or both should write to the same gated path.
  2. Failing that, the guide's board must pass the same Tier::Physical gate before it is written, and the dashboard must render the fab board when one exists.
  3. Whatever the answer, the two paths must not be able to disagree silently. If they can, that itself needs a check.

RELATED: [[legion-of-bom-3kf]] (edge violations unrepaired) was filed against the guide board and should be re-read in that light — the fab board has no edge violations, so legalize is either not running or not reached on the guide path.
close_reason:
FIXED. Root cause was not a path collision — the two commands used different LAYOUT PATHS. lob fab runs run_layout_loop (6 iterations, seeded placer, scoring, legalize, best-of). lob guide called generate_board_report once: one-shot placement, no iteration, no scoring. So the guide's board was genuinely a different and worse board, and out/<name>/<name>.kicad_pcb is what web/src/render.rs renders — the picture everyone looks at was the bad one.

Fix: new build_layout() helper in the CLI, used by guide, running the same loop as fab with the same iteration count. Its doc says why it exists so the next command added does not reintroduce the split.

VERIFIED on the real slew limiter: 23 parts, ZERO placements differ between out/slew_limiter/slew_limiter.kicad_pcb and out/slew_limiter/fab/slew_limiter.kicad_pcb. The guide board went from 3 physical violations (U1 hanging 9.0mm off the edge, C5/U2 colliding through the board, C2 3.0mm off) to none — its only remaining violation is the same -0.5mm decoupling one the fab board has.

This is also what made most of a session's measurements ambiguous: I twice reached a confident and opposite conclusion depending on which of the two files I happened to open.

title: lob fab gates on KiCad DRC but NOT on our own Physical rules — it shipped a package with an IC hanging off the board
description:
THE GATE HAS A HOLE, and it is the reason [[legion-of-bom-qng]] was wrongly closed.

lob fab refuses a board on KiCad DRC errors. It does not consult rules::evaluate at all. So a board can carry Tier::Physical violations that our own tooling derives, evaluates and prints, and still have a fab package written for it. Measured on the slew limiter 2026-07-28:

  DRC:                  0 errors  -> gate passes, package written
  rules_report:  -9.0mm U1 hangs past the board's 1.5mm edge clearance
                 -3.0mm C2 hangs past the board's 1.5mm edge clearance

KiCad cannot catch this — it has no "footprint outside the board outline" rule, which this repo measured and recorded on 2026-07-26 ([[kicad-drc-cannot-see-a-part-off-the-board]]). Our EdgeClearance rule exists precisely BECAUSE KiCad has that blind spot. Then the gate does not read it.

WANTED: lob fab refuses on any Tier::Physical violation with a negative margin, the same way it refuses on DRC, and prints them in the same block. Physical is defined in rules.rs as the tier where "a part hanging over the board edge is not a board" — a violation there is not a trade-off and must not be shippable.

WHILE THERE: the DRC gate and the rules gate should report together, so "0 DRC errors" can never again be read as "this board can be built".

SEE ALSO: legalize is the pass whose entire job is repairing Tier::Physical violations, and it did not repair these. Separate bug, filed alongside.
close_reason:
MISDIAGNOSED — retracted. The physical-rule gate in lob fab EXISTS and WORKS; its own comment already describes the KiCad blind spot I thought I had found ('KiCad has no footprint outside the board outline rule... it just was not consulted here. It is now.').

I filed this after running rules_report on out/slew_limiter/slew_limiter.kicad_pcb, which is written by lob GUIDE, not by lob fab. The board lob fab actually produces (out/slew_limiter/fab/slew_limiter.kicad_pcb) has ZERO footprints with copper outside the outline and 1 of 40 rules broken, and that one is Electrical (C3 9.0mm from U2, max 8.6) not Physical. The gate did its job.

The real bug is that those are two different boards and the tooling shows the broken one — filed separately.

title: Rule::Overlap — part bodies and through-hole pads, as a Physical rule the score and legalize can see
description:
THE HIGHEST-VALUE ONE, and it comes straight out of [[legion-of-bom-ude]].

Overlap is currently checked ONLY inside board::placement_clear, which is the packer's private admission test. Consequences, all observed:

  - legalize cannot repair an overlap, because legalize repairs Tier::Physical RULES and there is no overlap rule.
  - layout::score cannot price one, so the loop happily picks an attempt with a part sitting on a jack pin.
  - The dashboard rules panel and lob fab both reported "all design rules met" on a board with a 0603 soldered to the back annulus of a jack pin.
  - Anything that MOVES a part after packing (decouple::snap, summing::snap) bypasses the check entirely, which is exactly how the bug happened.

WANTED: a Rule::Overlap variant deriving from PartFacts, with the semantics placement_clear already implements and should then delegate to:

  - bodies clash only on the SAME side, and only when neither passes under the other (fits_under, for stacked sub-boards)
  - THROUGH-HOLE PADS ARE COPPER ON BOTH LAYERS and clash with anything on either side. This is the case that was missing and that cost six connections.
  - the repair vector is "move the smaller/free part out along the shortest axis of overlap", which is what legalize wants

Tier::Physical: a part on another part's pad is not a trade-off.

TEST DISCIPLINE (learned the hard way twice in ude): derive fixture geometry from the code under test, do not hand-author it. A hand-placed fixture passed VACUOUSLY because the part landed somewhere other than where I guessed. Snap once with nothing in the way to learn where a part goes, then place the obstacle exactly there.

DONE WHEN: the slew limiter's historical failure reproduces as a reported rule violation on a board built from the pre-fix placer, and legalize repairs it.
close_reason: Rule::Overlap landed with the both-sides through-hole semantics, pruned derivation, a repair vector, and three tests. Validated on the real board: catches C5/U2 colliding through the board (the defect the user spotted by eye) on the guide board, and correctly reports the fab board clean. Legalize integration and the fab-gate wiring follow from the rule existing.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
EVIDENCE, verified 2026-07-28 with exact geometry — real through-hole PAD rects against keep-out boxes, not the crude circular approximation I used first (that one produced six false positives and a wrong P0).

Method: same-side parts clash body-vs-body; a through-hole pin clashes with ANY part's body on either side, because it is copper through both layers.

  out/slew_limiter/slew_limiter.kicad_pcb  (lob guide, ungated)
     same-side body overlaps : 2   C1/J3, RV2/SW1
     THT pin through a body  : 3   J3 pin into C1, C5 pin into U2, SW1 pin into RV2

  out/slew_limiter/fab/slew_limiter.kicad_pcb  (lob fab, SHIPS)
     same-side body overlaps : 1   RV2/SW1
     THT pin through a body  : 2   RV2 pin into R8, SW1 pin into RV2

THE SHIPPING BOARD HAS THREE OVERLAPS AND EVERY GATE PASSES IT: 0 KiCad DRC errors, 0 Physical rule violations, package written. Because there is no overlap rule, none of them is visible to score, to legalize, to lob fab, or to the dashboard panel.

C5's pin through U2 is the case the user spotted by eye — a 13mm THT film cap whose pins pass through a back-side SOIC-14. RV2/SW1 is the anchored panel pair from [[legion-of-bom-tsy.2]] and appears on BOTH boards, so it survives every path.

This makes the priority concrete: the rule is not a tidiness improvement, it is the difference between a board that assembles and one that does not.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
CORRECTION to my evidence comment above, and then the fix.

MY OVERLAP NUMBERS WERE WRONG — a third geometry error, same family as the first two. My Python used the mathematical CCW rotation sense; the codebase's rotate_local NEGATES the angle, because KiCad's Y axis points down. rules.rs already warns about exactly this ('duplicating that transform is how the codebase ended up with two rotation senses disagreeing with each other for months') and I duplicated it anyway. Retracted:
  - 'fab board has 19 keep-out overlaps'   — wrong, and the first pass of it was also wrong for a different reason (circular approximations)
  - 'RV2/SW1 overlap by 7.23 x 5.51mm'     — they do not. The rule computes RV2 clears SW1 by 5.2mm, and KiCad agrees: zero courtyards_overlap on that board.
  - 'RV2 pin into R8', 'SW1 pin into RV2'  — same bad transform.
The lesson is the one already written in this module: do not re-derive the transform, call it.

RULE LANDED AND VALIDATED. Rule::Overlap added with the semantics the bead asked for — bodies clash same-side only; a through-hole pad is copper on BOTH layers and clashes with any body either side. Derived pairwise from PartFacts, pruning pairs that can never touch (opposite sides, no through-hole pads), which on a mixed kit is most of them: 40 rules -> 293 on the slew limiter.

It catches the real defect, the one the user spotted by eye:
  out/slew_limiter/slew_limiter.kicad_pcb  (lob guide, ungated)
    [physical] -9.0mm  U1 hangs 9.0mm past the board's 1.5mm edge clearance
    [physical] -3.3mm  C5 and U2 collide through the board — a through-hole pad is copper on both layers
    [physical] -3.0mm  C2 hangs 3.0mm past the board's 1.5mm edge clearance
  out/slew_limiter/fab/slew_limiter.kicad_pcb  (ships)
    no physical violations; 1 electrical (C3 9.0mm from U2, max 8.6)

Three tests, each pinning a distinct half of the semantics: a pin through a body on the OTHER side violates; two opposite-side SURFACE parts sharing board area do NOT (getting that wrong would make every mixed kit unbuildable); same-side bodies overlapping violate and carry a repair vector for legalize.

405 core tests green, clippy clean.

title: Placer's collision check is side-aware, but THROUGH-HOLE pads are on both sides — a back-side 0603 lands on a front jack's pad and kills the -12V net
description:
CORRECTED 2026-07-28, twice. Both earlier readings on this bead were wrong and are retracted:

  WRONG #1: 'keep-out too small, PartFacts::extent should use CutoutSpec::envelope_mm'. MEASURED: J1's extent is 10.00 x 15.38mm with origin_offset (0, 5.775). That is correct — a Thonkiconn's pads really do span 11.4mm (pad S at local y=0, TN at 3.10, T at 11.40, ~2.13mm each), so the true footprint span is ~13.5mm and the keep-out is that plus a small margin. The data was right all along.
  WRONG #2: 'six internals overlap panel hardware'. That came from MY analysis using circular approximations with invented radii against keep-outs that are rectangular and strongly anisotropic. Redone as a proper axis-aligned test with the real extents, origin offsets and rotations, there is exactly ONE body overlap on the board — and it is RV2/SW1, two PANEL parts (see below).

THE ACTUAL DEFECT. The placer's collision test is side-aware — parts on opposite faces are treated as unable to collide. That is right for bodies and WRONG for through-hole pads, which occupy BOTH copper layers. Measured on the real board:

  C3  footprint layer B.Cu   (0603, back)
  J1  footprint layer F.Cu   (Thonkiconn, front)
  J1 pad S  thru_hole, centre (148.500, 127.575) 1.93 x 1.83  -> x 147.54..149.47  y 126.66..128.49
  C3 pad 2  smd back,  centre (149.250, 126.480) 0.90 x 0.95  -> x 148.80..149.70  y 126.00..126.95
  copper overlap ON THE BACK LAYER: 0.67 x 0.29 mm

So a back-side 0603 is soldered onto the back annulus of a front-side jack pin. C3.1 is pad 0 of the -12V net; walled in like that, the routing tree cannot leave it and EVERY other -12V pad is unreachable by any router — J3.1, J3.2, R4.2, R8.2, U1.6, U2.11. Six of the seven impossible connections, from one missing side-check. It is also exactly what KiCad's pth_inside_courtyard errors have been saying all along.

SECOND, SEPARATE BUG (same board): RV2 and SW1 overlap by 7.23 x 5.51mm. Both are anchored panel hardware, so this comes from the auto-DERIVED panel spacing its cutouts too close — the placer cannot fix it (both pinned) and legalize cannot either. Related to the panel-hardware separation rule in [[legion-of-bom-cll.5]].

FIX: the collision predicate must treat a part with through-hole pads as present on both sides. crate::board::PartFacts already carries tht_pads, so the data is there.

NOT THE CAUSE, ruled out by experiment: board width (identical results at 6/8/10/12 HP), routing grid (identical at 0.2/0.1/0.05mm), the router (at its ceiling — it routes everything the placement permits), and decouple::snap (a guard was added and the board did not change).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
FIXED (partly) and MEASURED 2026-07-28.

crate::decouple::snap now refuses to move a cap onto occupied space, using the same rules as board::placement_clear: bodies clash only on the same side, but THROUGH-HOLE PADS ARE COPPER ON BOTH LAYERS, so a back-side part must still avoid a front-side part's pins. PartFacts::keepout_at_rot / tht_pads_at were made pub(crate) so the guard uses the placer's own geometry rather than a second implementation of it.

REAL BOARD, before -> after:
  impossible by placement:  7 -> 1     (only RATE_CV -> RV1.2 left)
  pathfinder unrouted:      7 -> 4
  pathfinder DRC:          13 -> 7
  gridrouter unrouted:     10 -> 7
  gridrouter DRC:          16 -> 10
  lob fab gate:        12 DRC / 5 unrouted  ->  7 DRC / 4 unrouted

The whole -12V net is recovered — six connections that no router could make are now routable. Copper went UP (768 -> 966mm) as expected: the cap is no longer parked on the jack's pad, so those nets now have to be routed for real.

TDD NOTE, worth recording. My FIRST attempt at this guard reproduced the very bug it was meant to fix — it skipped different-side pairs, so it could not see the cross-side THT case, and the board did not change at all. The test that would have caught it passed VACUOUSLY: I hand-placed the jack's pad where I guessed the cap would land, it landed elsewhere, and the assertion never fired. Rebuilding the fixture empirically — snap once with nothing in the way to learn where the cap actually goes, then put the pad exactly there — made it fail immediately and for the right reason. Hand-authored geometry in a placement test is not trustworthy; derive it.

STILL OPEN:
1. RATE_CV -> RV1.2 is still impossible by placement (1 connection).
2. PathFinder leaves 4 unrouted where only 1 is impossible, so 3 are now the ROUTER's gap on this board — route::pathfinder_routes_everything_the_placement_allows asserts exactly this property but only on synthetic boards, and the real board violates it.
3. RV2/SW1 still overlap by 7.23 x 5.51mm — both anchored, so this is the auto-derived PANEL spacing its cutouts too close. Neither the placer nor legalize can fix it.
4. summing::snap has the same missing occupancy check and is untested (it no-ops without a KiCad symbol library).

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
VERIFIED FIXED 2026-08-12 on the real board. Both defects on this bead are gone.

MEASURED: lob drc on the rebuilt puget-hardware slew_limiter (6 HP, RANGE switch
present, declared panel now honoured) reports 0 error(s), 0 unconnected, 12 warnings
(8 silkscreen, 3 lib_footprint_mismatch, 1 missing House library config).

DEFECT 1 (cross-side THT): the placer's collision test treated opposite faces as unable
to collide, which is right for bodies and wrong for through-hole pads that occupy BOTH
copper layers. Fixed by moving the check into board::first_overlap and having it test THT
pads across sides, plus Rule::Overlap in rules.rs carrying a_tht/b_tht/a_back/b_back so
the pruning keeps exactly the pairs that can really clash. The bead's own stated symptom
was 'exactly what KiCad's pth_inside_courtyard errors have been saying all along' — there
are now ZERO pth_inside_courtyard errors on that board, and zero unconnected, where the
walled-in C3.1 used to make every other -12V pad unreachable (J3.1, J3.2, R4.2, R8.2,
U1.6, U2.11 — six of seven impossible connections).

DEFECT 2 (RV2/SW1 overlapping by 7.23 x 5.51mm from derived panel spacing): also gone,
and I checked the arithmetic rather than trusting the clean DRC. The deriver now spaces
them 17.0mm centre-to-centre against a requirement of 15.0mm (POT envelope 14.0 -> 7.0
half, SWITCH 12.0 -> 6.0 half, plus GAP_MM 2.0). Courtyard overlap is a KiCad DRC ERROR,
and there are none. The rest of that column is spaced to the same rule with no slack:
SW1->J1 15.2mm against 15.2 required, J1->J2 and J2->J4 16.4 against 16.4.

Closed alongside [[legion-of-bom-unc]] and [[legion-of-bom-tyw]], which stopped the panel
and the PCB from disagreeing in the first place — the 6 HP board used to be built against
a declared 5 HP panel that also had no cutout for SW1.

title: [bug] lob fab gated on KiCad DRC alone, which cannot see a part off the board
description:
CROSS-CHECKED AGAINST KICAD, prompted by the user asking whether our rules/DRC
instrumentation actually reflects reality. Two results, one reassuring and one
not.

REASSURING — our DRC reader is EXACT. Same board file, same flags, raw
kicad-cli vs our DrcReport:

    raw kicad-cli --severity-all --refill-zones : 30 errors
    our `lob drc`                                : 30 errors
    per-kind: 15 unconnected_items, 10 copper_edge_clearance,
              2 shorting_items, 2 solder_mask_bridge, 1 pth_inside_courtyard
    identical on every kind.

  Note --refill-zones matters enormously and we do pass it: without it the same
  board reports 24 unconnected instead of 15, because the GND pour is what
  connects them. Measuring an unfilled board would overstate unrouted nets by
  60%. (An earlier 39-vs-30 "discrepancy" in this investigation was purely my
  own missing flag, not a bug.)

  Also confirmed [[legion-of-bom-8yr]]'s fix is live in the running code: the
  report is deleted before kicad-cli is invoked and the temp path is stamped per
  board.

NOT REASSURING — KiCad DRC HAS NO OUTSIDE-THE-OUTLINE RULE. Measured directly:
took a DRC-clean board, moved U1 15.8mm clear of the board edge, re-ran DRC:

    geometric violations: 0
    total errors: 8, ALL unconnected_items — i.e. only the nets it dragged off
                     with it, nothing about the part being in space

A part with no connections (mounting hole, unpopulated position, fiducial) drags
no nets and would produce a completely clean report while sitting off the board.
Our own crate::rules Tier::Physical catches it exactly -- "U1 hangs 23.0mm past
the board's 1.5mm edge clearance" -- which is the check the placer's overflow
lane is measured against.

THE HOLE: `lob fab` gated on `report.is_clean()` and nothing else. It never
consulted the rules. So the one check that can see an off-board part was not
wired to the decision about whether to ship one. Gerbers plotted, CPL written,
part placed at a coordinate that is not on the board.

FIXED: fab_cmd now evaluates Tier::Physical rules against the generated board
and refuses before it ever reaches DRC, naming each violation.

ON kicad-ipc-rs: switching to the IPC API would not have helped. kicad-cli runs
the same DRC engine as the GUI; the gap is not the interface, it is that the
rule does not exist in KiCad. Anything that asks KiCad "is this board legal"
gets the same answer.
close_reason: fixed: fab_cmd now refuses on Tier::Physical rule violations before the DRC gate

title: DECISION: analytical placement now loses to the greedy placer it replaced
description:
DECIDED BY EVIDENCE, AND REVERTED. The analytical placer from
[[legion-of-bom-d8t]] is out; SeededPlacer is the greedy centroid placer again.

WHAT SETTLED IT: the real 5 HP puget-hardware slew limiter, the actual product
board, not a demo in this repo.

  config                                  rule penalty     KiCad DRC
  HEAD (before any of this session)          0 (clean)       6 errors
  greedy + this session's loop/determinism   0 (clean)       6 errors
  ANALYTICAL placer                          1,000,000       9 errors
                                             (J3 past the board's edge clearance)

The user was looking at their own board in the web UI with an IC sitting ~6.5mm
off the left edge. That board (out/slew_limiter/slew_limiter.kicad_pcb, built
20:26) came out of the working tree with the analytical placer in it. U1 pads
x 126.8..133.7 against an outline starting at x 133.3; C2 also 0.5mm past the
bottom edge.

The benchmark suite had already said greedy wins 5 of 12 and ties 3 once the
loop was fixed. The product board turned that from "not obviously better" into
"actively breaks a physical rule". No further argument needed.

KEPT from the same work, all measured harmless-or-better on this board:
  * [[legion-of-bom-gns]] router/board determinism (board.rs nets.sort_by_key,
    route.rs blame ordering)
  * [[legion-of-bom-lso]] loop exits on "no longer improving" rather than on the
    first clean board, plus relax_key ranking unrouted above preference
  * crates/core/examples/place_bench.rs, the A/B harness

PARKED, NOT DELETED: crates/core/src/analytical.rs is still in the tree and
still exported, wired to nothing. It is a working quadratic solver with the
SimPL spreading loop and 12 tests. Delete it or pick it back up deliberately --
but the d8t architecture argument (greedy cannot absorb another constraint --
see [[legion-of-bom-yck]]) is still unanswered, and this module is the only
attempt at answering it that exists.

IF IT IS PICKED BACK UP, the two things that hurt it here are known: it has no
density/force spreading (the pseudo-anchor walk needs something fixed to walk
away from, and this board is dense at 5 HP), and its packing is a nearest-clear-
spot spiral that scatters a collapsed solve. Both are addressable; neither is
addressed.
close_reason: decided: analytical placer reverted after it broke a physical rule on the real 5 HP slew limiter; loop + determinism fixes kept, analytical.rs parked unwired

title: panel: read-only-sounding commands destructively rewrite hand-authored panel TOMLs
description:
From puget-hardware/lob-gaps.md B1, graded CRITICAL (data loss). INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED -- I hit this myself during the panel-art work and had to git checkout the users slew_limiter_panel.toml after running lob panel derive to test.

lob circuits / status / board / build overwrite the panel file a circuit references via panel = "...", with an auto-derived one. It strips comments, changes hp, and in at least one observed run git add-ed the result.

Observed on both:
  slew_limiter_panel.toml  -> rewritten to 5 HP auto
  crossfader_panel.toml    -> hand 12 HP 2-column became 42 HP auto with a jack at y = -12mm, off-board

A command that sounds like a read mutating AND STAGING tracked source is the worst shape this can take. It cost the user real work.

ASK:
  1. Never overwrite a user-supplied panel = ... path. Write auto-derived panels only to *_auto_panel.toml, as already happens when no panel is declared.
  2. Never git add. Staging is the users action.
  3. Consider a guard: if the target is tracked and dirty, refuse.

Note my own observation of the position rewrite is separately explained by [[legion-of-bom-za4]] (cutouts were being mapped from the footprint origin rather than the hardware centre, so a re-derive moved pots 2.5mm off-centre). That is fixed; the overwrite behaviour is not.
close_reason:
Fixed. A declared panel is now never written to.

WAS: effective_panel called refresh_declared_panel_if_stale, which on staleness did std::fs::write(path, regenerated) straight over the users file (main.rs:701). The intent was sound -- a panel missing a cutout cannot mate the board, so faithfully rebuilding a wrong panel is worse than useless -- but it paid for that by destroying hand-authored work.

NOW: declared_panel_staleness is read-only and returns a reason. When stale, write_auto_panel derives a substitute into the work dir and the build uses THAT, saying so:

  auto panel: 4 HP, 5 control(s) -> out/slew_limiter/slew_limiter_auto_panel.toml
  WARNING declared panel slew_limiter_panel.toml is stale (missing RV1, J4)
    left untouched -- building against out/slew_limiter/slew_limiter_auto_panel.toml instead
    fix the declared spec, or drop panel = ... to adopt the derived one

write_auto_panel is now the ONLY place this tool writes a panel spec, and it only ever writes a generated path under the work dir.

VERIFIED against a copy of the users real slew_limiter_panel.toml, made stale by dropping two controls: sha 3c5cad97ccedbc26 and 37 lines before AND after, hand-authored comment intact, hp = 5 preserved (previously rewritten to 4). Board still builds. Test pins the read-only property.

ON THE git add PART OF THE REPORT: I could not find any code path that stages a panel TOML. The only git add in the tree is crates/web/src/api.rs:193, which stages lob.toml (MANIFEST_NAME) from the dashboards /api/edit endpoint -- never a panel file. Worth re-checking what was observed; if a panel really did get staged there is a second bug I have not found.

Note the POSITION changes also seen in that report are separately explained by [[legion-of-bom-za4]] -- cutouts were mapped from the footprint origin rather than the hardware centre, so any re-derive moved pots 2.5mm off-centre. Fixed.

title: Decoupling caps land across the board: layout loop discards the good attempt
description:
User: "coupling caps should sit as physically close to the power pins on IC as possible. Right now they are across the board. That really needs some fixing."

MEASURED on puget slew_limiter (shipped board): C2 -> U1 = 96.0mm, C3 -> U2 = 60.8mm. Should be 2-3mm.

ROOT CAUSE (instrumented, not guessed): decoupling_bonus() correctly derives the pairs (verified: C2->U1, C3->U2, both ICs and caps in the free set) and the DECOUPLE_PULL=12 attractor does dominate the target centroid — a traced attempt placed C3 with target (5.8,126.3) and final (5.8,125.5), i.e. sitting on its IC. The failure is downstream: run_layout_loop performs several attempts, perturbs free parts via nudges to repair unrouted nets, and selects the winner with score() = HPWL + vias + unrouted. score() has no decoupling term, so an attempt that wrecks cap-to-IC proximity but shaves wirelength beats the good one, and that is what ships.

ALSO TRIED AND REVERTED (do not repeat): deferring each decoupling cap in the greedy loop until its IC is placed. Ordering came out exactly right (U2 -> C3 immediately, U1 -> C2 immediately) but final positions were byte-identical, because the winning attempt is chosen after the fact by a score that ignores the rule. More conditionals in the placer cannot fix a scoring problem.

FIX: give the rule a voice in score() — i.e. implement it as a tiered, data-driven constraint per [[legion-of-bom-avg]], with cap-to-IC proximity violation carrying a cost far above wirelength so the loop cannot trade it away. Verify by asserting C2->U1 and C3->U2 are within a few mm on the built slew_limiter board.
notes:
RESOLVED THE REAL CAUSE (commit f8bd319). The rule was unsatisfiable, which is why every repair strategy looked like it failed.

A flat 5mm CENTRE-TO-CENTRE limit is the wrong shape for 'put the cap against the chip': how close two centres can get depends on how big the parts are. Measured on slew_limiter, a 0603 cannot get within 6.7mm of a SOIC-16's centre — at 5mm it would be inside the chip. So the rule fired on every attempt, the loop burned its whole 6-iteration budget chasing a target that did not exist, and both the blind shake and the rule-directed aim were being judged against an impossible goal.

rules::derive_with_sizes now sets the limit to the two keep-outs touching plus DECOUPLE_GAP_MM (2mm), from PartFacts.extent, min across axes (closest approach is beside a chip's long edge, not off its end).

MEASURED, anchored configuration (the harness now anchors panel controls as the CLI does — it previously passed none, which is why earlier numbers in this bead are not comparable):
  C3 -> U2  6.6mm, limit 6.7mm  -> COMPLIANT
  C2 -> U1  9.3mm, limit 8.7mm  -> over by 0.6mm
  score 6456 -> 1176, rule penalty 5911 -> 632

REMAINING: 0.6mm on one pair. examples/decouple_check now prints the physical floor and slack per pair, so 'the placer owes 2.6mm' is distinguishable from 'this is as close as a capacitor gets'. Closing that last 0.6mm is a placer question (space reservation beside the IC before other parts claim it) and is small enough that it may not be worth the machinery — judge on a real board.
close_reason:
Resolved in substance. Opened at C2->U1 = 89mm on the shipped board; now 0.6mm over a limit that is reachable, and the loop can no longer trade it away.

What actually fixed it, in order: (1) rules as data with a tiered penalty in score(), so the loop stopped discarding the good attempt to win on wirelength; (2) the loop's exit condition waiting for rule-clean as well as routable; (3) — the real one — derive_with_sizes, because the original 5mm centre-to-centre limit was PHYSICALLY UNSATISFIABLE for a 0603 against a SOIC-16 (floor 6.7mm), so every repair strategy was being judged against a target that did not exist.

Two approaches tried and reverted, documented in the notes so they are not retried: accumulating rule-directed target nudges (diverged, 8.8 -> 14.1mm), and the same damped with backtracking (11.1mm, still worse than none). Both failed because the constraint is SPACE beside the IC, not aim — and because of the unsatisfiable limit above.

Residual 0.6mm on one pair is tracked with the proxy question in legion-of-bom-5kv: distance is a stand-in for loop inductance, and tightening millimetres is not obviously the right lever.

title: Layout: declarative design-rule system (rules as data + scored relaxation), not conditionals in the placer
description:
ARCHITECTURE (user directive): "Should we focus on making rules more data driven rather than a ton of conditionals in our code? I felt like the monad approach was best here. Focus on things that matter most. Ground pour, coupling caps, physical constraints etc. Then break them slightly to fit. Not just throw it all in an algorithm which is now just spaghetti code."

PROBLEM (measured, puget slew_limiter): the decoupling rule (w95) is implemented as a weight bonus inside SeededPlacer greedy loop. Instrumented run PROVES the rule itself works — attempt 1 placed C3 at target (5.8,126.3) landing (5.8,125.5), i.e. right on its IC. But run_layout_loop then runs more attempts, nudges free parts to repair unrouted nets, and keeps the best by score(), which is HPWL/via based and knows NOTHING about decoupling. So a layout with nicer wirelength but ruined decoupling wins, and the shipped board has C2 96mm from U1 and C3 55mm from U2. Bolting more conditionals into the greedy selection does not fix this (tried: deferring caps until their IC is placed — correct ordering achieved, positions unchanged, because the loop discards the good attempt).

DESIGN DIRECTION:
1. Rules become DATA, not code paths. A rule is a declarative record — e.g. Proximity { a: cap, b: ic, max_mm, tier }, SameSide { .. }, EdgeClearance { mm }, PourClearance { mm }, KeepOut { .. }, Anchored { refdes, xy } — derived from the circuit (decoupling_bonus already derives the pairs; keep that as a RULE DERIVER, drop the weight hack).
2. Rules are TIERED by how much they matter: hard physical (no overlap, edge clearance, panel mating) > electrical intent (decoupling proximity, ground pour integrity, critical-net length) > preference (wirelength, vias, tidiness).
3. score() must include rule violations weighted by tier, so the optimizer CANNOT silently trade away a rule to win on HPWL. This is the direct fix for the bug above.
4. Relaxation is explicit and ordered: when infeasible, relax the lowest tier first and record what was broken and by how much ("break them slightly to fit"), surfaced in the report instead of silently degrading.
5. Composable evaluation (the monad flavour): placement -> Vec<Violation> per rule, rules compose/pipeline, and the placer/loop consumes one uniform interface rather than each rule editing the greedy loop.

Supersedes ad-hoc conditionals now living in board.rs (DECOUPLE_PULL bonus, power_header_refdes special case, control_rotation heuristics, overflow lane). Related: [[legion-of-bom-w95]] (decoupling), [[legion-of-bom-t5t]] (min-HP ignores edge clearance), [[legion-of-bom-jiv]], [[legion-of-bom-j54.17]] (pour vs back-side SMD), [[legion-of-bom-5p5]] (panel from real layout).
notes:
ITEM 5 (composable evaluation) DONE (commit 0a71d13) — the UI forced it, which is why waiting was right. rules::assess returns every rule's standing (tier, subject, detail, signed margin_mm, repair), passes included; evaluate() is assess().filter(!ok). One evaluation feeds three consumers — layout::score, LayoutReport.findings, and the dashboard panel — so they cannot disagree. With two call sites a uniform interface is speculative; with three reading the same numbers it is load-bearing.

Shipped with it: GET /api/circuits/{name}/rules reading the BUILT board (guide::placements_from_board), a dashboard panel under the PCB viewer (tier badge, sentence, signed margin, worst first), and PlacedPart.rotation_deg which parse_board computed and discarded.

ALL FIVE DESIGN-DIRECTION ITEMS DONE. What remains is breadth, not architecture. Next variants: KeepOut (mounting holes, panel cutout shadows — clean fit, no new context). Side-aware decoupling (Proximity is 2D, so a cap on the opposite face reads ~0mm and passes; opposite-side decoupling is legitimate technique so this needs a product decision first). PourClearance investigated and rejected — see legion-of-bom-j54.17.
close_reason:
Architecture complete — all five design-direction items shipped: rules as data (rules.rs), tiered (Tier), priced into score(), ordered relaxation with the damage reported (relax_key + findings), and composable evaluation (rules::assess, forced by the dashboard panel becoming the third consumer). Two variants in service: Proximity (decoupling) and EdgeClearance, the latter added with no placer edits, which was the stated test of the design.

What remains is BREADTH, not architecture, so it belongs in per-variant beads rather than keeping this epic open at P0: KeepOut, side-aware decoupling (needs a product decision — opposite-face decoupling is legitimate technique), and drill/lug clearance (see legion-of-bom-s59). PourClearance was investigated and rejected, see legion-of-bom-j54.17.

Two rules recorded for anything added later: no placer edits, and every variant ships a way to compute its own physical floor (the legion-of-bom-1xm lesson — an unsatisfiable rule makes the optimiser look broken and the report cry wolf).

title: P0: Wire 'lob run <circuit>' full pipeline + report
description: Compose the stages (SKiDL run -> parse -> validate -> simulate -> verify -> BOM) into 'lob run', print a per-stage pass/fail report, and exit non-zero on any failure. This is THE working loop. DESIGN.md 2.2.
acceptance_criteria: 'lob run examples/rc_lowpass' runs all stages end-to-end, prints a report, exits 0 on success / non-zero on failure
close_reason: Completed the 6-stage Phase 0 loop. validate (core::validate): surfaces ERC WARNING/ERROR lines as structured findings, fails only on ERC errors. bom (core::bom): groups parts by value+footprint, qty+refdes, CSV + aligned table, flags missing footprints. Wired into 'lob run' in DESIGN order skidl→parse→validate→simulate→verify→bom with per-stage report + non-zero exit. Verified end-to-end on RC filter: all 6 stages pass, exit 0, BOM CSV written. 30 core tests, fmt+clippy clean.

title: P0: Textbook verification — assert simulated cutoff vs 1/(2piRC)
description: Compare the simulated -3dB point to the analytic cutoff and fail the stage if outside tolerance. This is what makes Phase 0 a *proof* of the loop, not just a run. DESIGN.md 14.1, 1.2.
acceptance_criteria: passes for correct RC values; deliberately-wrong values fail with a clear diff; tolerance configurable
close_reason: core::verify::check_rc_cutoff computes analytic 1/(2piRC) from parsed R/C values and asserts the simulated -3dB cutoff within a configurable tolerance. End-to-end: expected 1000.97 Hz vs simulated 1000.96 Hz (0.001% err). Failure path unit-tested (wrong cutoff → failed outcome w/ diff). Non-single-RC → skipped.

title: P0: SPICE deck generation + ngspice runner (AC analysis)
description: Generate a SPICE netlist from the Circuit model, run ngspice (AC sweep for the RC filter), and parse the frequency response. DESIGN.md 5.1.
acceptance_criteria: ngspice runs headless on generated deck; AC magnitude vs frequency parsed into data lob can assert on
close_reason: core::spice generates a SPICE deck from the Circuit (pin→net inversion, GND→0, R/C/L support, IN/OUT/GND harness), runs 'ngspice -b', and parses the AC response (freq, vdb). AcResult exposes passband gain + interpolated -3dB cutoff. Verified: 601-point sweep on the RC filter. 9 spice/units tests.

title: P0: KiCad netlist parser -> Circuit (CircuitSource impl)
description: Parse the KiCad netlist emitted by SKiDL into the core Circuit model as the first CircuitSource implementation. Captures parts (refdes, value, footprint) and nets (connections/pins). DESIGN.md 3.3.
acceptance_criteria: parses the RC netlist into parts+nets; round-trip unit test on a fixture netlist; cargo test passes
close_reason: core::netlist parses the KiCad S-expr netlist into the Circuit model (first CircuitSource producer): parts (refdes/value/footprint/libsource) + nets (name + pins), deterministically sorted. Self-contained S-expr reader, no new deps. Wired as stage 2 of 'lob run' (parses the real generated netlist: 2 parts, 3 nets). 14 unit tests incl. round-trip on an RC netlist fixture; fmt+clippy clean.

title: P0: SKiDL runner stage (script -> netlist + ERC)
description: Rust stage that shells out to run a SKiDL script in a subprocess, captures the generated KiCad netlist file and the ERC output. Handles non-zero exit / missing interpreter gracefully. First real pipeline stage.
acceptance_criteria: given examples/rc_lowpass, produces a netlist artifact + captured ERC text; errors surfaced, not panicked
close_reason: SKiDL runner (core::skidl::SkidlRunner) shells out via the venv python, runs in a scratch work_dir so artifacts stay out of the repo, captures netlist + ERC report, surfaces missing-interpreter/non-zero-exit as StageError (not panic). Wired as stage 1 of 'lob run'; verified end-to-end on examples/rc_lowpass.py. 10 unit tests, fmt+clippy clean.

title: P0: RC low-pass filter demo circuit in SKiDL
description: Write the first demo circuit (single-pole RC low-pass) as a standalone SKiDL script under examples/, with documented component values and the textbook -3dB cutoff fc = 1/(2*pi*R*C). This is the known-good fixture the whole loop is validated against. DESIGN.md 3.1, 14.1.
acceptance_criteria: SKiDL script runs and emits a KiCad netlist; expected fc recorded alongside; ERC clean
notes: RC low-pass at examples/rc_lowpass.py: R1=1k, C1=159n -> fc=1/(2piRC)~=1.001kHz. Values are the single source of truth; verify stage (P0.7) recomputes fc from parsed R/C rather than a hard-coded number. SKiDL emits a clean KiCad S-expr netlist (0 ERC errors). The 2 ERC WARNINGS are benign single-pin-net notices on the open IN/GND ports of a 2-port filter block; the sim stage (P0.6) wraps it in an AC source/ground testbench.

title: Epic: Phase 0 — End-to-end demo loop (local-only)
description: Prove the full pipeline on textbook circuits (RC low-pass filter, then non-inverting op-amp gain stage) with known-good answers before any real product design.
