SKiDL -> netlist -> parse -> validate (ERC) -> ngspice sim checked vs textbook values -> BOM. Entirely local, no network. DESIGN.md 14.1, 1.2.
close_reason: Phase 0 complete: the full 6-stage loop (SKiDL -> parse -> validate -> simulate -> verify -> BOM) is proven end-to-end on two textbook circuits with known-good answers — RC low-pass (cutoff vs 1/2piRC, 0.001%) and non-inverting op-amp (gain vs 1+Rf/Rg, 0.05% via the component's real subckt model). Local-only, self-verifying, non-zero exit on failure. Stretch task P0.11 (layout scaffolding) superseded by the Layout epic's kicad-ipc-rs task (j54.5).

title: Carrier validation for CV/audio/gate voltage ranges and protection
description:
Why this exists: carrier boards are a high-risk boundary between Eurorack voltages and STM32/codec pins. LOB should catch unsafe direct connections and missing protection before layout/fab.

Work: add validation rules over sub-board pin capabilities and panel/control nets: no raw Eurorack CV/audio into unprotected ADC/GPIO pins, audio pins use the expected conditioning/profile, gate inputs are clamped/protected, output drivers match expected range, and calibration/test points exist where required.

Acceptance: unsafe carrier fixtures fail with actionable findings; Patch SM direct connections that are already conditioned by the module profile pass.
close_reason: Added carrier safety validation over sub-board profiles: Patch SM direct panel wiring passes because the profile is Eurorack-conditioned; Seed2 DFM raw codec/ADC/GPIO-style pins fail when tied directly to external panel jacks and pass when a front-end breaks the direct net. Validated with cargo fmt --check, cargo test -p legion-of-bom-core, and cargo clippy -p legion-of-bom-core --all-targets -- -D warnings.

title: Carrier-board netlist model for SOM pins and panel controls
description:
Why this exists: a carrier board should describe panel hardware and SOM connections directly: audio jack to AUDIO_IN_L, pot/CV jack to ADC/CV input, gate jack to gate input, outputs to conditioned outputs.

Work: define the circuit/model conventions and helper APIs for a carrier around a sub-board/SOM, keeping topology explicit and still consumed through CircuitSource. It should support Patch SM first, then Seed2 DFM once analog front-end blocks exist.

Acceptance: a small carrier fixture can bind jacks/pots/switches to named SOM pins and produce a circuit/netlist that the existing board generation path understands.
close_reason: Added carrier-board circuit builder for Patch SM SOM pins and panel controls; validated with cargo fmt --check, cargo test -p legion-of-bom-core, and cargo clippy -p legion-of-bom-core --all-targets -- -D warnings.

title: Patch SM carrier profile and named pin/capability map
description:
Why this exists: Patch SM is the fast path for STM32 + codec + Eurorack CV/audio carrier boards because the module already carries the high-risk Eurorack-level conditioning. LOB has vendored Patch SM footprints, but only Daisy Seed has first-class named-pin metadata.

Work: add a Patch SM hardware profile under the existing sub-board primitive: named pad aliases, audio/CV/gate/control capabilities, board body/keepout/standoff metadata as far as the vendored footprint supports it, and tests proving a circuit can route to semantic names like AUDIO_IN_L, AUDIO_OUT_L, CV_1, GATE_IN_1 instead of raw A1/B2 pads.

Acceptance: Patch SM can be referenced through LobModule with semantic pin names/capabilities, the footprint still comes from the vendored Electrosmith file, and missing/unknown names fail clearly.
close_reason: Added Patch SM sub-board profile with semantic pin aliases and coarse carrier capabilities over the vendored Electrosmith footprint. Board generation now uses vendored profile aliases as well as synthesized SubboardSpec aliases, so carrier nets can target AUDIO_IN_L/AUDIO_OUT_L/CV_1/CV_OUT_1 by name and route to B4/B2/C5/C10. Added profile and routing regression tests. Verified cargo fmt --check, cargo test -p legion-of-bom-core, and cargo clippy -p legion-of-bom-core --all-targets -- -D warnings.

title: Layout scoring rewards attempts where DRC could not run
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] extra confirmed finding. layout.rs removes the large DRC error penalty when DRC is unrunnable, so an unchecked layout attempt can win over checked attempts. Fix should score missing/unrunnable DRC as unknown or failed, not as cleaner than reported DRC errors.

title: fab CPL parser silently drops rows with fewer than 7 fields
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] extra confirmed finding. fab.rs drops CPL rows with fewer than 7 fields without reporting skipped/incomplete data. Fix should record and surface skipped rows so malformed or truncated pick-and-place input cannot quietly produce an incomplete package.

title: fab exports can reuse stale fixed temp-path outputs
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] extra confirmed finding. fab.rs reads kicad-cli outputs back from fixed temp paths that are not cleared first; export_cpl is the worst case because a stale CPL can become the shipped pick-and-place. Fix should use fresh temp outputs or delete/validate expected outputs before reading, matching the stale-file defense already documented in drc.rs.

title: Dashboard reports broken: 0 when footprint facts cannot be built
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] finding 14. web/src/render.rs turns build_facts errors into facts=None, causing derive_in to omit edge-clearance and overlap rules and report no broken rules even when a part is off board. Linux hosts trigger this when kicad_footprint_dir cannot find KiCad footprints. Fix should surface the missing facts error and avoid clean-looking dashboard output.

title: Second CSV in a fab package silently replaces the first
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] finding 13. import.rs assigns the CPL/BOM result inside a loop, so a second CSV can replace rows parsed from the first. Reproduced with bottom-pos rows C9/C10 plus top-pos row R1 producing only R1 and no skipped diagnostics. Fix should merge compatible CSVs or report ambiguity instead of silently losing a board side.

title: Imported CPL rows are dropped and coordinates truncated without skipped-row reporting
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] finding 12. import.rs drops CPL rows with blank coordinates and parses values like '1,234.5' as x=1.0 without recording the problem. ImportedBoard::skipped exists so callers can report incomplete imports, but row parsers do not populate it. Fix should preserve skipped-row diagnostics and parse comma-formatted coordinates correctly or reject them explicitly.

title: Excellon reader creates zero-diameter holes, misses inch units, and drops modal holes
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] finding 10. gerber.rs fails common Excellon cases: tool definitions such as T01C0.800F00S00 parse to 0mm diameter, M71/M72 unit commands are ignored so inch files are scaled wrong, and modal single-axis coordinate lines are dropped. Fix should parse tool diameter prefixes, M71/M72 units, and modal X/Y coordinates with tests.

title: Gerber aperture parser panics and misreads legal leading-zero D-codes
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] finding 9. gerber.rs slices aperture definitions by the length of the reparsed number instead of the consumed digit run. Reproduced panic on '%ADD*%' and misread '%ADD010R,2.0X1.0*%' as a circular aperture. Fix should parse the D-code digit span explicitly and reject malformed definitions without panicking.

title: Invalid or empty DRC JSON parses as clean and can ship fab output
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] finding 8. drc.rs defaults all violation vectors, so arbitrary JSON objects deserialize to zero violations and is_clean()==true; an existing test enshrines from_json('{}') as clean. Fix should validate the expected DRC schema and treat missing/renamed/truncated reports as an error, consistent with stale-file defenses.

title: Simulation StageError is converted into a passing StageOutcome
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] finding 6. cli/main.rs converts simulation errors such as ToolNotFound, ToolFailed, or no transient data into StageOutcome::passed with a warning, so lob run exits 0 and bypasses vacuous-pass guards. Fix should preserve the StageOutcome versus StageError contract and make production code type-force the distinction.

title: SPICE skips socketed op-amps and JFETs before model resolution
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] finding 5. spice.rs is_electrical_noop skips any footprint containing socket and any refdes starting with J before model resolution. That deletes socketed op-amps and standard JFET designators from the deck, then simulation still reports numbers. Fix should only skip true electrical no-ops and should report missing SPICE models for active devices.

title: lob fab includes all THT parts in assembly BOM if board parse fails
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] finding 4. cli/main.rs guide::parse_board(...).map(...).unwrap_or_default() turns a board parse error into an empty hand_soldered set, so jlc_bom_csv filters nothing and silently puts THT parts back into the assembly BOM. Fix should surface the parse failure and avoid producing misleading fab assembly output.

title: ERC read failure or empty ERC file reports as a clean pass
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] finding 3. validate.rs swallows read_to_string failures with .ok(), and an empty ERC file matches no error prefix, so the stage returns passed plus affirmative info. Several out/* directories had 0-byte .erc files. Fix should distinguish unreadable/missing/empty ERC output from a clean ERC and return StageError or failing outcome as appropriate.

title: No LCSC part numbers anywhere: PartRecord has no field for one
description:
Found while fixing [[legion-of-bom-g5a]], and it is the half of that bead which is NOT a code defect.

The assembly BOM's 'LCSC Part #' column is filled from BomLine::mpn. Two problems, and the
second is the real one:

1. An MPN is not an LCSC code. The column wants a C-number (C6961); an MPN is the
   manufacturer's (TL074CDR). JLCPCB's BOM step will often match an MPN, but the column is
   misnamed for what we put in it.

2. THERE IS NOWHERE TO PUT A C-NUMBER. parts::PartRecord has mpn, manufacturer,
   datasheet_url, verified_by_human, verified_by, image_url, assembly_steps, pins, ratings —
   and no lcsc field. So even a fully verified part cannot carry the identifier the fab
   actually orders by. This is why every line on every board we produce is blank, not because
   the parts are unresolved.

MEASURED: slew_limiter 14 of 14 assembly designators unsourceable; dual 26 of 26.

WHAT g5a DID FIX: the fab gate no longer pretends. It now names every unsourceable designator,
stops saying 'upload the CPL + BOM for assembly', and says the PCB half is orderable on its own.
That converts a silent unusable artifact into a blocking, actionable one — but it does not put a
number in the column.

FIX: add lcsc: Option<String> to PartRecord, populate it from the JLCPCB/EasyEDA lookup we
already have (jlcpcb.rs fetches by LCSC code, so the code is in hand at fetch time and is being
discarded), thread it through BomLine, and prefer it over mpn in the LCSC column. Then the
existing 'lob parts suggest -> fetch -> verify' flow ends with an orderable BOM.

Until then, both boards need their 8 (single) / 14 (dual) lines matched by hand in JLCPCB's BOM
step, which is a normal workflow — just not an automated one.

title: Pot round-trips through the panel with 0.4mm of error; jacks are exact
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 on puget-hardware's slew_limiter.

The declared panel (now authoritative, committed 713ede2) says RV1 at y = 104.5. The board is
placed from that panel. Deriving a panel back OFF that built board returns RV1 at y = 104.9 —
0.4mm out. The three jacks round-trip EXACTLY (J1 IN 52.3 -> 52.3, J2 35.9, J4 19.5).

So the error is specific to the pot, which is also the part with (a) a large origin_offset —
an Alpha pot's origin is pin 1 and its shaft sits ~5.35mm away — and (b) a 90 degree rotation,
since board.rs control_rotation turns every pot. Both of those are exactly what
[[legion-of-bom-za4]] was about: 'the reverse trip (cutout -> placement) already subtracts that
offset, so origin-mapping made the two directions disagree and a part drift by one offset per
round trip'. za4 fixed the gross case; this looks like a residual.

WHY IT MATTERS: panel_from_board's bbox centre is the 'hardware mount point' that decides where
the DXF drills. 0.4mm is inside a Thonkiconn's slack but a pot bushing is a tighter fit, and
the error is systematic, not noise.

CAVEAT ON PROVENANCE: the number moved from 104.5 to 104.9 across [[legion-of-bom-4t9]] (the
rotated-pad-extent fix) in the same session. 4t9 changed pad_bb, which feeds the auto-outline,
and panel_from_board measures from the Edge.Cuts origin — so the outline shifting by a fraction
is a plausible cause and I have NOT separated the two. First step is to check out the commit
before 4t9 and re-derive, which settles whether this is old or newly introduced.

Do not close on inspection; measure it.

title: lob board --iterations 0 installs EurorackPlacer, which predates the cross-side THT fix
description:
Split out of [[legion-of-bom-p6m]]; noticed by the DRY audit 2026-08-12.

board_options_with_panel_and_placement (cli/main.rs) installs EurorackPlacer. It is replaced by
SeededPlacer only when iterations > 0 (layout.rs). So lob board --iterations 0 lays out with
the one-shot placer.

WHY THAT MATTERS: the two placers do not agree about what a collision is.

  EurorackPlacer  plain rects_overlap — no side awareness, no THT pads, no repack
  SeededPlacer    placement_clear — side/height/THT-pad aware, fail-first repack

The THT-pad awareness is exactly [[legion-of-bom-ude]], a closed P0: through-hole pads are
copper on BOTH layers, so a back-side 0603 can land on the back annulus of a front jack pin and
make every other pad on that net unreachable. SeededPlacer has the fix. EurorackPlacer does not.
So a closed P0 is reachable through a flag.

Compounding: minimum_hp sizes the board with SeededPlacer (board.rs), so at --iterations 0 the
width is chosen by one placer and the parts are placed by another.

Also noted by the audit: layout.rs's eurorack_trial_build sets EurorackPlacer in a block
documented as 'set up exactly as a real build', where run_layout_loop always overwrites it —
misleading, harmless.

FIX: install SeededPlacer in board_options_with_panel_and_placement when a panel exists, and
consider deleting EurorackPlacer outright — the DRY audit's recommendation, since nothing else
needs a second answer to 'where do the free parts go'.

title: Crossfader: 5 unrouted connections and ~20 minutes of wall clock to lay out 42 HP
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12. lob board on puget-hardware's crossfader (42 HP declared panel, fresh — it passed the new panel gate) took over 20 minutes of wall clock and finished with:

  5 connection(s) left unrouted
    - net 13 (CV_IN): could not route to pad R20.1
    - net 15 (GND): could not route to pad J7.S
    - net 15 (GND): could not route to pad J7.TN
    - net 31 (OUT_R): could not route to pad U5.6
    - net 31 (OUT_R): could not route to pad U5.7

TWO SEPARATE QUESTIONS, and the second needs answering first:

RUNTIME. 42 HP x 128.5mm at the current grid pitch is a large surface, and PathfinderRouter
now runs up to 160 iterations ([[legion-of-bom-z3t]]). 20 minutes makes this circuit
effectively untestable in a normal loop, which is likely why its problems have gone
unnoticed. Worth profiling before tuning anything: is it the iteration count, the grid
resolution, or per-iteration surface rebuild?

ROUTABILITY. Run unroutable_by_placement on it (examples/route_bench.rs already reports
this) to split 'the router gave up' from 'placement made it impossible'. That single
measurement is what made the slew limiter tractable and it should be the first thing done
here too. Two of the five are the same jack's ground pads and two more are adjacent pins of
one op-amp, which smells like local blockage rather than global congestion.

Do NOT reach for more HP — it is already 42.

title: Six tests pass against a no-op or a tautology: edge band, decouple keepout, analytical weights, analytic_check
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12, each verified by running the stub or flipping the constant.

1. routing_refuses_to_enter_the_board_edge_band (route.rs:2072) MEASURES THE PAD HALO, NOT
   THE EDGE BAND. Re-run with edge_clearance_mm: 0.0 -> still conflicts=1, tracks=0. Then
   with the inset fully neutralised -> STILL conflicts=1, tracks=0. The obstacle wall's own
   clearance halo already seals y<1. Fix: move the wall to y=2, pads to y=0.6, assert the net
   IS routed at edge_clearance 0.0 and IS NOT at 0.5 — the single-parameter delta is the
   only thing that proves the feature.

2. a_bypass_cap_is_not_snapped_on_top_of_an_anchored_control (decouple.rs:251) PASSES IF
   snap IS A NO-OP. Its only assertion is dx >= 5.8 || dy >= 5.4, and the fixture starts C2
   at (50,62) with J1 at (50,45) — dy = 17 BEFORE ANYTHING RUNS. The implementation is
   actually correct (it reports skipped: "C2: the spot against U1's rail pin is occupied by
   J1"), but the test cannot tell 'correctly refused' from 'did nothing'. Its own sibling at
   decouple.rs:314 already has the right guard (assert_ne! the start position). Copy it.

3. the_decoupling_bond_outweighs_a_signal_net (analytical.rs:453) is x >= x. C1 is the only
   free part between two anchors, so the weighted average makes to_jack/to_ic == DECOUPLE_PULL
   IDENTICALLY. Measured: PULL=3.0 -> ratio 3.000000000; PULL=1.0 -> ratio 1.0, assertion
   still true. Setting DECOUPLE_PULL=1.0 — i.e. deleting the decoupling bond entirely — keeps
   it green. At 0.5 it fails on float noise, so the only way it can fail is spuriously.

4. the_solution_stays_inside_the_hull_of_what_is_fixed (analytical.rs:507) passes against the
   documented no-op fallback: the fixture's home (20,64) is already inside the asserted hull,
   and solve-with-no-edges returns every part at exactly its home. Fix: put the home OUTSIDE
   the hull.

5. a_two_pin_net_pulls_harder_than_a_rail (analytical.rs:627) compares constants to
   themselves — w() SUMS all edges between a pair, so 1.0 + 0.5 == 0.5 + 1.0 and swapping the
   weighting leaves it green.

6. analytic_check_runs_the_matching_check (verify.rs:424) also passes when NO check ran —
   analytic_check returns StageOutcome::passed(STAGE) when nothing matched, and findings is
   never inspected. Its sibling asserts the same property for the opposite situation, which
   proves the two states are not separated.

NOTE on 3/4/5: analytical.rs has zero call sites anywhere (see the architecture audit), so
those three are testing dead code. Decide whether it lives before spending effort there.

title: summing.rs: 376 lines, zero executed coverage — its only snap test takes the first-line early return
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12.

summing.rs has two tests. no_symbol_library_means_no_opinion (summing.rs:352) passes
symbol_dir: None, and summing::snap line 94 is

    let Some(symbol_dir) = symbol_dir else { return report; };

so the test exits on the function's first line. The other test
(only_the_amplifier_inputs_count_as_high_impedance, summing.rs:336) is a pure string
predicate that never calls snap.

Net effect: no pin-name lookup, no net->passive walk, no placement, no pinned-part handling,
no determinism check is ever executed. The most recent commit on this branch before the
audit was 'summing: put the passives on an op-amp input against the pin' — that change is
untested in the literal sense.

Compounding: summing::snap is DELIBERATELY NOT CALLED from the board pipeline
([[legion-of-bom-6yh]] — it overrides placement and so wins even when it costs 5 DRC
errors). So this is 376 lines of untested, unreachable code that we keep maintaining and
that keeps appearing in commits.

DECIDE, do not drift: either (a) give it a seam that injects pin_names so the body can be
tested and it can be re-enabled as a tradeable pass rather than an override, or (b) move it
to examples/ or delete it, preserving the reasoning in the bead. The related DRY finding is
that its pad_on_net copy has the CORRECT numeric pin sort while the live copy in decouple.rs
sorts lexicographically — so the dead module holds the better code.

title: 14 tests silently return when KiCad/dolt/ngspice is absent — on CI the suite is green having asserted nothing
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12. 14 tests begin with a guard of the shape

    let Some(dir) = kicad_footprint_dir() else { return; };

and PASS by returning. Sites: board.rs:3213,4225,4304,4338,4429; panel.rs:2521,2910;
parts.rs:751,832; schematic.rs:1096,1128; spice.rs:1312; fetch.rs:129; cli/main.rs:3379,3443.

All three tools happen to be installed on this machine, so they really run HERE. Anywhere
else — Linux CI, a fresh clone, a colleague's laptop — they report success having executed
nothing. The suite cannot tell 'passed' from 'skipped'.

Several have a SECOND escape hatch: Err(_) => return with a comment like 'library layout
differs', so even with KiCad present a generation failure is swallowed as a pass.

Two of them also 'return' before their remove_dir_all, leaking temp dirs on the skip path.

FIX: #[ignore] with an explicit opt-in job makes the hole visible in the count
(N passed; M ignored) instead of invisible. Better where practical: a checked-in minimal
footprint fixture so the test does not need a system KiCad at all — the geometry these
tests exercise does not need the real library, only A library.

title: Fab package tells JLC two different things: CPL places 23 parts, BOM assembles 8, and every LCSC number is blank
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 on out/slew_limiter/fab, a package the gate reported as ready to upload
(0 DRC errors, 12 warnings).

THREE DEFECTS, all in the money path.

1. CPL AND BOM CONTRADICT EACH OTHER. The hand-soldered filter works on the BOM — C4 C5 J1
J2 J3 J4 RV1 RV2 SW1 are correctly withheld ([[legion-of-bom-vex]]). The CPL was never
taught the same thing: it still lists all 23 placements INCLUDING those 9. So the upload
says 'assemble these 8 SMD lines' and 'here are placement coordinates for 23 parts, 9 of
which are through-hole'. Exactly the two-paths-one-question shape — one path learned about
kit-awareness and the other did not.

2. EVERY LCSC PART # IS EMPTY. All 8 assembly lines:
     470nF,C1,C_1206_3216Metric,
     100nF,"C2, C3",C_0603_1608Metric,
     ... LM13700,U1,SOIC-16... ,   TL074,U2,SOIC-14... ,
   JLC cannot assemble a BOM with no part numbers; this needs manual matching for all 8 in
   their UI, or it bounces. vex mentioned this in passing about C4/C5 but its stated defect
   was the THT lines, which IS fixed — this is the separate half.

3. THE CONSOLE MISCOUNTS. It prints 'BOM (14 line items)' while the file has 8 data rows
   (cli/main.rs:1469) — it reports the pre-filter count. A number that says 14 when the
   artifact says 8 is how you stop trusting the summary.

FIX: (1) route the CPL through the same hand_soldered set the BOM uses — one shared
kit-split, not two. (2) resolve LCSC numbers from the parts library into the fab BOM, or
refuse to write an assembly BOM with blank part numbers and say which parts are unresolved.
(3) count after filtering.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
CONFIRMED SYSTEMIC 2026-08-12, not specific to the slew limiter. The dual's fab package, written today with 0 DRC errors, has all three defects identically:

  console says   BOM (14 line items)
  file has       8 data rows            <- pre-filter count, same off-by-six as the single
  CPL has        46 placements
  of which       17 are hand-soldered   <- C41 C42 C51 C52 J11 J12 J21 J22 J3 J41 J42
                                           RV11 RV12 RV21 RV22 SW11 SW12, all correctly
                                           withheld from the BOM and all still in the CPL
  LCSC filled    0 of 8

So the kit-split reaches the BOM and not the CPL on every circuit, and no assembly BOM this
project produces currently carries a part number.

CONSEQUENCE, now that the dual actually builds ([[legion-of-bom-kcq]], [[legion-of-bom-ku4]]):
both boards are BUILDABLE and neither is ORDERABLE. The gate says 'upload the CPL + BOM for
assembly' and what it wrote would have JLC quoting placements for 17 through-hole parts nobody
asked them to fit, against 8 lines with no part numbers to fit anything with. This is the last
thing between the dual and a real order.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
FIXED 2026-08-12, verified on both circuits by set-comparing the two files rather than reading the summary.

  slew_limiter        CPL 14  BOM 14   in CPL not BOM: none   in BOM not CPL: none
  dual_slew_limiter   CPL 29  BOM 29   in CPL not BOM: none   in BOM not CPL: none

Was 23 vs 8 and 46 vs 8. The dual's 29 is 46 parts minus 17 hand-soldered, which is the number
it should always have been.

1. CPL/BOM CONTRADICTION — the cause was ORDERING, not a missing filter. hand_soldered was
computed AFTER export_cpl ran, so structurally only the BOM could ever see it. Moved it before
and threaded the set through export_cpl and jlc_cpl_from_kicad_pos.

2. THE MISCOUNT — new jlc_assembly_bom returns the rows it actually wrote. It used to print
bom.lines.len(), the pre-filter number: '14 line items' over an 8-row file.

3. THE BLANK LCSC COLUMN — the gate no longer pretends. It stops saying 'upload the CPL + BOM
for assembly', says the PCB half IS orderable on its own, names every unsourceable designator,
and gives the remedy. That converts a silent unusable artifact into a blocking, actionable one.
The underlying data gap is NOT fixed and is not a code defect — see [[legion-of-bom-4iz]]:
PartRecord has no lcsc field, so there is nowhere to put the number JLCPCB orders by. Splitting
it out rather than closing this bead over it.

TWO MORE FOUND IN THE SAME CODE, both the same class as the bug itself:

• export_cpl read kicad-cli's output back from a FIXED temp path that was never cleared. A
  failed export after a previous success would have shipped a PREVIOUS BOARD'S pick-and-place.
  This is item 'fab.rs:130/209/595' from the robustness audit ([[legion-of-bom-z8c]]) and
  exactly the hazard drc.rs documents and defends against. Now removed before the run, and a
  missing file after a reported success is a ToolFailed rather than a silent read of whatever
  was there.
• The hand_soldered lookup did unwrap_or_default() on a parse failure — an empty set puts every
  through-hole part BACK into the assembly BOM, quietly reintroducing the exact regression the
  split exists to prevent. Now a hard error; the board was written and DRC'd seconds earlier, so
  failing to parse it is a real fault.

TESTS: the_cpl_withholds_exactly_what_the_bom_withholds (drives both halves with one set and
asserts the reported count equals the artifact's row count) and
a_bom_line_with_no_part_number_is_reported_unsourceable (including that a hand-soldered part is
not reported, since it is not the fab's problem). 427 -> 429 core.

title: build_layout exists to stop guide/board/fab diverging and two of the three do not call it
description:
VERIFIED 2026-08-12 by grep. build_layout (cli/main.rs:1063) has exactly ONE caller:
guide_cmd at main.rs:1834. board_cmd (main.rs:1183) and fab_cmd (main.rs:1329) each inline
their own copy of the same match.

Its own doc comment claims the opposite: 'Exists so no command can quietly emit a
*different* board from the one the fab package contains. If you are about to call
generate_board_report directly, you probably want this instead.' I wrote that. It is not
true, and my commit message on c69abff repeated the claim by describing build_layout as
shared by guide and fab. Correcting the record here.

THE CONCRETE DIVERGENCE — build_layout uses LayoutLoop::default(), so mode is always
Analog. board_cmd and fab_cmd pass parse_mode(&mode). So:

  lob fab slew_limiter --mode digital   -> digital-mode layout
  lob guide slew_limiter                -> analog-mode layout, always

Two different boards from the same circuit. And guide_cmd writes out/<n>/<n>.kicad_pcb,
which is what the web dashboard renders (web/src/render.rs:443-455) and what lob panel
derive reads back (main.rs:2824), while fab's board is out/<n>/fab/<n>.kicad_pcb. That is
precisely the guide-vs-fab split this function was written to close — it just closed it
for the default mode only.

SECOND GAP: fab_cmd runs a pre-DRC Tier::Physical refusal gate (main.rs:1382-1406) that
neither of the other two has, so the rendered board can carry a violation fab would refuse
to package.

FIX: give build_layout mode + kicad_cli parameters and route board_cmd and fab_cmd through
it. The iterations-0 fallback should go through it too — see [[legion-of-bom-4t9]] and the
EurorackPlacer note below.

RELATED, same match arm: both fall back to generate_board_report / generate_board_artifacts
when iterations == 0, which installs EurorackPlacer (cli/main.rs:924) — the one-shot placer
that predates the 'THT pads are copper on both layers' fix in [[legion-of-bom-ude]].
SeededPlacer has that fix; EurorackPlacer does not. So lob board --iterations 0 can
reintroduce a closed P0. Worth folding into this fix or its own bead.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
FIXED 2026-08-12.

WHAT CHANGED
build_layout now takes the whole LayoutLoop and returns board + conflicts + collisions, so
there is no knob a caller can hold that it silently ignores — it used to hardcode
LayoutLoop::default(). board_cmd and fab_cmd no longer inline their own copy of the match;
both go through it. guide gained --mode, which it never had, so it could not be told and
always laid out analog. build_one passes one LAYOUT_MODE and one LAYOUT_ITERS to both guide
and fab.

The compiler confirmed the routing the useful way: generate_board_report became an UNUSED
IMPORT in the CLI. That is the evidence that nothing bypasses the shared path any more.

NEW TEST board_fab_and_guide_default_to_the_same_layout parses all three commands with no
--mode and asserts the defaults match and that the shared default parses. This bead's root
cause was three separately-chosen defaults that happened to agree; an assertion is what keeps
them agreeing. Same lesson as [[legion-of-bom-69v.1]] — the invariant was in a doc comment and
drifted.

MEASURED, and the result is narrower than the bead predicted. Ran lob guide slew_limiter at
--mode analog and --mode digital and diffed the emitted boards:

  seeded layout (analog):  6 attempt(s), signal HPWL 396mm, critical 52mm, 20 via(s)
  seeded layout (digital): 6 attempt(s), signal HPWL 396mm, critical 52mm, 20 via(s)
  boards: byte-identical

So the flag now demonstrably REACHES the layout — the guide reports the mode it was given, and
that line did not exist on the guide path at all before this change — but on this circuit it
does not change the board. The chain is verified link by link: flag -> parse_mode ->
LayoutLoop.mode -> build_layout -> run_layout_loop, where layout.rs:290 does
cfg.mode.weights(), and analog_mode_weights_criticals_harder_than_digital proves the weights
differ. The board is the same because the same placement attempt wins under both weightings on
a 23-part board.

Stating that plainly rather than claiming a fix I did not demonstrate: the divergence this bead
describes was STRUCTURAL and latent, not active on the slew limiter. lob fab --mode digital and
lob guide would have been scored differently and could have diverged on a board where the
weighting changes the winner; on this one it does not.

NOT DONE, and it is the deeper version: mode is still a per-invocation flag, not a per-circuit
manifest field like kit and panel. Guide and fab can now be MADE to agree; a manifest field
would make them agree by construction. Worth its own bead.

ALSO STILL OPEN from this bead's last paragraph: the iterations-0 path installs EurorackPlacer
(cli/main.rs), which predates the cross-side THT fix in [[legion-of-bom-ude]] that SeededPlacer
has. lob board --iterations 0 can therefore still reintroduce a closed P0. Untouched here —
needs its own bead.

Gates: 424 core + 21 web + 5 cli, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean.

title: [bug] Dual: decouple::snap leaves 5 bypass caps past the proximity rule (C2 20.1mm from U1, limit 8.7mm)
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-28 on ~/src/puget-hardware out/dual_slew_limiter, derived
10 HP panel, via crates/core/examples/rules_report. 5 of 1153 rules broken, all
Tier::Electrical, all the same rule:

  -11.5mm  C2 is 20.1mm from U1 (max 8.7mm)
   -2.2mm  C8 is 10.7mm from U2 (max 8.6mm)
   -1.0mm  C6 is  9.6mm from U3 (max 8.6mm)
   -0.5mm  C7 is  9.2mm from U1 (max 8.7mm)
   -0.3mm  C9 is  8.9mm from U3 (max 8.6mm)

C2 at 20.1mm against an 8.7mm limit is not a near miss — decouple::snap did not
move it at all. The dual has FOUR op-amp packages on shared rails where the
single has two, so decoupling_pairs is spreading caps across more ICs than snap
was exercised against; that is the first place to look.

This is most of the dual's placement score: 17895 total, of which roughly 2809
is the preference terms (signal 1010 + 3x204 critical + 0.5x51 vias +
0.2x1806 copper + 50x16 unrouted) — the remaining ~15100 is this rule penalty.

NOT a physical violation, so lob fab does not refuse on it; the board is refused
on DRC (13 errors, all unconnected) instead. See [[legion-of-bom-kcq]] for that
half.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
FIXED 2026-08-12 — THREE stacked defects, each only visible once the one outside it was fixed.

The bead's diagnosis (snap did not move C2 at all) was close but not the mechanism. New
examples/decouple_probe.rs runs the pass directly and prints its four exits separately, which
is what made the layers visible.

DEFECT 1 — THE FIRST GUESS LANDED INSIDE THE TARGET IC. clearance() carried a trailing * 0.5,
asking for half the distance that can ever separate two bodies. The probe printed it plainly:
    C6: the spot against U3's rail pin is occupied by U3
Blocked by the very part it was snapping to.

DEFECT 2 — ONE GUESS WAS THE ENTIRE SEARCH. When the spot was taken, snap gave up and left the
cap wherever global placement dropped it. That is how a cap ends up 20.1mm from its IC against
an 8.7mm rule: not a bad move, no move. 4 of 6 caps were skipping. It now walks outward from
the pin with a +/-25/+/-50 degree fan and takes the first genuinely clear spot, nearest and
straightest first. 6 snapped, 0 skipped.

DEFECT 3 — THE REACH WAS MEASURED FROM THE WRONG REFERENCE POINT, and this only surfaced
because fixing 1 made things WORSE. clearance() returned a CENTRE-TO-CENTRE half-sum,
min((cap+ic)/2), and snap applied it as a reach FROM THE PIN. The pin is already on the IC, so
the IC's half-extent was counted twice — caps landed 9-12mm out against an 8.6mm rule. The
original * 0.5 was a fudge cancelling roughly half that error, which is why removing it
(correct on its own terms) pushed the caps FURTHER out, 4.5 -> 7.9mm pad-to-pin. Now the reach
is what actually has to fit in it: the cap's own half-extent plus PAD_GAP_MM, from the pin,
with the verified outward search finding the tightest legal spot.

WHAT SETTLED IT was examples/decouple_check, whose doc already framed the right question — 'the
physical floor: two keep-outs touching... distance at it means the rule threshold is what needs
revisiting'. Measured slack above that floor was 1.1 to 5.6mm with the floor at ~6.6mm against
an 8.6mm limit, so the rule was satisfiable all along and the caps were simply too far out.
That ruled out 'the rule is wrong' before I went looking for a placement fix.

ON THE REAL BOARD, lob board + rules_report:
  BEFORE  5 broken, worst -11.5mm (C2 at 20.1mm from U1)
  AFTER   4 broken, worst  -1.3mm (C3 at  9.9mm from U2)
Also -0.9 C6, -0.5 C8, -0.3 C2. DRC 0 errors, 0 unconnected throughout.

NOT FULLY CLOSED, and the residual is different in kind — see the follow-up bead. These four
are near-misses of 0.3-1.3mm produced by the layout loop's global trade-off (6 attempts scored
across wirelength, vias, copper and rule penalty; a slightly worse-decoupled attempt can win on
the other terms), not by snap giving up or aiming wrong. snap itself now achieves 3.5-7.9mm
pad-to-pin on every cap.

title: [bug] Dual: PathfinderRouter returns byte-identical results to GridRouter on a 46-part board
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-28 on ~/src/puget-hardware out/dual_slew_limiter (46 parts,
derived 10 HP panel, 12 anchored), crates/core/examples/route_bench:

  router        unrouted   drc      copper  vias     score
  grid                16    16   1806.0mm    51   17895.2
  pathfinder          16    16   1806.0mm    51   17895.2

Identical to the last digit. On the 23-part single at the same widths the two
separate cleanly (6 HP: grid 4/4, pathfinder 2/2). Two different algorithms
producing the same copper to 0.1mm is not a coincidence — the likely reading is
that PathfinderRouter's negotiated-congestion loop is not converging on a board
this size and its "never worse than the grid baseline" guard is handing back
the baseline every time. PathfinderRouter::default() is max_iters 160, tuned on
a 23-part board.

IT IS NOT THE PLACEMENT, and that is measured:
  • nothing overflows — all 46 parts are on the board (place_probe, 10 HP:
    front 33.0%, back 11.2%, overflowed: none)
  • on an empty board (panel controls + power header only) every free part has
    a legal pose and position
  • route::unroutable_by_placement reports 0 — every net individually has a
    path; collectively they do not fit. That is congestion.
  • no Tier::Physical rule is broken (rules_report: 5 of 1153 broken, all
    Tier::Electrical)

FIRST EXPERIMENT: raise LOB_PF_ITERS well past 160 and see whether the numbers
move at all. If they do not move even at 1000, the fallback guard is firing and
the negotiation never produces a better board — which is the real bug.

Related: [[legion-of-bom-yck]] (router leaves nets unrouted on dense 2-layer
boards).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
ANSWERED AND FIXED 2026-08-12. This bead's premise was wrong, and the correction is the useful part.

THE MEASUREMENT WAS TAKEN AGAINST A ROUTER WE DO NOT SHIP. examples/route_bench defaulted to
max_iters: 24 while board.rs builds with PathfinderRouter::default(). So 'byte-identical to
GridRouter on 46 parts' was a 24-iteration PathFinder, and every theory built on it — the
negotiation not converging, the never-worse guard handing back the baseline every time — was
reasoning about the wrong binary. Fixed: route_bench now defaults to
PathfinderRouter::default().max_iters, and route.rs has the_shipping_router_is_the_default_one,
a deliberate change-detector so nobody moves the number without every recorded routing figure
being flagged as stale. It failed the moment I raised it, which is exactly when those figures
stopped meaning anything.

THE GUARD WAS WORKING CORRECTLY. At 160 rounds the negotiation genuinely had not settled, so
handing back the grid baseline was the right call — which is precisely why it looked identical.
Right mechanism, wrong budget.

IT CONVERGES. New LOB_PF_TRACE=1 prints every round that improves on the best so far. On the
dual, overused cells fall 1006 -> 237 by round 10, then grind: 161@33, 115@106, 94@123, 55@156,
5@158, 3@184, and ZERO at round 186. The 160 cap stopped it at round 158 holding five contested
cells — 26 rounds short.

  160 iters -> 17 unrouted, 16 DRC   (identical to grid, as reported)
  300 iters ->  0 unrouted,  0 DRC
  600 iters ->  0 unrouted,  0 DRC   (nothing bought over 300)

FIX: default 160 -> 600, plus PF_STALL_ROUNDS = 120 — stop when the best has not improved for
that many consecutive rounds. The stall break is what makes a generous cap safe: without it the
cap is the only stopping condition, so covering a hard board taxes every board that will never
settle, and the 42 HP crossfader already spends ~20 minutes at 160 ([[legion-of-bom-an8]]). 120
is sized from the trace, not picked: the longest gap between two improvements on this board is
33 rounds (123 -> 156), so 120 is ~3.6x the worst observed rate.

END TO END, shipping defaults, no env overrides:
  lob board dual_slew_limiter -> 2434 tracks, 106 vias
  lob drc                     -> 0 error(s), 0 unconnected
Twice, with different track counts (2817/111 and 2434/106) after a decoupling change — so
clean is robust, not a lucky seed.

COST: 16.6 minutes wall clock for the dual at 10 HP. That is 6 layout attempts x up to 600
rounds. Acceptable for a board that previously did not build at all, but it is the reason the
stall break exists and it makes [[legion-of-bom-an8]] (crossfader runtime) more pressing.

A CAVEAT ON THE FIRST SWEEP I RAN: its grid rows changed between runs, which is impossible
since grid does not read LOB_PF_ITERS. I had edited decouple.rs mid-sweep and cargo run rebuilt
partway through. Those numbers were discarded and the sweep re-run from one fixed binary. Worth
recording because the tell was the control row moving, not the treatment row.

title: Bench: LM13700 die/thermal channel coupling on the dual — SPICE cannot answer this one
description:
SPICE has answered the board-level half of channel independence on the dual
(legion-of-bom-9wh.1) and the answer is "negligible, and it is a layout
variable". This bead is the half SPICE STRUCTURALLY CANNOT ANSWER, so it does
not get closed by any simulation result.

WHY IT CANNOT BE SIMULATED. The LM13700 model is a datasheet BEHAVIOURAL OTA
(Iout = IABC*tanh(Vd/2Vt), bias pin two diode drops above V-). It has no thermal
node and no substrate term. Die coupling between the two OTAs cannot appear in
it at ANY parameter setting — not a tolerance question, a structural one.

WHY IT IS THE MOST PLAUSIBLE REAL CROSSTALK PATH ON THIS BOARD. The bias law is
IABC = (Vctrl - V_BIAS)/R3 with V_BIAS = 2*VBE + V-. Two VBEs is roughly
-4 mV/degC. At the SLOW end of the RATE knob the entire IABC is about 1 uA
(Vctrl = -10 V, R3 = 620k), so a few millivolts of V_BIAS shift is a
percent-level rate error. A channel running at full rate dissipates more than an
idle one, both halves are on one die, and the quiet channel's rate follows the
busy one's temperature. Board-level coupling measured at ~ -136 dB; this path
has no such bound from anything we have run.

MEASURE ON THE BENCH, with a real LM13700:
  1. Set channel 2 to the SLOW end of RATE and the DRIFT range (its most
     temperature-sensitive operating point). Log its slew rate over several
     minutes with channel 1 idle. This is the reference drift.
  2. Then drive channel 1 continuously at full rate and log channel 2's slew
     rate again. Look for a drift with a THERMAL TIME CONSTANT (tens of seconds
     to minutes), which is what distinguishes die heating from electrical
     coupling — electrical coupling would appear instantly.
  3. Repeat with the two channels' RANGE settings swapped, to separate a real
     die effect from anything specific to one OTA half.
  4. Signal crosstalk: channel 1 slewing full-scale, channel 2 holding DC,
     scope channel 2's output with the input shorted. Board-level SPICE says
     ~1.5 uVpp against a 10 Vpp aggressor at 20 mohm of shared return, so
     ANYTHING above about 100 uVpp is a real effect the simulation did not
     predict and needs explaining before fab.
  5. DRIVE BOTH CHANNELS SIMULTANEOUSLY IN THE SAME DIRECTION, not opposite.
     Measured in 9wh.1: the OTA output current follows the slew direction, so
     antiphase slewing CANCELS in the shared pins (V- moved 0 Vpp) while
     in-phase ADDS (5e-5 Vpp). A bench test built around antiphase would be
     testing the easy case.

ALSO NOT MODELLED, so also bench-only:
  * the behavioural OTA draws output current from V- for both polarities; the
    real part sources from V+ when sourcing, so per-rail conclusions are weaker
    than aggregate ones;
  * the Darlington buffer is an ideal follower drawing no rail current, while on
    the real part it is the largest current in the package.

DO NOT SEND THE DUAL TO FAB ON THE SIMULATION RESULT ALONE.

title: Simulate seam: whole-package LM13700, TL074, open pins, switches, multi-channel I/O
description:
The dual could not be simulated at all before this, and neither could the mono
board. Four measured blockers, all in the simulate seam, all fixed.

MEASURED BEFORE:
  lob run circuits/slew_limiter/slew_limiter.py
    -> error: simulate stage failed: no SPICE model or primitive mapping for: SW1, U2
  lob run circuits/dual_slew_limiter/dual_slew_limiter.py
    -> error: simulate stage failed: simulation needs a net named 'IN'
       (have: ... SIG_IN1, SIG_IN2, SIG_OUT1, SIG_OUT2 ...)

MEASURED AFTER: mono passes 7 stages, dual passes 8 (the extra one is the new
crosstalk gate, which self-selects and does not run on the mono board).

CHANGES, all in legion-of-bom:

  crates/core/src/spice/lob_builtin.lib
    * LM13700 goes from CHANNEL A ONLY (8 terminals: pins 1,3,4,5,6,7,8,11) to
      the whole package, all 16 pins in numeric order, both OTAs and both
      Darlington buffers. This is the change that makes a dual expressible.
      Pin numbers cited to the KiCad symbol the circuits themselves instantiate
      (Amplifier_Operational.kicad_sym): OTA A = 1 IABC, 2 DIODE_BIAS, 3 In+,
      4 In-, 5 Iout; buffer A 7->8; OTA B = 16 IABC, 15 DIODE_BIAS, 14 In+,
      13 In-, 12 Iout; buffer B 10->9; power 6 = V-, 11 = V+. Never memory —
      that is the [[design-guardrail-legion-of-bom-must-structurally-prevent]]
      mistake and it happened on this exact part.
    * TL074 added (quad). The mono board moved TL072 -> TL074 when the CV
      attenuverter needed sections C and D, and the catalogue never followed.
      Note the rails are NOT where the dual has them: V+ 8 -> 4 and V- 4 -> 11,
      so quietly reusing the TL072 model would tie section A's output to a rail.
      Cited to KiCad LM2902, which TL074 extends.
    * The behavioural model's limits are now written into the file itself
      rather than left to be rediscovered: output current drawn from V- for both
      polarities, ideal buffer drawing no rail current, and NO die/thermal
      coupling term at all.

  crates/core/src/symbols.rs — builtin_model()
    * LM13700 pin_order 1..16; TL074/TL084/LM324 entry added. Models list every
      pin of the package, so one entry serves a board that uses one channel and
      a board that uses both. This is the resolver (the parts-library stand-in),
      NOT the generator, so it stays on the right side of
      [[architecture-user-feedback-spice-macro-models-must-not]].

  crates/core/src/spice.rs
    * Unconnected subckt pins get their own dangling node (`U1_nc2`) instead of
      failing the deck. Required by the whole-package model: the mono board
      leaves OTA B's seven pins open, and both boards leave DIODE_BIAS (2/15)
      open — which is the datasheet's own normal test configuration. Whether an
      open pin is a MISTAKE is ERC's judgement, not the simulator's, and ERC
      already reports both. Each open pin gets a UNIQUE node; collapsing them
      would short an unused channel's inputs together.
    * Switches (`SW...`) contribute no device. A netlist records a switch's
      wiring and never its position, so there is nothing to instantiate and the
      contacts are open — for the RANGE switch that is the centre detent, the
      documented fastest range. This follows the existing refdes-CLASS precedent
      in the generator (R/C/L primitives, RV pots split at 50 %, J connectors
      skipped); it is not a per-DEVICE conditional.
    * Channel-suffix I/O inference: `channel_suffix`, `channel_nets`, and the
      public `signal_channels()`. A multi-channel board has no bare SIG_IN, and
      the harness previously just failed. `SimConfig::infer` now falls back to
      the lowest-numbered channel, and `signal_channels()` returns the paired
      per-channel I/O ([(SIG_IN1, SIG_OUT1), (SIG_IN2, SIG_OUT2)]) and is EMPTY
      for a single-channel board, so nothing downstream has to ask "is this a
      dual?".
    * `TranResult::peak_to_peak_v()`.

  crates/core/src/verify.rs — check_channel_crosstalk()
    New self-selecting check in the same style as check_rc_cutoff /
    check_noninverting_gain: returns None unless the circuit really has >= 2
    channels. Compares the undriven channel's excursion against the driven
    channel's swing, reports the ratio in dB, and fails a vacuous pass (an
    aggressor that never swung).

  crates/cli/src/main.rs — crosstalk_stage()
    New pipeline stage between transient and verify. Builds a step SEQUENCE
    stimulus (tus.13's ask (1)), holds every other channel's input at 0 V via
    TranDrive.cv (ask (2)), runs two driven transients with identical
    deterministic stimulus (one probe per run), and gates at 1e-3 = -60 dB.
    Soft-fails to a warning if the transient will not converge, matching the
    existing step-response stage.

VALIDATION RUN:
  cargo test    -> 417 + 21 + 1 passed, 0 failed
  cargo fmt --check -> clean
  cargo clippy -p legion-of-bom-core --lib --tests
                -p legion-of-bom-cli --bins --all-features -- -D warnings -> clean
    (NOTE: `cargo clippy --all-targets` fails on crates/core/examples/place_probe.rs
     with a type_complexity error. That file is UNTRACKED and not mine — another
     agent's concurrent work. My targets are clean.)
  lob run on slew_limiter (7 stages) and dual_slew_limiter (8 stages) -> pass
  mutation test on a copied dual with one shared net -> crosstalk gate FAILS,
    as designed

NEW UNIT TESTS: channel_suffix parsing; infer picks channel 1 on a dual;
signal_channels pairs channels and is empty for a single; unconnected subckt
pins get unique dangling nodes; a switch emits no device; crosstalk passes when
independent, fails on a shared node, fails vacuously on a dead stimulus, and
bows out of a single-channel circuit.

PRODUCT REPO (~/src/puget-hardware), for reference — not lob code:
  circuits/dual_slew_limiter/dual_slew_limiter_crosstalk.cir  (new)
  circuits/dual_slew_limiter/dual_slew_limiter.py  (docstring only: the "STILL
    OPEN / channel independence" bullet replaced with the measured result)

NOT COMMITTED. NOT PUSHED.

title: Dual slew limiter: channel independence — SPICE answer, with what SPICE cannot answer
description:
ANSWERED, with measurements. The dual's docstring flagged this as the one
dual-specific unknown: "Nothing here has yet confirmed that channel 1 slewing
does not disturb channel 2." It is now confirmed in two halves, one automated
and one a standalone deck, plus a residue that SPICE structurally cannot answer.

WHAT DID NOT EXIST BEFORE THIS. There was no SPICE test on the dual, and there
could not have been one, for four measured reasons:
  1. `lob run` on the dual died at `SimConfig::infer`: "simulation needs a net
     named 'IN' (have: ... SIG_IN1, SIG_IN2 ...)". The harness assumed exactly
     one input and one output net; a dual has two of each by definition.
  2. `lob run` on the MONO board also failed, at the deck generator: "no SPICE
     model or primitive mapping for: SW1, U2". The RANGE switch had no handling
     and the builtin model catalogue knew TL072/TL082/NE5532 but not TL074 —
     and the mono board moved to a TL074 when the CV attenuverter needed two
     more sections. So neither board had a working simulate stage.
  3. The builtin LM13700 model was CHANNEL A ONLY — 8 of 16 pins
     (1,3,4,5,6,7,8,11). A dual cannot be expressed in it at all.
  4. Any pin left open failed the whole deck, so a whole-package model would
     have broken the mono board, which leaves OTA B unconnected.

ALL FOUR ARE FIXED (see the sibling bead for the code). `lob run` now completes
8 stages on the dual and 7 on the mono.

HALF 1 — NETLIST LEVEL, NOW AN AUTOMATED GATE. New self-selecting check
`verify::check_channel_crosstalk`, wired into `lob run` as a crosstalk stage that
skips single-channel boards entirely. It drives channel 1 with a step SEQUENCE,
holds every other channel's input at 0 V, and probes both outputs.

  measured on the real dual netlist:
    drove SIG_IN1 -> SIG_OUT1 swung 4.000 Vpp
    undriven SIG_OUT2 moved 0.000000 Vpp   (0.000e0, -inf dB, limit 1e-3)

  and the gate BITES — proven by mutation, not by assertion. A copy of the dual
  with ONE net object shared between the channels (the realistic bug: a net that
  did not get its per-channel suffix) fails:
    drove SIG_IN1 -> SIG_OUT1 swung 2.000 Vpp   (halved: two buffers fighting)
    undriven SIG_OUT2 moved 1.999960 Vpp  -> 1.000e0 (0.0 dB)  FAIL
    pipeline failed (2 of 8 stages)
  The check also refuses to pass vacuously: if the aggressor did not swing at
  least 0.1 V it fails rather than reporting perfect isolation.

  WHAT THIS HALF PROVES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. A netlist has ideal supplies and a
  zero-impedance ground, so the only coupling expressible in it is a SHARED
  NODE. That is exactly the failure mode of a channel instantiated twice, which
  is why it is worth gating on every build — and it is the whole of what it
  covers.

HALF 2 — BOARD LEVEL, standalone deck (see sibling bead for the file). Real
series resistance on the shared rails, a real shared ground return under both
integrating caps, and the LM13700 behavioural model copied verbatim from
crates/core/src/spice/lob_builtin.lib so both halves measure the same part.
Pin numbers from the KiCad Amplifier_Operational:LM13700 symbol, never memory.

  1. ISOLATION. Channel A at full rate (Vctrl +12 V, 470 nF SNAP) driven with a
     +/-5 V square while B holds 0 V. B's leakage is LINEAR in the shared
     ground-return resistance and vanishes without it:
        0 ohm     -> 7.4e-17 Vpp   (numerically zero: proves the mechanism)
        0.02 ohm  -> 1.49  uVpp    (~ -136 dB below the 10 Vpp aggressor)
        0.2  ohm  -> 15.3  uVpp
        2    ohm  -> 165   uVpp
        20   ohm  -> 1.41  mVpp
     ~74 uV of leakage per ohm of shared return. So channel isolation is a
     LAYOUT number on this board, not a topology property.

  2. ASYMMETRIC RANGES — the case two copies of the mono deck would never test.
     Fast aggressor against a victim in DRIFT (5.17 uF) at the slow end of RATE,
     where its own restoring current is ~1 uA and injected charge matters most:
        1.93 uVpp at 0.02 ohm — 1.3x the symmetric case, still ~ -134 dB.

  3. RATE INDEPENDENCE — the mechanism closest to sharing a die, because
     IABC = (Vctrl - V_BIAS)/R3 and V_BIAS = 2*VBE + V-, so BOTH channels take
     their bias reference from the SAME V- pin. B's own slew rate, A idle vs A
     slewing, swept over rail resistance:
        0.1 ohm/rail -> 78.4504 -> 78.4522 V/s   shift 0.0023 %
        1   ohm/rail -> 78.4487 -> 78.4508 V/s   shift 0.0026 %
        10  ohm/rail -> 78.4315 -> 78.4370 V/s   shift 0.0070 %
        100 ohm/rail -> 78.2607 -> 78.2970 V/s   shift 0.046  %
     Even at an absurd 100 ohm/rail the other channel retunes this one by well
     under a tenth of a percent.

  4. DECOUPLING IS NOT THE LEVER, and this is the most actionable result
     because decoupling is the thing that can be changed on a built board.
     Rails and ground deliberately bad (10 ohm/rail, 2 ohm shared return),
     decoupling swept over SEVEN orders of magnitude:
        1p -> 147 uVpp leak, V- moved 2.70 mVpp
        1n -> 149 uVpp,      2.70 mVpp
        10n-> 160 uVpp,      2.76 mVpp
        100n->149 uVpp,      2.70 mVpp
        1u -> 137 uVpp,      2.70 mVpp
        10u-> 99  uVpp,      2.68 mVpp
     A 10,000,000x change in decoupling buys 33 % less leakage and does not move
     the V- rail excursion at all. The reason is structural: the bypass caps sit
     between each rail and the LOCAL ground node, so they do nothing about the
     resistance between that node and the star point — which is where the
     coupling actually happens. Do not spend BOM or area on bigger bypass caps
     expecting channel isolation; separate the returns instead.

  5. BOTH CHANNELS SLEWING AT ONCE. The brief asked for antiphase as the worst
     case for supply current. MEASURED, IT IS THE BEST CASE, and that matters
     for whoever designs the bench test. The OTA's output current follows the
     slew DIRECTION, so two channels slewing opposite ways draw opposite
     currents through the shared pins and cancel; slewing TOGETHER adds:
        B alone (A quiet)      : B rate 78.4526 V/s, V- moved 3e-5 Vpp
        both, ANTIPHASE        : B rate 78.4526 V/s, V- moved 0    Vpp  (cancels)
        both, IN PHASE         : B rate 78.4528 V/s, V- moved 5e-5 Vpp  (adds)
     B's rate changed by 1.1e-6 % antiphase and 2.0e-4 % in phase. Design the
     bench test around SIMULTANEOUS SAME-DIRECTION slewing, not opposite.

BOTTOM LINE. Board-level channel interaction is negligible — four to five orders
of magnitude below anything audible — and what little exists is a pure function
of shared ground-return resistance, i.e. a layout variable the placer/router
controls. This is not a clean bill of health for the module; it is a clean bill
of health for the part of the question SPICE can see.

WHAT SPICE STRUCTURALLY CANNOT TELL US, and therefore what the bench MUST cover
(filed as its own bead):
  * DIE / SUBSTRATE / THERMAL COUPLING. The model is a datasheet behavioural OTA
    (Iout = IABC*tanh(Vd/2Vt)) with no thermal node and no substrate term. Two
    OTAs on one die that heat each other cannot appear in it at any parameter
    setting. This matters more than it looks: V_BIAS = 2*VBE + V- has a ~-4
    mV/degC tempco, and at the slow end of RATE the whole IABC is ~1 uA, so a
    few degrees of die heating from the busy channel is a percent-level rate
    error on the quiet one. That is the single most plausible real crosstalk
    path on this board and SPICE cannot see it.
  * The behavioural OTA draws its output current from V- for BOTH polarities;
    the real part sources from V+ when sourcing. Magnitudes are right, the split
    between rails is not, so rail-specific conclusions are weaker than the
    aggregate ones.
  * The Darlington buffer is modelled as an ideal follower and draws no rail
    current at all, so the buffers contribute nothing to the measured coupling
    while on the real part they are the largest rail current in the package.

title: [epic] Dual slew limiter — the variant that keeps being asked for and keeps not existing
description:
FILED 2026-07-28 because the user has asked for this repeatedly ("for the 10th TIME") and there was no bead for it. That is the actual bug: a product decision that keeps being requested and keeps evaporating between sessions.

WHAT THE RECORD SAYS, and it contradicts the request. [[legion-of-bom-tus.11]], dated 2026-07-24, locks the positioning as "precise compact VC portamento — does one thing perfectly" and lists what was CUT deliberately: "separate rise/fall, EOC, DUAL, oscillate (that's the function-generator positioning we did NOT pick)".

So either that decision has been reversed and never written down, or the dual is a SECOND product rather than a change to the first. Those are different things and the difference matters:
  - Reversing tus.11 changes the single's positioning and its 4-6 HP target.
  - A separate dual leaves the single alone and adds a wider sibling.
The second reading fits better with what is already recorded — [[legion-of-bom-qng]] notes "a dual at ~10-12 HP may land in the width where this actually routes" — and with the fact that the user still wants 4 HP for the single ([[legion-of-bom-tsy.10]] / the 4 HP bead).

WHAT IS ALREADY KNOWN, so this is not starting cold:
  - The single is DRC-clean and fab-ready at 6 HP as of 2026-07-28, deterministic. Two of them is a known-good starting point rather than a new circuit.
  - The circuit is one LM13700 OTA (2 OTAs per package, only one used) + TL072. A dual can likely share the LM13700 rather than doubling it — that is a real BOM saving and the reason a dual is attractive, and it needs checking against the topology in circuits/slew_limiter/slew-limiter-circuit.md.
  - Panel: 2x (RATE, CV AMT, RANGE, IN, OUT, CV IN) = 12 controls. At 14mm pot pitch that is two columns; 10-12 HP is the plausible width.
  - At 4 HP the single occupies 44.6% of one side. Two channels in 8-10 HP is not obviously area-limited.

BLOCKED ON A DECISION, not on engineering: confirm whether the dual replaces or accompanies the single, and at what HP. Everything after that is a known path.

DO NOT let this evaporate again — that is what this bead is for.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
DECIDED (user, 2026-07-28): the dual IS the product. Recorded in the [[dual-slew-limiter-is-the-product]] memory so it stops evaporating — the reason it kept getting lost is that every WRITTEN trace said the opposite and nobody had filed this.

THE RANGE SWITCH IS THE LEVER FOR BOTH THIS AND 4 HP, and that was already in the tree unread. [[legion-of-bom-tus.12]]:
  - the switch's premise 'has largely dissolved' — summing RATE and CV as voltages into TL074-D with ONE V->I conversion took the range 3.0:1 -> 35.2:1, giving 22ms..783ms from a single knob, which is exactly the portamento range this product is positioned for
  - 'C5 is 14mm wide and is what pushed the board past 4 HP'
  - dropping it removes SW1, C4, C5, one panel cutout and probably a whole HP

So the single-at-4HP ask and the dual ask are the SAME simplification:
  single, no RANGE: 5 controls, widest part no longer a 14mm film cap  -> 4 HP
  dual,   no RANGE: 10 controls (2 x RATE/CV AMT/IN/OUT/CV IN), 2 columns -> ~8 HP

ORDER OF WORK, once the switch call is confirmed:
  1. Drop SW1/C4/C5 from circuits/slew_limiter/slew_limiter.py; re-run the SPICE verify to confirm 35:1 holds at the chosen C1.
  2. Re-measure the single: it should now fit 4 HP, which also tests the P0 claim that the placer rather than geometry was refusing.
  3. Duplicate the channel. The LM13700 carries TWO OTAs and the single uses one, so a dual likely shares the package rather than doubling it — real BOM saving, and the reason a dual is attractive. Check against circuits/slew_limiter/slew-limiter-circuit.md.
  4. Panel: two columns of five.

The single is DRC-clean, deterministic and fab-ready at 6 HP as of today, so this starts from a known-good board rather than a new circuit.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
SIZED, from the actual circuit (2026-07-28). User's calls: keep the RANGE switch (it adds features), THT is fine provided the build guide is clear, dual using the whole OTA package, dense packing.

WHAT IS SHARED vs WHAT DOUBLES — read out of circuits/slew_limiter/slew_limiter.py, not assumed:

  U1  LM13700  SHARED. The notes say 'Mono, confirmed — OTA A only, OTA B left unpopulated'. A dual uses both OTAs, so ONE package serves both channels. That is a real saving of the expensive, stock-constrained part (the notes flag LM13700 availability as the first board where JLCPCB stock reality matters).
  U2  TL074    DOUBLES. All four sections are already used by ONE channel: A input buffer, B output buffer, C the unity inverter making -CV for the pot's bottom end, D the RATE+CV voltage summing stage. Eight sections for a dual = 2x TL074. No waste either way.
  J3  power    shared. C2/C3 supply decoupling shared.
  Everything else x2, including the RANGE switch and its caps: 2x SW1, 2x C1 (base integrating), 2x C4, 2x C5.

So dual BOM = 1x LM13700 + 2x TL074, against 2x LM13700 + 2x TL074 for two singles. Exactly the saving the user asked for.

AREA, keep-out sums against board area:
  single 1525 mm2   dual 2834 mm2
   8 HP (40.6mm): 27.1% of two-sided area
  10 HP (50.8mm): 21.7%
  12 HP (61.0mm): 18.1%
For comparison the single at 4 HP is 29.2%. So A DUAL AT 8 HP IS SLIGHTLY LESS DENSE THAN THE SINGLE AT 4 HP — the user's 'I know we can densely pack them' is right, and both asks depend on the same thing: the placer, which currently refuses 4 HP at 44.6% single-side occupancy.

PANEL: 12 controls, two columns of six. 2x14mm pot + 2mm gap + 2x1mm edge = 32.0mm = 6.30 HP, so 7 HP is the geometric floor and 8 HP is comfortable. Six controls per column at ~14mm pitch is 84mm of the 128.5mm height — room to spare vertically, which is where the C5 14mm film caps can go.

ALSO FOUND: slew-limiter-circuit.md already says 'Dual deferred to a v1.1 revision once mono [works]'. Mono is now DRC-clean and fab-ready, so v1.1 is due.

BLOCKED ON the same P0 as 4 HP: the placer. Nothing here needs a wider board, it needs a packer that uses the board it is given.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
CHANNEL INDEPENDENCE ANSWERED, 2026-07-28 — the question the dual's docstring
flagged as the one dual-specific unknown. Three child beads:

  [[legion-of-bom-9wh.1]] — the measurements. Netlist-level gate (now automated
    in `lob run`, 0.000000 Vpp leaked against 4.000 Vpp driven, and proven to
    bite by mutation) plus a standalone board-level deck. Headline: channel
    isolation on this board is ~ -136 dB and is a PURE FUNCTION OF SHARED
    GROUND-RETURN RESISTANCE (linear, ~74 uV/ohm, exactly zero at 0 ohm). It is
    a layout variable, not a topology risk. Decoupling is NOT the lever — swept
    over seven orders of magnitude it buys 33 % and does not move the V- rail
    excursion at all.
  [[legion-of-bom-9wh.2]] — the machinery it took. Before today NEITHER board
    could be simulated: the builtin LM13700 model was channel-A-only (8 of 16
    pins), TL074 was not in the catalogue at all, any open pin failed the whole
    deck, switches had no handling, and the harness assumed exactly one input
    and one output net so a dual could not even be addressed.
  [[legion-of-bom-9wh.3]] — what SPICE structurally CANNOT answer, kept open on
    purpose: die/substrate/thermal coupling. The behavioural OTA has no thermal
    node, and V_BIAS = 2*VBE + V- has a ~-4 mV/degC tempco against a ~1 uA IABC
    at the slow end of RATE — so die heating from the busy channel is the most
    plausible real crosstalk path and the one we have no bound on. DO NOT read
    the simulation result as a clean bill of health for the module.

ONE FINDING THAT CHANGES A DESIGN ASSUMPTION: antiphase slewing is the BEST case
for the shared rails, not the worst. The OTA's output current follows the slew
direction, so opposite-direction slewing cancels in the shared pins (V- moved
0 Vpp) while same-direction slewing adds (5e-5 Vpp). Any bench test built around
antiphase would be testing the easy case.

Also confirmed against the built netlist, not from the docstring: 46 parts,
1x LM13700 with both halves wired, 2x TL074, and the crosstalk gate's own
measurement is independent evidence that no net bridges the two channels.

title: lob panel derive --hp N silently overrides N instead of honouring or refusing it
description:
`lob panel derive circuits/slew_limiter/slew_limiter.py --hp 4` prints:

    widened to 6 HP — 4 HP can't fit the control hardware
    derived panel: .../slew_limiter_panel.toml (6 control(s), 6 HP)

and writes a 6 HP spec. The flag's own help says "Panel width in HP", with omitting it as the way to get automatic sizing. Passing it explicitly should either be honoured or REFUSED with a non-zero exit — quietly substituting a different number is how a user ends up believing 4 HP was tried and failed when it was never attempted.

SECOND PROBLEM, same command: it wrote to circuits/slew_limiter/slew_limiter_panel.toml — the tracked, hand-authored spec — without warning or confirmation. [[legion-of-bom-byh]] is the bead about a command destroying hand-authored panel work (comments, a deliberate layout, a chosen HP), and effective_panel was carefully changed to never write to a declared spec for exactly that reason. `panel derive` still does. It should default to a new path, or require --force to overwrite a file that already exists.

Recovered here with git checkout because the spec happened to be committed minutes earlier.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
FIXED 2026-08-12, both halves.

--hp N IS NOW HONOURED. Root cause was worse than the bead recorded: panel_from_board
takes its hp FROM THE BOARD OUTLINE, so with a built board present the requested width
was not overridden by a fitting check — it was discarded before any check ran, and the
'widened to 6 HP — 4 HP can't fit the control hardware' line was the 6 HP board
asserting its own width. Nothing tried 4 HP. Now an explicit --hp that differs from the
built board sets the board aside and lays out from scratch, saying why: 'built board is
6 HP but you asked for 4 — laying out from scratch; positions from a board of another
width prove nothing here'. Measured: derive --hp 4 emits a real 4 HP column at x=10.2,
and the no --hp path still reads the board (the board is master, unchanged).
Also suppressed the follow-on 'no built board at <path>' line, which was untrue when a
board existed and had just been deliberately ignored.

IT NO LONGER WRITES OVER A TRACKED SPEC. New --force flag; without it the command
refuses any existing output path and names two ways forward (--out elsewhere and diff,
or --force). This mattered immediately: the slew_limiter panel was hand-authored minutes
before with comments and a deliberate jack order, and the DEFAULT output path is exactly
that file. Verified — 'lob panel derive circuits/slew_limiter/slew_limiter.py' now exits
non-zero with the file byte-intact.

Same session as [[legion-of-bom-unc]], which made the matching refusal on the build side
(a declared panel that does not fit the PCB now stops the build instead of being replaced
by a derived substitute). Gates: 422 core + 21 web + 3 cli, clippy -D warnings clean,
fmt clean.

title: Fab BOM hands JLC through-hole parts it will not assemble (C4, C5) with empty LCSC numbers
description:
out/slew_limiter/fab/slew_limiter-bom.csv, the file uploaded for ASSEMBLY, contains:

  Comment,Designator,Footprint,LCSC Part #
  1uF,C4,C_Rect_L7.0mm_W2.5mm_P5.00mm,
  4.7uF,C5,C_Rect_L13.0mm_W5.0mm_P10.00mm_FKS3_FKP3_MKS4,

Both are through-hole (Capacitor_THT footprints, 2 thru_hole pads each; build_facts correctly reports tht=2 for both). The confirmed assembly model is [[assembly-model-fab-does-smd-we-do-tht]] — the fab house reflows surface-mount, through-hole is ours. So these lines are asking JLC to place parts it will not place, and they carry no LCSC number, so they cannot be sourced from that BOM either.

This is the mirror of [[legion-of-bom-095]] (V-BOM lists SMD parts JLCPCB already soldered). Same root: neither BOM is kit-aware. On a mixed kit the fab BOM should contain SMT only, and the hand-solder list should contain THT only, and the split is already derivable — PartFacts::tht_pads is populated and correct.

Noticed by the user, who also observed these do not appear as through-hole in the build guide. Worth checking the guide's kit classification in the same pass, since it reads the same data.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
FIXED and VERIFIED 2026-08-12. The stated defect is gone: out/slew_limiter/fab/slew_limiter-bom.csv no longer contains C4 or C5, or any other through-hole part. The gate now reports 'hand-soldered (9, withheld from the assembly BOM): C4 C5 J1 J2 J3 J4 RV1 RV2 SW1' and the file is 8 SMD lines.

Implemented as fab::jlc_bom_csv(bom, hand_soldered: &HashSet<String>), with the set derived
from guide::parse_board's through_hole flag in cli/main.rs — so the split comes from the
same pad geometry the build guide reads, not a second classifier. Mixed lines are kept with
only their placed designators rather than dropped whole.

The bead's parenthetical about empty LCSC numbers is NOT fixed and is now
[[legion-of-bom-g5a]] — all 8 remaining SMD lines still have a blank LCSC Part #, and the
CPL still lists all 23 placements including the 9 withheld ones, so the two files in the
package contradict each other. Splitting that out rather than leaving this bead open for a
different defect than its title.

title: legalize does not repair the edge violations it exists for — U1 left 9.0mm over the edge
description:
legalize.rs states its own contract: "This pass takes the placement as given and repairs it directly. It only touches Tier::Physical violations: a part hanging over the board edge is a board that cannot be built, and moving it is not a trade-off."

On the slew limiter 2026-07-28 it left exactly that, unrepaired:
    [physical]  -9.0mm  U1 hangs 9.0mm past the board's 1.5mm edge clearance
    [physical]  -3.0mm  C2 hangs 3.0mm past the board's 1.5mm edge clearance

The EdgeClearance rule fires with a repair vector, so legalize has everything it needs. Candidate causes, in order of suspicion:
  1. legalize runs but cannot find a legal destination and gives up silently. MAX_PASSES is 4 and the module says "a part that cannot be legalized in a few passes needs a bigger board, not more iterations" — but this board has a 5.96mm unused strip down its right-hand side, so there IS somewhere to put it.
  2. It runs before something that moves the part back (the snap passes ran before it; summing::snap has since been removed).
  3. The outline it is given is not the outline the board is written with — consistent with the ~6.5mm left shift, where parts occupy x 126.76..157.78 against an outline of 133.26..163.74.

(3) is the one I would test first: instrument the outline legalize receives against the Edge.Cuts finally emitted. If they differ, that single displacement explains the part off the left edge, the dead strip on the right, and why legalize thought it had nothing to fix.

Whatever the cause, it must also SAY it failed. Giving up silently on a Tier::Physical violation is how this reached a fab package.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
RELATED FINDING, 2026-07-28, from the 4 HP work ([[legion-of-bom-unc]]). Not
the same bug as the U1/C2 edge overhang this bead is about, but the same area
and it was refusing a fab package outright:

1. THE POWER HEADER WAS PLACED 3.58mm OFF THE LEFT EDGE AT EVERY WIDTH.
   SeededPlacer's header lane laid J3 out by its footprint ORIGIN as if that
   were its keep-out centre. A 2x5 header's origin is pin 1, 5.08mm from the
   middle of its body, so J3's keep-out ran x -3.58..10.28 on a board starting
   at x 0. Fixed by placing on the keep-out centre and converting back to an
   origin, the way the anchored and free paths already do. Same correction
   applied to EurorackPlacer. Test:
   board::tests::a_power_header_lands_inside_the_board_despite_its_off_centre_origin

2. …and once it lands correctly, it lands EXACTLY on the line, because
   board::EDGE_MARGIN_MM and rules::EDGE_CLEARANCE_MM are both 1.5mm. The
   placer reaches that coordinate as sheet_origin + (lane_x - keepout_offset)
   and the rule reaches the limit as sheet_origin + min + half_extent — the
   same number by different summation orders, 2.8e-14mm apart in binary
   floating point. Half the widths land on the wrong side of it. Measured on
   the real board:
     lob fab slew_limiter --panel <derived 8 HP>
       BEFORE: error: board breaks 1 physical rule(s) KiCad DRC does not check
               ✗ [physical] J3 hangs 0.0mm past the board's 1.5mm edge clearance
       AFTER:  DRC: 0 error(s), 10 warning(s) — fab package written
   Fixed with rules::TOLERANCE_MM = 1e-6 in Assessment::ok (KiCad's own board
   unit is 1nm). Test:
   rules::tests::a_part_exactly_on_the_edge_clearance_line_is_not_a_violation —
   and it drives the real SeededPlacer rather than hand-written coordinates,
   because a fixture that guesses where the header lands cannot reproduce the
   arithmetic that IS the bug.

Note "hangs 0.0mm" as a symptom: a Tier::Physical rejection reported at 0.0mm
is arithmetic, not a board. Worth remembering next time one shows up.

title: phono_preamp blocked before placement: RCA jack footprint is a literal TODO placeholder
description:
Found while baselining the fast-follow board 2026-07-28, straight after the slew limiter went fab-ready.

  lob fab phono_preamp
  error: footprint 'Connector_Audio:RCA_Jack_FIRST_USE_TODO' not found

It fails before placement even runs, so nothing is known yet about whether this board places or routes. The name is a deliberate placeholder in the circuit — FIRST_USE_TODO — so this is a circuit-authoring gap, not a layout one.

NEEDED: pick a real RCA jack, add its footprint to puget-hardware/.lob/parts/footprints, and record the part in the Dolt parts library with its citation per the [[legion-of-bom-okm]] gate. Mechanical envelope matters as much as the footprint here — an RCA jack is panel hardware, so BuiltinCutouts needs a cutout spec for it or the derived panel will not know how much room it takes (compare [[legion-of-bom-tvs]], where a toggle's cutout was 6.5mm against a real 4.95mm).

THEN re-baseline: lob fab phono_preamp, plus route_bench for the impossible-by-placement count, so we learn whether the placement work that unblocked the slew limiter carries over to a second board. That is the real question this board answers — the slew limiter is now n=1.

title: rules::derive is profile-blind — thread LayoutMode through Context so a rule declares which boards it is true of
description:
FOUNDATION for the rest of the epic — the other children all want to add rules that are only true for some boards.

TODAY: LayoutMode { Analog, Digital, Mixed } is parsed from lob fab --mode, reaches LayoutLoop, and produces CostWeights and nothing else. rules.rs has ZERO references to it. So every rule is derived for every board, and the only way to express "this matters on digital boards" is to not write the rule.

WANTED:
  1. LayoutMode (or a richer Profile, if the sketch in the epic argues for one) on rules::Context, which derive_in already takes.
  2. derive_in emits the rules that apply to that profile, and no others.
  3. Each Rule variant states which profiles it belongs to, next to its "why" — a reader should be able to see that a rule is analog-only without inferring it.
  4. The profile-INDEPENDENT set (edge clearance, courtyard/overlap, drill-to-edge — IPC-2221 territory) stays unconditional. Splitting these correctly is most of the design work, and getting it wrong is worse than not splitting: a manufacturing rule silently scoped to one profile is a board that cannot be built.

CHECK BEFORE BUILDING: does the profile belong on Context, or on the Rule (each rule declares its profiles, derive filters)? The latter keeps the knowledge with the rule, matching the standing pattern that a component's data travels with the component. Worth ten minutes of argument before writing code.

ALSO: the default is LayoutMode::Analog and every board we ship today is analog, so this change should be a NO-OP on the slew limiter. That is the test — profile plumbing that changes the current board's rule set has got the split wrong.

title: Panel Separation is unenforceable when both parts are anchored — it must feed panel DERIVATION, not just the score
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-28 on the real slew limiter: RV2 and SW1 keep-outs overlap by 7.23 x 5.51mm. Both are panel hardware anchored to their cutouts, so:

  - the placer cannot move them (pinned)
  - legalize cannot move them (pinned)
