title: panel: auto-layout is single-column, degenerates on many-control boards
description:
From puget-hardware/lob-gaps.md B2 (high).

Placement is a single centred column, so an 8-control board becomes absurdly wide and pushes parts off the panel. Repro:

  $ lob panel fit crossfader.py
  minimum panel width: 42 HP

and the auto panel puts J7 (CV IN) at y_mm = -12.1, off a 3U panel entirely -- after which the board fails to route (10 unconnected) and trips edge clearance.

ASK: multi-column / HP-aware placement, and clamp cutouts to panel bounds so a derived spec can never place hardware off the panel.

RELATED: the 1U tile work added a row layout (derive_panel_for, PanelFormat::is_tile) and a sum-of-widths sizing rule. The 3U case wants the general version of the same idea -- pack into N columns to fit a target width, rather than one column at any width. The panel-hardware Separation rule ([[legion-of-bom-za4]]) already exists to catch overlap once a packer starts placing things near each other.
notes: The panel-hardware Separation rule referenced above landed in [[legion-of-bom-za4]]; the 1U row layout is in derive_panel_for / PanelFormat::is_tile.
close_reason: derive_panel_for now picks a column count from the width available and the height required, splits by height rather than count, and clamps every cutout inside the panel. Sparse modules keep a single centred column. Tests cover both the crowded case (10 controls, multiple columns, nothing off-panel) and the sparse one. Slew limiter: single column at 4 and 6 HP, two columns at 8.

title: sim: no committed per-circuit sim spec
description:
From puget-hardware/lob-gaps.md A3 (high).

lob run sim requires a net literally named IN and probes by convention. There is no way to declare input/probe nets, drive waveform, or analysis type. Repro:

  $ lob run phono_preamp.py
  error: simulate stage failed: simulation needs a net named IN
         (have: +12V, -12V, A_N_L, ... PHONO_L, PHONO_R, OUT_L, OUT_R)

The richer scope sim (input_net/probe_net/drive/cv) exists but only interactively via lob serve -- nothing repeatable or committed.

ASK: a [circuit.sim] manifest table, repeatable (N allowed): analysis (ac|dc|tran), input/probe nets, drive (pwl|step|ac|dc-sweep), control-net values, and mode/switch positions.

This is the keystone of section A -- A1, A2 and A4 all become expressible once a sim can be declared.

title: sim: no switch model, so mode switches cannot be represented
description:
From puget-hardware/lob-gaps.md A2 (high). BLOCKS the phono line/phono mode feature.

lob_builtin.lib has OPAMP_IDEAL, TL072, LM13700 -- no switch. And a static netlist cannot flip a SW_DPDT_x2, so a mode switch cannot be expressed at all. Repro: phono_preamp SW1; both modes had to be simulated as two parallel paths in a hand deck.

ASK: (a) a behavioural switch model, and (b) a way to declare switch/mode positions so lob emits one deck per mode, or a parameterised deck.

title: sim: no AC analysis in the generated deck
description:
From puget-hardware/lob-gaps.md A1 (high).

The generated sim is transient only. An RIAA accuracy spec is a frequency-response claim (<0.2 dB, 20Hz-20kHz) and needs .ac. phono_preamp_riaa.cir exists as a hand deck purely because lob cannot emit an AC sweep.

ASK: support .ac (dec/oct sweep) as an analysis type in the generated deck.

Part of the single-source goal: every hand deck in that repo duplicates lobs models and mirrors the topology by hand, which is the drift risk the generated deck exists to remove.

title: verify 1U mounting-hole inset against the Intellijel drawing
description:
PanelFormat::hole_inset_y_mm reuses the 3U inset (3.0mm from top and bottom edges) for both 1U formats. The PANEL HEIGHTS are verified from published sources -- Intellijel 39.65mm, Pulp Logic 1.700in = 43.18mm -- but the hole positions are NOT.

Intellijel publish 1U hole spacing as a diagram image on
https://intellijel.com/support/1u-technical-specifications/
and their text says only that "the 1U panel size is based on the 3U size scaled down to fit in a 1U row" and defers to the Doepfer mechanical spec. WebFetch could not read numbers out of the diagram.

So 3.0mm is a derivation, not a citation. On a 39.65mm tile a wrong inset means the tile does not bolt into the rails -- the one failure that makes a panel scrap.

FIX: read the figure off the Intellijel drawing (or measure a known-good tile) and correct the constant. It is deliberately one function, PanelFormat::hole_inset_y_mm, so this is a one-line change with a test.

Note also the x inset is shared with 3U at 7.5mm and has the same status.

title: CV AMT: make it a real attenuverter (needs an op-amp section that does not exist)
description:
User chose to make RV2 a true attenuverter so the bipolar panel art is honest. The option was offered as "an unused op-amp section, or a resistor flip". Neither exists -- checked.

TL072 U2 is fully used: section A (pins 1/2/3) is the input buffer, section B (5/6/7) is the output buffer. LM13700 U1 has OTA-B and buffer-B free, but an OTA is a transconductance stage and its Darlington buffer is a follower -- neither inverts usefully.

The standard one-op-amp attenuverter is: pot top = CV, bottom = GND, wiper -> non-inverting input; CV also into the inverting input via R with R feedback. Output = 2*wiper - CV, which sweeps -CV (wiper at 0) to +CV (wiper at CV). One section, two resistors. So the cost is exactly one op-amp section.

OPTIONS:
  A. TL072 -> TL074 quad. No new BOM line, one part swapped, two sections spare. Cost: SOIC-8 -> SOIC-14, more board, re-place and re-route.
  B. Add a TL071/TL061 single as U3. +1 BOM line, small package, U2 untouched.
  C. Leave it an attenuator. Zero cost; the panel already says so honestly.

NOTE the panel does NOT need a decision to be correct: crate::panel::cutout_role derives bipolar-vs-not from topology, so CV AMT renders as a plain knob today and flips to attenuverter art by itself once the track end moves off ground. There is a test for that.

ALSO: an attenuverter here means CV can SUBTRACT from the RATE knobs bias current. Worth confirming that is the musical intent -- IABC cannot go negative, so negative CV just closes the OTA.
close_reason:
Done. User chose the TL074 quad swap.

TL074 was the right pick for a reason I did not anticipate: sections A and B keep the TL072s pin numbers exactly (1/2/3 and 5/6/7), so the input and output buffers did not move at all. Only the rails shift, V+ 8->4 and V- 4->11.

TOPOLOGY. Used the two spare sections rather than the textbook one-op-amp attenuverter, deliberately. The one-op-amp version (pot top=CV, bottom=GND, wiper->+in, CV->R->-in, R feedback; Vout = 2W - CV) keeps the pots bottom on GROUND, which means panel::cutout_role would still read it as a plain knob -- correct by its own rule and wrong about the circuit. Instead:
  C = unity inverter (R6/R7 100k) making CV_INV
  RV2 track spans CV_IN .. CV_INV, so its centre is a true zero
  D = unity buffer on the wiper, so CV depth stays linear into R5
Both track ends are now live signal nets, so the attenuverter art derives itself with no override. Verified: RV2 comes out as role=attenuverter, renders with the large centre dot and -/+ at the extremes, RATE stays a plain knob.

ALSO: renamed the wiper net to CV_AMT and the buffered output to CV_SUM. Before the rename RV2 labelled itself "CV IN" -- the same as the jack -- because control_label takes the alphabetically-first signal net and CV_AMT had moved to the buffer output. The new naming is also just truer: the knob sets the amount.

VERIFIED: ERC 0 errors, minimum buildable width 4 HP DRC-clean (was 5), decoupling still 4.5mm pad-to-power-pin on both caps after U2s power pins moved.

Files changed in puget-hardware: slew_limiter.py (+75/-20), slew_limiter.net regenerated. NOT committed -- that repo is the users to commit.

BOM impact: TL072 -> TL074 (SOIC-8 -> SOIC-14), plus R6/R7 100k 0603. Board needs a re-place/route at the new width.

title: decoupling measured part centres, not the power pin
description:
User: bypass caps are not close to the power pins like they should be. Correct, and worse than it looked.

The rule measured centre-to-centre between cap and IC. What sets a bypass caps effectiveness is the inductance of the loop from its pads to the chips power PIN and back through ground, and inductance goes with loop area. On a 16-pin package the power pin is at the end, so a cap could sit 8.7mm from an LM13700s middle, pass the rule, and still be 10mm of copper from pin 11 -- or on the far side of the chip with the loop wrapped around it.

Measured cap pad to IC power pin on puget slew_limiter:
  shipped board  C2 94.19mm  C3 58.58mm   (128mm board, caps at the opposite end from the chips)
  before         C2 10.00mm  C3  4.92mm
  after          C2  4.54mm  C3  3.54mm

FIX: new crate::decouple::snap pass, run before legalization. Placer pull seeds roughly, this sets exactly. Deliberately NOT a stronger attractor: a pull is a suggestion competing with every other nets, and there is one right place for a bypass cap with nothing else bidding for it. PartFacts gains pin_offsets (footprint_pads already read pad positions and we discarded them). Board stays DRC-clean.

STILL A PROXY: crate::rules Proximity continues to score centre-to-centre. It now passes comfortably, which means a future regression could hide behind it. The unit test in decouple.rs is the actual guard. Making the rule measure pad-to-pin is the honest follow-up -- it changes thresholds and the layout loops scoring, so it was not worth destabilising in the same change.
close_reason: Fixed by crate::decouple::snap. Worst cap-pad-to-power-pin on slew_limiter: 10.00mm -> 4.54mm, board still DRC-clean, 337 tests pass. Follow-up (rule still scores the proxy) tracked on [[legion-of-bom-5kv]].

title: back-side footprint flip mirrored the wrong axis
description:
Reported: the back-side power header 3D body was drawn offset from its pads, running off the board edge.

flip_to_back mirrored local X. KiCad mirrors local Y, and negates any angle riding on an (at x y rot). Verified against pcbnew FOOTPRINT::Flip: TQFP-120 pad (-5.8, 7.7, 90) flips to (-5.8, -7.7, 270) -- X held, Y negated, angle reversed.

The two conventions differ by a 180 degree turn, which is why this hid for so long: invisible on every symmetric part (all our SMD passives, the ICs), and only visible on a footprint whose origin is off-centre. KiCad renders the 3D model from ITS convention, so the body landed a footprint-length from our pads.

Fixed all nine sites together, since the router aims at pads via place_point and would otherwise miss: flip_to_back, place_point, keepout_at, keepout_at_rot, tht_pads_at, offset_of, the anchor conversion, GridPlacer target, rules.rs measured_box. Also now negates pad-local angles, which we never did in either convention -- latent for any footprint with rotated pads.

Pinned with a test carrying the pcbnew ground-truth numbers.
close_reason: Fixed and verified: header body now sits over its pads, fully inside the board outline, and the harness still reports DRC 0 errors. 316 core tests pass, clippy clean.

title: facts: PartFacts.tht_pads misses PTH pads that KiCad flags for edge clearance
description:
MEASURED on slew_limiter at 4 HP. KiCad reports copper_edge_clearance for a PTH pad of RV1 at x=119.96 on a board whose right edge is x=120.32 (limit 0.5mm, actual 0.0). rules::EdgeClearance, after being fixed to apply origin_offset AND to take the union of keep-out and tht_pads, still passes that part with +1.5mm clearance — so the pad KiCad flags is not in PartFacts.tht_pads.

Arithmetic: the rule's union box for RV1 spans origin-1.9..origin+12.6. For the rule to report +1.5mm on a 4 HP board the origin must be at ~106.2, putting the flagged pad at +13.7 relative to origin — outside the union. Something in the Alpha pot footprint (mounting lugs, most likely, reported by KiCad as 'PTH pad [<no net>]') is not reaching build_facts.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the last thing standing between minimum_hp and a trustworthy answer. minimum_hp was briefly legalizing before judging, which made it answer 4 HP for slew_limiter — correct if the rules bounded the copper, dangerously optimistic while they do not, and a number somebody could order a panel against. It has been reverted to 5 with a comment pointing here (crates/core/src/board.rs, in minimum_hp). Restore that call once the facts bound the copper.

WHERE TO LOOK: build_facts -> footprint_pads. Check whether it skips pads with no net, pads with no drill, or NPTH/PTH mechanical pads, and compare its output for Potentiometer_Alpha_RD901F against the raw .kicad_mod.

Reproduce: cargo run -p legion-of-bom-core --example board_preview -- out/slew_limiter/slew_limiter.net /tmp/b.kicad_pcb 4, then kicad-cli pcb drc --format json on the result.
notes:
RETITLED IN SPIRIT: this is not (only) a tht_pads gap. Investigating it found and fixed a deeper bug — see commit 95eb731, two rotation senses in the codebase, keep-outs rotated opposite to pads. That is root-caused, fixed and tested.

WHAT REMAINS, with a much cleaner repro than the original. Generate 4 HP:
  cargo run -p legion-of-bom-core --example board_preview -- out/slew_limiter/slew_limiter.net /tmp/f4.kicad_pcb 4

MEASURED on the resulting board (board x 100.0..120.32, J3 origin 114.01,45.89 rot 90):
  J3 pad copper spans x 113.16..125.02
  -> J3's copper extends 4.70mm PAST the right board edge
  our EdgeClearance rule reports: 'J3 clears the board edge by 0.0mm (min 1.5mm)'
  KiCad reports: copper_edge_clearance on J3 pads 5, 6, 7, 8

So the rule's box for J3 is wrong by roughly the width of the part, and legalization therefore never fires. J3 is a plain PinHeader_2x05_P2.54mm_Vertical — no exotic mounting lugs — which makes it a far better test case than the Alpha pot the bead was opened on.

WHERE TO LOOK NEXT, in order:
1. Hand-compute what rules::derive_in stores for J3 (extent, origin_offset after the keep-out ∪ tht_pads union) and what assess() then does with rotation_deg=90, and compare against the measured copper span above. One of those two steps is wrong; the arithmetic above says the rule's box should have been ~5.7mm outside the edge, not +0.0mm inside, so it is likely the derive-time union or the facts feeding it rather than assess.
2. Confirm build_facts sees all ten of J3's pads (the filter is PadLayer::Both; a through-hole pad's layers are '*.Cu' '*.Mask' so it should pass, but verify rather than assume).
3. Only then revisit whether tht_pads is genuinely missing pads.

STILL BLOCKS: minimum_hp legalizing before it judges (crates/core/src/board.rs has the comment and points here). Until the rule bounds the copper, minimum_hp must stay conservative.
close_reason:
RESOLVED, but not as titled — tht_pads was never missing pads. The rule and KiCad disagreed because of TWO coordinate-transform bugs, both now fixed and both pinned by tests.

1. commit 95eb731 — two rotation senses in the codebase. rotate_rect (pads) used KiCad's (x,y)->(y,-x); keepout_at_rot and both anchor-to-origin conversions used the inverse. Self-consistent inside the placer, wrong against the real footprint: a 90-degree-rotated Alpha pot's shaft landed ~11mm from the panel hole it was anchored to. Latent on every shipped board only because none had a rotated control.

2. commit 1056474 — back-side footprints were mirrored in X AFTER rotating instead of before. Harmless at 0/180, wrong otherwise. J3 (back-mounted power header, rot 90) had a rule box at x 102.00..115.86 while its copper sat at 113.16..125.02 — ~10mm out. Flipping in the footprint's own frame first puts the box at 112.16..126.02, containing the copper with exactly the 1.0mm clearance expansion on all four sides.

MEASURED, slew_limiter 4 HP: copper_edge_clearance 5 -> 0.

Both bugs were one test case away from being caught: the old rotation test asserted a pad's +X swinging to -Y and, four lines later, a keep-out's +X swinging to +Y. It now asserts the real invariant — keep-out and pads move together — across both faces and all four rotations.

title: layout: add a legalization stage between global placement and scoring
description:
We have two of the three stages the PCB placement literature describes (global placement -> LEGALIZATION -> fine-tuning; see the ScienceDirect analytical/fine-tuning paper and DAC 2025 constraint-graph legalization in [[legion-of-bom-REFS]]). Ours is greedy global placement plus a blind golden-spiral shake, with no legalization at all.

This is the best explanation for why rule-directed repair failed (see the notes on legion-of-bom-1xm): I was trying to do legalization's job from inside the global stage, by nudging targets and re-running the whole greedy placement. Legalization is a separate pass that takes a placement which may violate physical rules and moves the offending parts the minimum distance to make it legal, without disturbing the global intent.

We already have the inputs: rules::assess gives every Physical violation, and Violation.repair gives the nearest legal position for each. What is missing is the pass that applies them without creating a new overlap.

Verify at 4 HP on slew_limiter — the original t5t report says 4 HP gave 2x copper_edge_clearance, so it is the case with real edge violations to legalize.
close_reason:
Shipped (commit f35644b). crates/core/src/legalize.rs is the middle stage: every part breaking a Physical rule moves the minimum distance to a position that satisfies it and clashes with nothing, spiralling outward from the target so a displaced part settles beside its spot rather than across the board. Only Physical rules — a part over the edge is not a trade-off; moving one to improve decoupling is, and trade-offs belong in the score. A part with no legal position is left put and reported stuck rather than dumped somewhere and called fixed.

Wired into generate_board_artifacts (no-op without a fixed outline, where nothing can be outside by construction) and into minimum_hp, because the build legalizes and asking whether the GLOBAL placement is legal reports a wider board than we would manufacture.

MEASURED, slew_limiter 4 HP, legalization off vs on:
  off: RV1 and RV2 hang 1.0mm past the edge (Physical), score 2001205
  on:  clean, score 1203
  minimum_hp: 5 -> 4

title: panel: derive cutouts and labels from the board's actual placement, not an idealised stack
description:
derive_panel (crates/core/src/panel.rs:680) never reads the board. It stacks every control in a single column at x = panel centre, spaced by class pitch, centred vertically between the title and the logo. So a derived panel matches the board only when the board was itself placed FROM that panel — the current EurorackPlacer flow, where the panel is master and anchors the parts.

That breaks for the case that matters: an existing or imported board, or one whose placement moved. The panel is then idealised fiction and will not fit.

Wanted: derive the panel FROM a built .kicad_pcb. The pieces already exist — guide::parse_board reads placed positions, guide::is_panel_mounted picks out the jacks/pots/switches/LEDs, and EurorackPlacer already defines the board-origin-to-panel mapping (origin_mm plus a Y flip from the panel's bottom-up cutouts to KiCad top-down), so the inverse is available. Needs: read panel-mounted parts and their placed x/y, invert that mapping, emit one CutoutFile each at the real position with the label from the refdes/value, and pick the cutout shape from the footprint (panel::footprint_shape already does something like this).

Open question for the design: which artifact is master. Probably both directions should exist — derive-panel-from-scratch for a new module (today's behaviour) and derive-panel-from-board for anything already placed — with the CLI choosing on whether a board exists.
notes:
Shipped (commit 6a69bea). "lob panel derive" now reads out/<name>/<name>.kicad_pcb when it exists and emits one cutout per panel-mounted part at the position that part actually occupies; --idealised forces the old from-scratch column for a circuit with no board yet. The command prints which of the two it did rather than leaving you to guess.

panel_from_board (commit 2da0ac0) does the mapping: the exact inverse of the placer, framed off the board own Edge.Cuts rather than the KiCad sheet origin so it works on an imported board too, with the board width deciding the HP.

The round trip is now a test — panel::panel_from_board_tests::a_hand_placement_survives_the_trip_through_the_board_and_back. Hand-place a control in panel space via a PlacementFile, let the board follow, derive the panel back from the built board, land within a grid step of what was authored. That is the guarantee the design rests on: the placement file, the board and the panel describe ONE layout and cannot silently drift into three.

DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: effective_panel, which auto-derives during lob board / lob build. There is no board at that moment — it is being made — and feeding the previous board panel back in would make every layout sticky to the last one.
close_reason:
Shipped (commit 6a69bea).  now reads out/<name>/<name>.kicad_pcb when it exists and emits one cutout per panel-mounted part at the position that part actually occupies; --idealised forces the old from-scratch column for a circuit with no board yet. The command prints which of the two it did.

panel_from_board (commit 2da0ac0) does the mapping: the exact inverse of the placer's, framed off the board's own Edge.Cuts rather than the KiCad sheet origin so it works on an imported board too, with the board width deciding the HP.

The round trip is now a test — panel::panel_from_board_tests::a_hand_placement_survives_the_trip_through_the_board_and_back. Hand-place a control in panel space via a PlacementFile, let the board follow, derive the panel back from the built board, land within a grid step of what was authored. That is the guarantee the design rests on: the placement file, the board and the panel describe one layout, and cannot silently drift into three.

DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: effective_panel, which auto-derives during lob board / lob build. There is no board at that moment — it is being made — and feeding the previous board's panel back would make every layout sticky to the last one.

title: build guide + v-BOM read as generic template output, not a kit manual
description: Copper accent on everything, pill chips, uppercase letterspaced eyebrows, warm tinted paper, rounded corners everywhere. Reads as a styled template rather than a DIY synth build doc. Target the register of a Thonk/Music Thing/Befaco manual: black ink on white, one accent reserved for polarity and warnings, ruled boxy tables, tight leading, photos and diagrams carrying the page instead of decoration.
close_reason: Both documents rebuilt as a photocopied kit manual rather than a styled template. Black ink on white; the copper accent, pill chips, tracked-out eyebrows, tinted paper and rounded corners are gone. Red is now reserved for what can destroy the module (polarity, orientation, the highlight box) so its presence carries information. Structure comes from ruled tables and weight. Rationale is written into the theme.rs module doc as three rules so the next change has something to hold to.

title: BOM misses loose hardware: jack nuts, pot nuts + washers
description: A netlist has no line for the hardware that ships with a panel part, so the BOM (and therefore the sorting sheet and the pull-and-sort list) never mentions the M6 nut for each Thonkiconn jack or the nut+washer for each Alpha pot. The builder finds out when the panel will not go on. Derive it from the footprint, include it in the Visual BOM and the guide, and keep it OUT of the fab/JLC BOM — a machine does not place a nut.
close_reason: New crates/core/src/hardware.rs derives loose hardware from the footprint: a jack nut + washer per 3.5mm jack, a nut + washer per pot. Bom::with_hardware() folds them in as LineKind::Hardware lines carrying the refdes they serve; the Visual BOM and the guide's pull-and-sort sheet show them (italic, 'in the bag'), and jlc_bom_csv now iterates bom.components() so the fab never sees a fastener. Deliberately narrow — an unrecognised footprint gets nothing rather than a guessed fastener.

title: board: Eurorack power header should mount on the BACK, with a -12V orientation stripe on the silk
description: Two defects, one symptom. (1) J3 on slew_limiter is placed front (its netlist Side field says front), but a Eurorack power header mounts on the back of the module PCB — so its silkscreen lands on F.SilkS where it is invisible to the person installing it. (2) There is no -12V marker at all, yet guide.rs already tells the builder 'Check the -12 V stripe against the silkscreen: a reversed header is the one mistake that damages the module.' The guide promises a mark the board does not draw. The -12V end is derivable from the netlist rather than hardcoded: on slew_limiter J3 pins 1+2 are on net -12V (pins 9+10 on +12V, 3-6 GND), which is the Doepfer convention. Draw a silk stripe across the pin-1 end plus a -12V label, on whichever side the header mounts.
close_reason: EurorackPlacer now mounts free 2xN power headers on the back (POWER_HEADER_ON_BACK), so refdes + orientation silk land on the face the builder installs from. power_polarity_silk draws a bar across the -12V end plus a mirrored -12V label on that face, with the end read from the netlist (NEG_RAIL_NETS) rather than an assumed pinout — no readable rail, no mark. Offset clears the footprint courtyard (not just the pads) so a shrouded header doesn't cover it, and the label is clamped inside the outline. Found and fixed along the way: (justify mirror) nested inside (font ...) instead of beside it made KiCad refuse to load the board, which our own s-expr parser accepted.

title: guide: render_scale under-predicts the board's size in a pcb render, so step highlights drift off their pads
description:
guide.rs::render_scale models kicad-cli 'pcb render' as framing the board's bounding circle against the frame's short side. Measured against real renders it under-predicts, and by an amount that varies with aspect:

  slew_limiter  40.6 x 128.5mm  predicted board/window 87.1%, actual ~90.2%  (~3.5% low)
  double_sided  32.4 x 16.8mm   predicted 84.4%, actual ~93.5%              (~11% low)

Because the overlay is scaled by render_scale, a too-small scale pulls every highlight toward the image centre. On double_sided the R1/C1 boxes land roughly a pad-width right of the actual pads; on slew_limiter the error is small enough to still look seated. Wide boards are worst.

Pre-existing (predates the print-quality work in legion-of-bom-0v1); that work made it visible by enlarging the diagram. Robust fix is probably to stop predicting and instead detect the board's bounding box in the rendered PNG (the render background is a flat gradient, the board is not), or to calibrate render_scale against a set of renders spanning aspect ratios. Affects both guide_to_html and guide_to_pdf, plus the new board_window crop, which inherits the same scale.
close_reason: Re-measured properly with scripts/measure_render_scale.py (checked in): decodes a real render, finds the board, compares to Edge.Cuts. The bounding-circle model was wrong, not just miscalibrated — KiCad frames the board's LONGEST dimension against the image HEIGHT with ~2.3% headroom, and the frame's width does not enter at all. Confirmed across 6 boards (aspect 0.32-2.67) and 5 frame sizes, including cases where the old model was 9.1% low. render_scale is now h_px/(1.023*max(w_mm,h_mm)), holding to +/-0.35%. Also fixed the related complaint that highlights sat inside their silkscreen: parse_board now unions the pad box with the footprint courtyard, so a 3.5mm jack's box spans its 10mm body instead of its 2.8mm pad column.

title: print quality: v-BOM + build guide are print-hostile (tiny pictures, wasted paper)
description: Audit found: board render letterboxed (board = 21% of image area) then squeezed into a half-width flex column, so the board is ~8% of the printed page; ~65% of every step page blank; highlight labels illegible; v-BOM cells 38mm with overflowing labels and 12/14 empty; BOM table has 3 all-empty columns and no package column. Redesign both for Letter/A4 at 100%.
close_reason: Both documents rebuilt print-first. Diagram cropped to the board (board_window) and sized to the sheet (diagram_fit): on a 5HP Eurorack panel the step picture goes from ~19x62mm to 74x214mm. Refdes labels now sized from the printed width (label_size_for) so they read ~10pt on any board. Steps restructured: per-refdes tick boxes, package column, orientation cue per part instead of a repeated banner. Sort list deduped across steps. Kit sheet gained a front/back board overview. Every sheet identified + numbered. v-BOM cells 43.5mm x4 spanning the full measure, labels wrap, life-size package silhouettes fill photoless cells, all-empty BOM columns dropped. Native PDF switched to Letter with the same crop and layout. Follow-up filed: legion-of-bom-gko (render_scale accuracy).

title: Import existing boards via their fab package (JLC BOM + CPL + gerbers)
description:
User: "importing other schematics (DipTrace) — PHRSR, SCANNER, TVCA, EG then 2OPFM from SuperSynthesis... We can re-use existing layouts though no?" YES — and without parsing any CAD file.

FINDING (verified on ~/src/fpl/supersynthesis-eurorack): DipTrace .dch/.dip are PROPRIETARY BINARY (magic \\x07DTSCHEM), undocumented — reverse-engineering them is a large fragile job, see [[legion-of-bom-diptrace-native]]. But every target module already ships a complete JLCPCB fab package, in formats LOB ALREADY EMITS:
  <mod>_JLCBOM.csv  -> Comment(value), Designator(refdes), Footprint, LCSC Part #
  <mod>_JLCXY.csv   -> Designator, Mid X, Mid Y, Layer(Top/Bottom), Rotation
  <mod>_gerber.zip  -> .GTL/.GBL/.GTO/.GBO/.GTS/.GBS/.GTP/.GBP/.GKO + drill
  plus panel gerbers and a schematic PDF
Coverage confirmed: PHRSR, SCANNER, TVCA, EG, 2OPFM all have BOM + CPL + gerbers.

So: import the FAB PACKAGE, not the CAD file. That is format-stable, vendor-neutral, and is literally the shape we already write (jlc_bom_csv, jlc_cpl_from_kicad_pos, export_gerbers).

WHAT THIS BUYS: components (refdes/value/footprint/LCSC) -> BOM, MPN sourcing, visual BOM; placement (X/Y/rotation/side) -> build-guide step highlights and assembly ordering; gerbers -> fab re-order and the layer viewer [[legion-of-bom-02b]]. The proven layout is re-used as-is — our placer and router are bypassed entirely, which sidesteps every layout-quality issue for these boards.

WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY: connectivity. A fab package has no netlist, so no schematic view, no ERC, no simulation, no netlist-driven DRC. Be explicit about that in the UI rather than showing an empty schematic.

WORK: (1) a CircuitSource impl (or a distinct ImportedBoard model) built from BOM+CPL, with nets absent rather than faked; (2) manifest support for declaring an imported circuit and its package paths; (3) make guide/vBOM/BOM paths tolerate a circuit with no nets; (4) surface it in the dashboard with its own badge so it is never mistaken for a circuit LOB laid out.
notes:
SHIPPED (first slice). Manifest: circuits may declare 'import' (fab-package dir) instead of 'source'; source is now Option, with Manifest::declaration_errors() enforcing exactly-one-of since serde cannot see a meaningless combination. core/import.rs parses JLC-style BOM + CPL (quote-aware CSV so grouped designators like "C1, C5" survive; alternative column spellings Comment/Value, Mid X/PosX, Layer/Side; DNP detection; unit suffixes) and locates gerbers. Web: gerber view resolves an imported circuit's package dir; /source returns a clear 'imported — defined elsewhere' 404 rather than an empty pane; lob circuits marks imported entries. Copied PHRSR/SCANNER/TVCA/EG/2OPFM fab packages into puget-hardware/supersynthesis (~6MB, fab package + schematic PDF only). VERIFIED all five parse: 43-98 components each, placements matching, gerbers render. TWO REAL BUGS found by real third-party data, both fixed with tests: (1) LayerKind::classify only knew KiCad + Protel names, so DipTrace's descriptive '1 - Top.gbr'/'TopSilk.gbr'/'BoardOutline.gbr' all fell to Other and scanner rendered empty (527B); now matches on meaning, compound names first. (2) Excellon coords may be signed with an IMPLICIT decimal ('X+013476' = 1.3476in) — the '+' was rejected so every hole was silently dropped (183 on scanner). Gates: 233 core + 11 web, fmt/clippy clean. NOT DONE: imported BOM is not yet surfaced through /api/bom or the vBOM/guide (they still read the cached netlist), placements are parsed but unused, and no dashboard badge distinguishing imported circuits in the UI list.
2026-08-18 stale in-progress cleanup: removed from active work. Keep open because the bead is broader than the shipped slice or still has unresolved scope in the existing notes.

title: Gerber viewer: layer-by-layer, in the dashboard
description:
User: "a gerber viewer for layer by layer". Render a gerber set in the web UI with per-layer visibility — copper top/bottom, silk, mask, paste, outline, drill — the way a fab house viewer does, so a board can be checked before it is sent and so IMPORTED boards (which arrive as gerbers only) can be seen at all.

WORK: (1) parse RS-274X in core (new gerber.rs): apertures (AD/ADD with C/R/O/P + macros), D01/D02/D03, G01/G02/G03 arcs, G36/G37 polygon fill, MO/FS coordinate format, LP dark/clear. This is a real but well-specified format — unlike DipTrace, it has a public spec. (2) Excellon drill for holes. (3) Render each layer to SVG with the usual colour convention, composited with per-layer opacity/visibility. (4) Web: GET /render?view=gerber&layer=... plus a layer checklist in the PCB viewer, reusing the existing ZoomPan.

Note the layer NAMING differs by tool: our KiCad exports use F.Cu/B.Cu/etc, the SuperSynthesis DipTrace exports use Protel extensions (.GTL/.GBL top/bottom copper, .GTO/.GBO silk, .GTS/.GBS mask, .GTP/.GBP paste, .GKO outline). Map both to a canonical layer set. Enables [[legion-of-bom-vendored-layouts]].
close_reason: Gerber viewer shipped. core/gerber.rs parses RS-274X (%FS/%MO incl. imperial, %LP clear-as-board-colour, apertures C/R/O/P, aperture macros with primitives 1/4/20/21 + expression evaluator for KiCad's RoundRect '$1+$1', G01 draws, G02/G03 arcs flattened, G36/G37 regions, D01/D02/D03) and Excellon drill. LayerKind::classify handles BOTH our KiCad names (-F_Cu.gtl) and Protel extensions (.GTL/.GBO/.GKO) so imported boards map to the same canonical layers. layers_to_svg renders per-layer groups in fab-viewer colours with sane z-order. Web: /render?view=gerber&layers=cu-top,cu-bot,... cached per selection; PCB viewer gets a 'Gerber' segment + layer checklist with colour swatches. Verified on the real slew_limiter fab package: 13 layers parsed (B.Cu 463 prims, drill 64 holes), render correct (top pour, bottom traces, punched holes, outline). 6 unit tests (classification, outline geometry incl. 25.4x128.5mm, flashes+regions, imperial units, macro expressions, Excellon). Gates: 225 core + 11 web, fmt/clippy clean. NOT done: no G74 single-quadrant mode, no step-and-repeat (%SR), no gerbjob parsing, and no netlist recovery from copper — see [[legion-of-bom-u0c]].

title: Schematic: pin names on ICs (In+/In-/OUT/IABC), not bare numbers
description:
The single change that makes the schematic readable. Today a boxed IC shows bare pin numbers, so on puget slew_limiter U1 (LM13700 OTA) renders as a rectangle with 1,3,4,5,7,8 — and pins 4 and 5 BOTH landing on SLEW_NODE is the entire slew-limiter topology (OTA output charges C1, cap voltage feeds back to the inverting input) which the reader cannot see, because nothing says 4 is In- and 5 is the output. Same for pin 1 = IABC, the bias input RV1 (the RATE pot) drives.

DATA IS ALREADY THERE, VERIFIED: KiCad symbols carry pin names — LM13700 declares +, -, V+, V-, DIODE_BIAS — and symbols::read_symbol_graphics already parses every pin; it keeps `number` and discards `name`. The netlist has ZERO pinfunction fields, so the symbol is the only source.

WORK: (1) add `name` to SymPin; (2) label boxed-part pins with name (falling back to number) instead of number alone; (3) label real symbol pins too where the symbol does not already draw them (KiCad hides pin_numbers on passives via (pin_numbers (hide yes)) — respect that). Follows [[legion-of-bom-n5l]].
close_reason:
Done, with one honest shortfall handed to [[legion-of-bom-22u]].

BUILT:
1. SymPin.name, plus SymbolGraphics.pin_names harvested across ALL units. This was the actual bug: read_symbol_graphics skipped units 2+ entirely (if idx > 1 continue), and a multi-unit IC keeps most of its pins there -- which is exactly the part that falls back to a labelled box. Harvesting unit 1 only left the LM13700 showing bare numbers.
2. SymbolGraphics.hide_pin_names from (pin_names ... hide), honoured when drawing.
3. Boxed parts label 5 OUT rather than replacing the number: the netlist and the datasheet pinout both key on the number, the name is what makes it mean something. Ellipsized to 11 chars, which is what a 108-wide box gives each side.
4. Drawn symbols label their named pins too, inside the body, KiCads own convention. Passives draw nothing -- they name their pins ~ and most also set hide.
5. Fixed a collision the wider labels exposed: box pin labels sat 3px above their lead, and the topmost pin is only ~8px below the box edge, so the cap height cut through the border. Centred on the lead now.

VERIFIED on puget slew_limiter: U1 reads 3 + and 4 -, U2 reads 2 -, 3 +, 5 +, 6 -. Rendered and eyeballed, not just grepped.

SHORTFALL: this beads title asks for In+/In-/OUT/IABC and KiCad does not declare IABC or OUT -- LM13700 pins 1, 5, 7, 8 are all ~. The beads own VERIFIED list says the same thing (+, -, V+, V-, DIODE_BIAS). So pins 4 AND 5 both landing on SLEW_NODE is still only half legible: 4 - shows, 5 stays bare. Real pinout names need a parts library, filed as 22u.

New examples/schem_preview for iterating on the schematic. 332 tests pass, clippy clean.

title: Visual build guide: red highlight rects are misplaced + on the wrong side
description: User: "The visual build guide red-rects are off in position and side." The per-step highlight rectangle in the generated build guide does not line up with the part it points at, and appears on the wrong board side (front vs back). Likely causes to check in guide.rs/fab.rs: (1) the rect is computed from the placement origin without applying the part origin_offset and rotation (uq2 just made rotation real for pots — keepout_at_rot / rotate_offset are the correct helpers); (2) back-side parts need the X mirror applied to match the flipped bottom render (keepout_at and tht_pads_at already take a back flag); (3) board-mm to render-pixel scaling must use the same origin/extent as render_board_png, and the bottom render is mirrored. Verify against a rotated pot (RV1/RV2 now at 90 deg) and a back-side SMD (C1/U2) on puget slew_limiter.
close_reason: Build-guide highlight rects now land on their parts. TWO stacked bugs, both fixed and visually verified on puget slew_limiter: (1) parse_board ignored footprint rotation — KiCad stores pads un-rotated and applies orientation at draw time, so 90-deg parts (pots after uq2, power header) got wrong-shaped boxes in wrong places; now rotates in KiCad's sense (x,y)->(y,-x) at +90, matching board.rs. (2) mm->px scale was a fixed 0.70 'fraction of frame' constant, but KiCad's ortho camera frames the board's bounding CIRCLE, so the fit depends on the board diagonal and hence its aspect ratio — a single constant is unfixable. On the tall 5HP board it was ~40% short, dragging every box toward centre. New render_scale() = min(w_px,h_px)/hypot(w_mm,h_mm), predicts a real render's board pixel size within 0.2%. Verified across rotated front pots, back-side SOICs on the mirrored bottom render, and the rotated header — all boxes hug their pads with correct pin-1 markers. Tests pin rotation sense + scale. Gates: 207 core + 11 web, fmt/clippy clean.

title: Panel cutouts must be derived from the real board layout, not an idealized grid
description: User: 'The panel still doesn't get its holes derived from the layout of the board. It is idealized/simplified and wouldn't actually fit.' derive_panel currently lays controls out on its OWN idealized grid (derive_rules: JACK_PITCH 16mm, POT_PITCH 20mm, single centreline column at x=hp/2, TOP/BOTTOM margins) and the board placer then anchors parts TO those cutouts. So the panel is the source of truth and the board follows — but the panel positions were never validated against real footprint geometry (pot body 13.75x12.82 incl. lugs, jack barrel + body, rotation from control_rotation, knob/nut diameters, finger clearance). Result: a panel that looks fine but whose real hardware collides or does not fit. Fix direction: make the pipeline board-aware — either (a) derive cutouts from the PLACED board (place first with real PartFacts + rotations, then project each panel-facing part's mount point up to the panel), or (b) keep panel-first but validate/repair the derived positions against PartFacts (body extents at their actual rotation, knob clearance, edge margins) and iterate until collision-free. Must account for rotated controls now that uq2 rotates pots 90deg. Related: [[legion-of-bom-6f8]] (silk vs cutout collision), [[legion-of-bom-j54.21]].
close_reason: Panel cutouts now derive from real mechanical envelopes instead of hole sizes. CutoutSpec.envelope_mm carries the space a control actually occupies (larger of panel-side hardware — knob skirt / nut + plug grip — and the anchored PCB body), filled by BuiltinCutouts via the existing CutoutSource seam so the parts library can replace it. Added min_panel_hp() (narrowest panel whose hardware fits: widest envelope + 2x edge material); derive_panel spaces by real envelope + gap and WIDENS rather than emit an unbuildable panel; board::minimum_hp now floors its search at min_panel_hp so 'PCB drives the panel' cannot pick a width the panel can't carry; CLI reports the emitted width. slew_limiter min HP 3 (unbuildable: 15.24mm panel vs 13.75mm pot body) -> 4, all controls fit with >=1mm edge material, no envelope overlaps, 5HP build still DRC-clean + fab builds. Test derived_panel_hardware_physically_fits pins width-fit + no-overlap. Gates: 205 core + 11 web, fmt/clippy clean. NOT done (follow-ups): cutout positions are still a single centre column — no 2-column layout for dense modules; envelopes are per-KIND defaults not per-MPN (real knob diameter should come from the parts library, epic okm); panel does not yet consult the PLACED board (option (a) in this bead) — it remains panel-drives-board with the panel now validated.

title: minimum_hp is optimistic: ignores copper edge clearance + routability (3HP/4HP fail)
description: User: 'The latest 3HP has overlap and components are hanging off on slew limiter.' After the uq2 pot-rotation fix, minimum_hp reports 3 HP for slew_limiter, but building at 3HP gives 6 DRC errors (4x copper_edge_clearance actual 0.0000mm vs 0.5mm required, 2x unconnected_items) and at 4HP gives 2 copper_edge_clearance errors. Only 5HP is clean. Cause: minimum_hp only checks that part keep-outs FIT in the width (placement fit); it does not model (a) copper/track-to-board-edge clearance (0.5mm), (b) whether the router can actually complete all nets in that width, (c) parts overhanging the outline. Fix: make minimum_hp route-aware — trial-build candidate widths smallest-first and accept the first that is DRC-clean (or at least reserve EDGE_MARGIN + copper edge clearance around the outline and verify no part/track exceeds it). Until then min-HP must not be trusted as a buildable width. Closely related to [[legion-of-bom-jiv]] (HP-minimizing mode).
notes:
minimum_hp legalizes before judging again (commit 1056474), now that the rules actually bound the copper. slew_limiter: 5 HP -> 4 HP, and unlike the first attempt at this change, the width it names has ZERO copper_edge_clearance errors under real KiCad DRC.

REMAINING, and it is the original part (b): minimum_hp still models geometry, not routability. It does not ask whether the router can complete every net in that width, and track-to-edge clearance is unmodelled (only part copper is). The remaining DRC errors on generated boards are tracks_crossing / shorting_items / solder_mask_bridge, i.e. router quality — but note those appear at 4 HP AND 5 HP roughly equally, so they are not width-driven and do not invalidate the 4 HP answer.

CAVEAT ON MEASUREMENT: all of the above is via examples/board_preview, which derives an idealised panel and produces boards with ~70 DRC errors where the shipped board has 5 (see legion-of-bom-nz1). The copper_edge_clearance 5->0 result is trustworthy because it is a before/after on the same harness; the absolute counts are not. Re-measure against a real declared panel before closing.

Closing this properly means trial-build smallest-first and require DRC-clean — with legion-of-bom-jiv.
close_reason:
Route-aware sizing landed: minimum_routable_hp in layout.rs trial-builds each width smallest-first (place -> route -> real KiCad DRC) and accepts the first clean one, degrading to an explicit unproven rather than guessing when kicad-cli is absent. lob panel fit now reports a PROVEN width with per-width evidence; new examples/hp_search harness shows the search.

Reproduced and fixed the original complaint. Searching slew_limiter from 3 HP:
  3 HP - 8 DRC errors: 4x copper_edge_clearance (the parts hanging off the edge the user reported) + 4x unconnected_items (unroutable)
  4 HP - DRC clean

FINDING worth knowing: the geometric floor now says 5 HP while 4 HP builds DRC-clean, so minimum_hp is CONSERVATIVE against KiCad, not optimistic as this bead was filed for. Cause: our EDGE_CLEARANCE_MM is 1.5mm where KiCad copper_edge_clearance is 0.5mm. That is a deliberate manufacturing margin, so 5 HP is the right shipped answer and 4 HP is DRC-clean-but-below-our-own-policy. Both numbers are correct, they answer different questions, and the tool now says which is which.

The trial config lives in ONE place (layout::eurorack_trial_build) and is what the CLI builds with. A trial configured differently from the build proves nothing about the build -- see nz1.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: lob panel derive / the auto-panel path on lob build still use the fast geometric floor, not the DRC-proven width. It costs ~10s per build to prove, and now that the floor is conservative on edge clearance the downside is much smaller. Remaining exposure is routability at the floor, which is real but not what this bead was about. Filed as follow-up if wanted.

title: Panel render UX: size parity with PCB + cache/own-version + show current HP
description: User: 'panel renders slow and is much smaller than the pcb ... doesn't show current HP.' Three fixes: (1) .panel-strip is width:150px beside a 520px PCB viewer — make the panel a comparable-height column so they read at parity. (2) render.rs panel branch has NO disk cache (board views do) AND the SPA cache-busts it with the *board* mtime, so it re-renders on every board rebuild though it's independent — give the panel its own version (panel-file mtime) + cache it keyed by that. (3) Expose panel hp/finish/format in CircuitView (project.rs) and show HP in the workspace head/panel caption. Discovered from awu.
notes: Server+API done & verified: panel_hp/finish/format/mtime in CircuitView; render.rs caches panel SVG keyed by spec mtime (0.0018s warm); SPA cache-busts panel on its OWN mtime (not board's); HP tag in head-row + 'Panel · 8 HP · black' caption; CSS makes panel a 520px-tall column at parity with PCB viewer. Compiles clean; gate pending.
close_reason: Render UX shipped & verified. (1) Size parity: panel now renders as a full 520px-tall column matching the PCB viewer (was a 150px strip). (2) Speed/own-version: render.rs caches the panel SVG keyed by spec mtime (0.0018s warm); SPA cache-busts the panel on its OWN mtime, not the board's, so board rebuilds no longer re-fetch it. (3) HP shown: CircuitView exposes panel_hp/finish/format/mtime; head-row shows an 'N HP' chip + 'Panel · 5 HP · black' caption. Gates green (192 core+10 web, fmt/clippy clean).

title: Router improvement: net-aware routing that doesn't short at density
description: The current GridRouter/MstRouter shorts nets + leaves connections unrouted as boards get dense (slew_limiter: 8HP clean → 5HP 1 err → 4HP 15 errs / shorting_items + solder_mask_bridge). The 3mm placement clearance was a band-aid spreading parts so the crude router couldn't cross them (asinine space waste). Needs a real router: net-by-net with rip-up-and-retry, layer assignment, escape routing from dense pin fields, honoring copper/mask clearances so no shorts. Pairs with design-rule placement (sibling) — good placement shortens the routing burden. DESIGN 6.5/6.6.
notes: INVESTIGATED (not rewritten). GridRouter is more capable than the docs implied: obstacle-aware maze/Dijkstra, correct clearance halos around pads AND committed traces (trace-half+clearance) + wider via halos, and a blame/rip-up pass. It still (a) leaves some nets unrouted at density and (b) trips copper/mask DRC at aggressive spacing (grid 0.2mm precision + copper-only 0.2mm clearance not covering soldermask expansion + sheer density). KEY FINDING: better PLACEMENT is the lever — with w95 (decoupling caps clustered on ICs) the router now routes DRC-CLEAN at 1.5mm placement clearance where it was 15 errors at 2.0mm before. So the practical density win came from placement, not the router. REMAINING genuine router work: mask-aware clearance (copper+mask, not just copper), finer/needed grid, robust rip-up-and-retry to eliminate the unrouted tail, so 4HP density routes clean. Blocks getting slew_limiter below 5HP.
close_reason: Reconciled/dedup: the concrete router-quality work is already filed under the layout epic — j54.25 (the specific 4HP back-side SOIC pad short, our exact blocker), j54.17 (back-side GND pour ↔ back components), j54.7 (DFM checks). Investigation folded into j54.25: GridRouter is actually obstacle-aware (halos on pads+traces, rip-up) — the gaps are mask-aware clearance (copper-only 0.2mm ignores soldermask) + the pour/back-flip interaction, not a rewrite. Pursuing via j54.25 + j54.17.

title: Design-rule-driven placement: codify electrical intent (decoupling/coupling caps, feedback, critical nets)
description: USER DIRECTION: 'important design decisions should be codified in PLACEMENT, not bolted on at the end.' The placer today only knows connectivity (SeededPlacer centroid seeding = crude proxy). It needs component ROLES + placement rules: (1) DECOUPLING/bypass caps (cap between an IC power pin and GND) placed IMMEDIATELY adjacent to that pin — shortest loop, the #1 rule; (2) COUPLING caps (series in signal path between stages) placed between the two stages; (3) FEEDBACK/gain networks (R/C around an op-amp) tight to the amp; (4) series resistors next to their pin; (5) CRITICAL/sensitive nets (integrator caps, high-Z nodes) short + prioritized (DESIGN 6.4 critical-net tagging). Roles inferred from topology (cap VCC↔GND=decoupling) and/or SKiDL tags / parts-library. This is BOTH correct design AND the lever that makes routing tractable (short, obvious traces → the crude router stops shorting on tight boards). Relates to DESIGN 3.4/6.3/6.4, layout epic j54.
close_reason: First design rule codified in placement: DECOUPLING CAPS (the #1, highest-leverage). core/src/board.rs decoupling_bonus(circuit): identifies a cap tied between a power rail (+/-/VCC/VDD/VEE...) and GND, pairs it with an IC (footprint Package_*) on that rail (fewest-decoupled-first when several), and emits a strong DECOUPLE_PULL(12.0) attractor edge cap↔IC folded into SeededPlacer's centroid adjacency — so the cap SEEDS hard against the chip's power pin. Roles inferred from TOPOLOGY (no SKiDL tags needed). VERIFIED on slew_limiter: C2(+12V↔GND)→U1 (11mm nearest), C3(-12V↔GND)→U2 (8.4mm nearest), C1 (signal cap) correctly NOT bonded (16.9/20.9mm away). BIG: the 5HP auto board now passes DRC 0 errors (was 1 error before the rule) — better placement made the previously-unroutable board route clean, exactly the thesis. 187 core tests (+decoupling_bonus test), fmt+clippy clean. FOLLOW-UPS (same pattern, own beads later): coupling caps in signal path, feedback networks tight to the amp, tighter 'hard-against' adjacency (place decoupling cap immediately after its IC / reserve the pad). Next: 4e4 router. Relates [[placer-router-honest-state]].

Drop the hard-coded 'back side first (mostly SMD)' framing for THT kits. title: Path B: Circuit -> pedalkernel .pedal DSL emitter
description: Emit a pedalkernel .pedal file from our Circuit IR. DSL shape: 'pedal "name" { components { R1: resistor(10k) C1: cap(47n) U1: opamp(ca3080) } nets { in -> R1.a  R1.b -> U1.pos  ... -> out  ... -> gnd } }'. Maps ~1:1 to our parts+nets. Mapping table: R/C/L primitives -> resistor/cap/ind; LM13700/CA3080 -> opamp(ca3080) (OTA); TL072 etc -> opamp(<model>); pot (RV) -> ? (PK pot component or two resistors); jacks -> in/out ports; supplies -> PK supply. Foundation of cross-engine validation (proven: PK compiles our slew topology, exit 0).

title: Path A: source pedalkernel op-amp/OTA model params into our ngspice subckts
description: Replace legion-of-bom's hand-guessed op-amp subckt with one driven by pedalkernel's curated params (opamps.model: TL072 A0=200k GBW=3MEG SR=13V/us RO=75; CA3080 gm=2mS IABC=100u VT=25.86mV). Build a 1-pole slew-limited op-amp subckt parameterised by (A0,GBW,SR,RO,rails); source per-part params from the pedalkernel registry, fall back to our behavioural GENERIC. OTA already parameter-free in ngspice (tanh + circuit-set IABC, matches their ota_ca3080.spice). Depends on the dependency-boundary decision. Improves fidelity: real TL072 slew limiting on the buffers.

title: Decide the pedalkernel dependency boundary: sub-crate vs vendor vs optional dep
description: User question: is the pedalkernel DSL/models a SMALL isolatable crate, or does depending on it pull the whole WDF/MNA engine? pedalkernel/src/models.rs + dsl.rs live inside the big 'pedalkernel' lib crate. Options: (1) extract a lightweight pedalkernel-models and/or pedalkernel-dsl sub-crate in the pedalkernel workspace, then take an OPTIONAL (feature-gated) path/crates.io dependency from legion-of-bom-core; (2) vendor the small .model files (like the Daisy footprints) + a tiny parser — self-contained, no dep, must sync; (3) hard path-dep on the whole pedalkernel crate (heavy, fragile). Recommend (1) if the models/dsl modules are dependency-light; measure what they pull. AGPL: an optional-feature dep keeps legion-of-bom's default build AGPL-free.

title: Pedalkernel integration — shared model library + cross-engine validation
description: Integrate pedalkernel (~/src/pedalkernel/pedalkernel, AGPL, owned by us) as legion-of-bom's model + differential-validation partner. Pedalkernel vends a curated behavioural model registry (models/*.model: opamps.model has op-amps with real SR/GBW/RO + an OTA CA3080 with gm/IABC/VT; plus transistors/jfets/diodes/tubes) driving its realtime WDF/MNA engine — NOT ngspice. Two complementary directions, both proven feasible this session: (A) SOURCE pedalkernel's model PARAMS into legion-of-bom's ngspice subckt generation (our OTA tanh already matches their ota_ca3080.spice exactly); (B) CROSS-ENGINE VALIDATION — convert our Circuit IR -> pedalkernel .pedal DSL, run it through the WDF (pedalkernel process), and diff vs our ngspice simulate_tran (two independent engines agreeing = high confidence). pedalkernel compiles our slew topology (OTA+integrator+feedback) exit 0; the .pedal DSL maps ~1:1 to our parts+nets. See memory [[pedalkernel-cross-engine-validation]]. Complements tus.3 (model catalog) + tus.10 (transient).

title: Cross-engine validation: Circuit -> pedalkernel DSL -> WDF, diff vs our ngspice
description: Differential validation across two independent engines. PROVEN FEASIBLE this session: pedalkernel's .pedal DSL (components{R/C/opamp(model)} + nets{a->b}) maps ~1:1 to our Circuit IR; pedalkernel (~/src/pedalkernel/pedalkernel, AGPL, owned by us) compiles OTA circuits AND our exact slew topology (OTA -> integrator cap -> feedback), exit 0, 2 WDF stages; 'pedalkernel process <pedal> <in.wav> <out.wav>' runs it through the realtime WDF/MNA engine. BUILD: (1) Circuit -> .pedal emitter in legion-of-bom (map R/C/L, opamp(model), OTA, pot->? , jacks->in/out ports); (2) harness: emit .pedal + a step/sequence WAV, run pedalkernel process, read out.wav, measure slew/response; (3) compare to our ngspice result (simulate_tran), gate on agreement within tolerance. NOTE: pedalkernel's OTA IABC is a model param (fixed rate), so PK validates slew at a fixed IABC vs our ngspice at the same bias; the VC/CV sweep stays ngspice-side unless PK exposes IABC as a control. Same model DATA source (pedalkernel opamps.model: TL072 SR=13, CA3080 gm=2mS), two engines. Complements tus.3/tus.10.
close_reason: Reorganized under the dedicated pedalkernel-integration epic [[legion-of-bom-ef4]]: cross-engine validation split into ef4.3 (Circuit -> .pedal emitter) + ef4.4 (WDF-vs-ngspice diff harness), with ef4.1 (dependency boundary) + ef4.2 (Path A model-param sourcing) + ef4.5 (VC/CV via OTA IABC control). Feasibility proof (PK compiles our slew topology, DSL maps ~1:1) captured in the epic + memory.

title: RATE range control: switchable integrating cap (~4.7n/47n/470n) + reverse-log taper
description: The defining v1 feature (competitive gap vs A-170's 3-range switch). Single 47nF + linear pot spreads 'frozen -> audio-rate' too thin to play. Add a 2-3 position switch selecting the integrating cap C1 (fast/med/slow, e.g. 4.7n/47n/470n) and a reverse-log (or log) taper on the RATE pot so portamento-to-slow-glide has musical resolution. Keep CV scaling consistent across ranges. Requires: switch part + panel element (feeds the compact 4-6HP panel + 3jh narrow-layout work).
notes:
THE PREMISE HAS LARGELY DISSOLVED. This bead says "single 47nF + linear pot spreads frozen -> audio-rate too thin to play". True, but the cause was not the cap or the taper.

R3 (pot) and R5 (CV) each injected current INDEPENDENTLY into the IABC pin, which sits at V_BIAS. Unpatched, J4 normals CV to 0V -- still 10.6V above V_BIAS -- so R5 poured a fixed 225uA in permanently. The pots own 12.8..481uA sat on that floor: total 238..706uA, i.e. 3:1. No taper fixes a floor.

Fixed by summing RATE and CV as VOLTAGES into TL074-D and doing ONE V->I conversion, the way Doepfers A-171-2 does (their A-170 gets 0..10s from one knob because it has NO CV -- no second branch). R5 deleted. SPICE: 3.0:1 -> 35.2:1.

At C1 = 1uF that is 22ms .. 783ms from ONE KNOB, which is the portamento range this product is positioned for ([[legion-of-bom-tus.11]]).

SO: is the RANGE switch still wanted? With the switch fitted the three modes are
   centre  1uF     22ms .. 783ms
   up      2uF     45ms .. 1.57s
   down    5.7uF  127ms .. 4.47s
Two of those are slower than portamento needs, and they cost a panel control, a
switch, and TWO FILM CAPS -- C5 is 14mm wide and is what pushed the board past
4 HP ([[legion-of-bom-e7k]]).

Dropping the switch would take out SW1, C4, C5, one panel cutout, and probably a
whole HP. Reverse-log taper on RV1 is still worth doing either way -- 35:1 of
linear-in-current still bunches the fast end.

NOT dropping it unilaterally: the switch is named in the v1 panel spec in
tus.11, so it is a product call.

title: Product v1: precise compact VC portamento (positioning + feature set locked)
description: Market positioning DECIDED (user): the slew limiter ships as a precise, compact VC portamento — 'does one thing perfectly'. Beats A-170 (adds VC + precision on every mode), beats 2hp Slew (adds range/feel), undercuts Rampage/Maths. Panel: RATE, CV amount (attenuator), RANGE switch | IN, OUT, RATE CV. Specs: VC LINEAR slew (constant dV/dt), dead-accurate 1V/oct (feedback topology, no diode offset), switchable range for fast<->slow feel. Compact 4-6HP, lean BOM (LM13700 OTA-A + TL072). CUT deliberately: separate rise/fall, EOC, dual, oscillate (that's the function-generator positioning we did NOT pick). Reference targets from competitive analysis: A-170 ranges L 0-0.5s/M 0-10s/H minutes; ours 0->~10 V/ms pot, ~40 V/ms w/ CV.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
CONTESTED 2026-07-28. This bead records 'dual' in the deliberately-cut list. The user has since asked for a dual slew limiter repeatedly and said so again today ('for the 10th TIME'), which means either the cut was reversed without being written down, or the dual is a separate product rather than a change to this one.

Filed as its own epic so it stops evaporating between sessions. This bead's positioning ('does one thing perfectly', compact 4-6 HP) is NOT edited, because reversing a recorded product decision is the user's call and not mine to infer — but anyone reading the cut list should know it is disputed.

Also relevant to the 4-6 HP target stated here: 4 HP was never actually tried. board::minimum_hp returns 6, so any narrower panel is rejected and silently replaced. Measured today, a 4 HP board is 44.6% occupied on its busiest side — the refusal is the placer's, not geometry's.

title: Wire transient sim into lob run + step-sequence & CV stimulus + slew-rate/CV verify
description: The transient sim (simulate_tran, the actual slew test) exists but is only in unit tests — lob run only does an AC sweep, which says nothing for a slew limiter. Need: (1) run transient for time-domain circuits in lob run; (2) stimulus beyond a single step — a step SEQUENCE (sequencer) on the signal input AND a CV input driving the rate node; (3) verify checks: output slews toward each step + slew rate scales ~linearly with CV/IABC. Behavioural validation done by hand (see artifact + scratchpad/slew_val.cir): base 2.13 V/ms, CV+5V -> 4.21 V/ms (1.98x), tracks 0/+5/-3/+2. Depends on OTA/op-amp models (tus.3).
close_reason: lob run now runs a transient step-response (simulate_tran) alongside the AC sweep and reports peak slew rate; soft-fails (warning) if a circuit's step won't converge. Slew limiter: 'transient step response peak slew 5.54 V/ms' — matches the 0-10 V/ms competitive envelope. With tus.9 + tus.3, the real board is validated end-to-end through the pipeline. Remaining (step-sequence + CV stimulus + formal slew-rate/CV verify gate) split to tus.13.

title: simulate stage hardcodes input net 'IN' — lob run fails on the slew limiter (uses SIG_IN)
description: lob run <slew_limiter> errors: 'simulation needs a net named IN'. SimConfig defaults input_net='IN'/output_net='OUT' and the CLI passes SimConfig::default(), but the circuit uses SIG_IN/SIG_OUT. So the real board has NEVER simulated through the pipeline (AC or transient). Fix: auto-detect I/O nets (jack-tagged / by name heuristics) or let the circuit declare them; don't hardcode.
close_reason: SimConfig::infer(circuit) auto-detects I/O + supply nets from the circuit's own net names (SIG_IN/SIG_OUT via a candidate list; +12V/-12V/+5V/+3V3/VCC/VEE via rail_voltage name parsing), falling back to IN/OUT/±15V. CLI 'lob run' uses it. Slew limiter now passes the net-config error (next blocker is missing part models = tus.3). Unit tests rail_voltage_parses_supply_names + infer_adapts_io_and_supplies_to_the_circuit.

title: Add Daisy Patch SM + Seed2 DFM via vendored Electrosmith footprints
description: Beyond the synthesized Seed: vendor the real Electrosmith DaisyKiCad footprints (MIT) for Patch SM (40 THT pads, 4x 2x5 headers) and Seed2 DFM (50 SMD pads, 5x 2x5 @1.27mm). Bundled under crates/core/footprints/Daisy-Boards.pretty (+LICENSE), embedded via include_str! and resolved through subboard::footprint_text for the LobModule: lib. Pads named by physical pin (A1..D10 / A1..E10), so nets map straight to the datasheet pinout. Pinouts sourced from the official pinout PDFs/CSVs. Patch SM demo routes 0 DRC errors; Seed2 DFM places but fine-pitch SMD routing is a follow-up.
close_reason: Vendored the real Electrosmith DaisyKiCad footprints (MIT) for Patch SM (40 THT) + Seed2 DFM (50 SMD, SMT+PTH variants), embedded via include_str! + subboard::footprint_text under the LobModule: lib. Pads named by physical Daisy pin. Patch SM verified 0 DRC errors end-to-end. Seed2 DFM footprint correct + places; fine-pitch SMD routing tracked as 25z.7. 145 tests, clippy/fmt clean.

title: Named header pins + real Daisy Seed pinout (map nets by function, silk/fab labels)
description: Let authors reference sub-board pins by function name (AUDIO_OUT_L, D15, 3V3) not pad number. Add pin names to SubboardSpec (per pad), a name->pad lookup, and emit per-pad function labels on the footprint fab/silk layer. Replace the placeholder DIP numbering in daisy_seed() with the real Electrosmith Daisy Seed pinout (verified from the official source).
close_reason: SubboardSpec gains per-pad PinLabel (name + aliases); daisy_seed() carries the real Electrosmith pinout (libDaisy Daisy_Seed_Rev4_Pinout.csv) — D0-D30, AUDIO_IN/OUT_L/R, AGND/3V3_ANA/3V3_DIG/VIN/GND, with A0-A11 ADC aliases; the DIP pad numbering already matched the physical layout. pad_for(name)/pin_name(pad) lookups (case-insensitive + aliases); function-name labels emitted on F.Fab. board.rs resolves a net to a pad by pad number OR function name, so a net wired to 'AUDIO_OUT_L' connects pad 18. Daisy demo stays 0 DRC errors with fab labels. 140 tests (5 new), clippy/fmt clean.

title: Generate header/sub-board footprints from a spec (Daisy Seed built-in)
description: A footprint generator: spec (rows, pins/row, pitch, row spacing, body outline) -> KiCad .kicad_mod (THT header pads numbered, courtyard = board outline, silk outline + pin-1 marker). Built-in Daisy Seed spec (18x51mm, 2x20 @ 2.54mm, rows ~15.24mm apart). Synthesized in-memory via a reserved lib prefix in load_footprint so a part with footprint 'LobModule:Daisy_Seed' places+routes through the existing pipeline (courtyard -> keepout, THT pads -> router reaches from either side). First slice of epic 25z.
close_reason: subboard.rs generates KiCad .kicad_mod footprints from a spec (rows/pins/pitch/spacing/body); THT header pads reach both layers, courtyard=body=keep-out, pin-1 marked. Built-in Daisy Seed (18x51mm, 2x20 @2.54mm, DIP numbering). load_footprint synthesizes the reserved 'LobModule:' lib in-memory, so a part with footprint 'LobModule:Daisy_Seed' places+routes through the normal pipeline with no file on disk. Validated end-to-end through real KiCad: daisy_demo (Daisy + 2 SMD passives) places, routes 14 tracks 0 unconnected; only DRC error is a GND-pour thermal island (filed 25z.2, inherent to dense THT grids), not a footprint defect. 135 tests (4 new), clippy/fmt clean.

title: Sub-board & board-to-board header support (Daisy as placed module; 2-board stack)
description: Support building boards AROUND stacked sub-boards joined by headers — the user imports Daisy (Electrosmith) modules often and wants headers in specific layouts. Core primitive (user-confirmed first target): a sub-board is a PART whose footprint is a defined header layout + a board-sized keepout/height, pins mapped to nets, carried by the parts library (same seam as SPICE model / panel cutout), so the existing place->route->check loop mostly just works on it. A bought SOM (Daisy Seed) is a rich connector we don't fab; the generated 2-board stack (design+fab both PCBs) reuses the same primitive later. Also enables generic board-to-board headers in specified layouts.

title: Router: keep copper edge_clearance inside the board outline (fix copper_edge_clearance DRC)
description: The GridRouter was never told the board edge: route_options.bounds stayed None so it routed against the pad bbox and laid tracks/vias onto Edge.Cuts on tight boards. Fix: RouteOptions.edge_clearance_mm (default 0.5, = KiCad copper_edge_clearance); when bounds is the board outline the router insets the routable area by edge_clearance + widest-copper-half, keeping all copper the clearance inside the edge (surfaces the net as a conflict when the only path is in the band). board.rs now passes the panel outline as bounds. Verified: real 8HP slew limiter stays 0 DRC errors; the 6HP variant's 2 track copper_edge_clearance errors are eliminated. 130 tests, clippy/fmt clean.
close_reason: Router insets copper by edge_clearance_mm (0.5) + widest-copper-half inside the board outline; board.rs passes the panel outline as route bounds. 8HP slew limiter stays 0 DRC errors; 6HP track copper_edge_clearance errors eliminated (remaining 6HP errors are J4 placement-at-edge, filed separately). Regression test routing_refuses_to_enter_the_board_edge_band; 130 tests, clippy/fmt clean.

title: Router: A* pathfinding (done) — was Dijkstra flooding the whole grid
description: GridRouter.route_one now uses A* (admissible cost-scaled Manhattan heuristic to nearest target) instead of unbounded Dijkstra. 8HP board gen: never-finished-in-110s -> 6.6s (~17x+). Paths still optimal (all route tests pass). First milestone of the 'invest in auto-layout' work.
close_reason: A* landed: route_one uses an admissible Manhattan heuristic; 8HP gen 110s+->6.6s, routing still optimal (route tests pass, clippy/fmt clean).

title: Panel jack cutout must be the barrel hole (circle ~6mm), not the jack-body rect — else the mounting nut can't tighten onto the panel
description: footprint_shape maps Thonkiconn/PJ301 to RoundedRect{10x8.5} (the jack BODY). A Eurorack jack mounts through a ~6mm round barrel hole with a nut on the front; a square/body-sized cutout leaves nothing for the nut to grip. Panel cutout for jacks should be Circle{~6mm}.
close_reason: footprint_shape: Thonkiconn/PJ301 now resolve to a 6mm barrel Circle (JACK_BARREL_MM), not the body rect — the nut can tighten. Also fixes the hand-authored slew panel.

title: Main board generates as a wide landscape strip, not a vertical Eurorack 3U board
description: GridPlacer rows parts out wide (per_row=8) and the outline is just their bbox, so the slew limiter came out 178x52mm landscape — sideways, not Eurorack. Needs a Eurorack BOARD format: vertical outline (HP wide x ~3U tall) with parts placed to fit. Best done as panel-ANCHORED placement (extends PanelSpec/j54.10): the panel-facing parts (jacks, pots) placed at the SAME positions as the panel PCB cutouts so board+panel match, rest placed in the remaining area. Needs a refdes<->cutout link (e.g. optional refdes on panel TOML cutouts) + a EurorackPlacer. User feedback.
close_reason: EurorackPlacer: panel-facing parts anchored at their panel-cutout positions (via optional refdes on cutouts), rest spread down the tall board by first-fit collision placement; courtyard_extent spaces by real courtyards; BoardOptions.fixed_outline + lob board --panel. Slew limiter (8HP) now generates a vertical 3U module, 0 DRC errors, matching the panel PCB. Non-panel boards unchanged.

title: GND pour fragmented into isolated islands by traces -> starved_thermal (slew limiter)
description: Now that routing completes (tus.6), the extra B.Cu signal traces carve the GND ground pour into disconnected islands: DRC starved_thermal — C2 pin 2 [GND] connects only to an isolated island of the pour, not the main GND. A pad connected to a cut-off island isn't truly grounded (functional defect on a real board). Fixes to weigh: keep the pour on one layer + route signals on the other; add GND stitching vias to rejoin islands; route GND as tracks in addition to the pour; or make the router avoid splitting the pour. DESIGN 6.2 (ground pour). Exposed by the slew limiter, the first real board.
close_reason: Two-sided GND pour (THT pads bridge layers) + front-biased routing (back_penalty_mm keeps signals off the pour layer) -> ground plane stays intact, no more isolated-island starved_thermal. Slew limiter fully DRC-clean (0 errors, 0 unconnected). Example boards unaffected. Tests added.

title: Router routes through no-net pads -> DRC shorting_items (slew limiter: 24 errors)
description: On the first real board (slew limiter), 24 DRC shorting_items errors: tracks route straight through pads that carry no net — unused IC pins (LM13700 pin 2/15 diode-bias), jack switch contacts (PJ398SM 'TN'), and unused Eurorack header pins (J3 7/8). Root cause: board.rs passes only routed nets' pads to the Router, so no-net pads are never seeded as obstacles in the GridRouter grid. Phase 0 demo boards had a net on every pad, so this never surfaced. Fix: collect ALL pads (incl. no-net) and seed them as routing obstacles (blocked cells + clearance halo), routed-around but not connected. Blocks any real board with unused pins.
close_reason: Fixed: generate_board_report seeds each no-net pad as a single-pad obstacle net; GridRouter routes around them but never connects them. Slew limiter DRC 24 shorting_items -> 0. Regression test added.

Wire into guide_to_html (data-URI PNG in SVG) and guide_to_pdf (PNG->JPEG embed). Validated feasible.

title: Double-sided boards: per-footprint side attribute + side-aware placement (DESIGN 6.1)
description: Board side is a REAL, CURRENT requirement for Eurorack, not deferred. The Super Synthesis resurrection line (PHRSR/SCANNER/EG/TVCA) is genuinely double-sided in production: SMD/PCBA components on one side, THT + silkscreen on the OPPOSITE side — with the power header as the sole exception (THT, but placed on the PCBA side rather than the THT side). Requirements: every footprint in the anchored-cutout AND free-placement data model needs a side: front|back attribute; the placer assigns SMD to the PCBA side and THT+silk to the other, honoring the power-header exception. Guitar Pedal STAYS single-sided (real THT-pedal convention) — this is Eurorack-specific, do NOT generalize to 'all formats need both-side support' without evidence. Note: the emission seam already exists (Placement.back mirrors a footprint to B.Cu, pads mirror via pad_layer_on_board); the new work is the side attribute in the placement data model + the side-assignment convention. Integrates with the layout loop (j54.6) which owns free placement.
notes: CORRECTED per user + Super Synthesis pick-and-place: side is NOT derivable from SMD-vs-THT (Mutable boards mix both yet are single-sided). Side is now an explicit per-part declaration (Side field: front/back, top/bottom), default front. Model: Part.side: Option<Side> (Side in model.rs), parsed from the netlist Side field (SKiDL passes it through), threaded to the placer via PartFacts. Back parts flip correctly (child F./B. layers, mirror X, mirror back text; place_point mirrors pad X). Validated: rc/opamp default front (0/0); double_sided.py declares R1/C1 (SMD signal) on the poured back + J1 header on front — renders correctly, DRC 0 errors (remaining warnings are j54.18 THT-aware vias + j54.19 lib mismatch). DONE. Follow-ups: power-header exception is just a Side=back declaration now (no special code needed); board-level convention presets could live in PanelProfile (j54.1).
close_reason: Double-sided via explicit per-part Side declaration (default front). Back parts flip correctly (layers/coords/text), validated by render + DRC 0 errors. Mutable single-sided and Super Synthesis double-sided both handled.

title: Subcircuit library + role-requirements (DESIGN 3.4/3.4.1)
description: Extract reusable subcircuits into a git-native circuits/lib (Section 2.6 storage split). Each subcircuit entry declares what it REQUIRES from the part filling its role — a requires block (min_gbw_mhz, max_vos_mv, max_noise_nv_hz, part_family) — NOT which specific part was used. This is what makes substitution (9.6) possible without a hand-maintained pairwise compatibility table: the requirement lives with the ROLE, so a part valid in a buffer isn't automatically valid in a noise-sensitive signal path. First real member (3.4.1): the LM13700 bias generator (CV->IABC network), genuinely shared between the slew limiter and the crossfader. Boundary lesson to enforce: ONLY the bias generator is shared; the OTA application stays circuit-specific (slew=bounded current source, no diode linearization; crossfader=linear signal path, diode linearization required). Do not model the whole LM13700 circuit as one reused subcircuit — the boundary is narrower than the IC.

title: Real op-amp: carry SPICE model on the part (fix ideal U1)
