Mechanism (proven): SKiDL passes manually-set custom fields into the netlist, so the circuit definition — and later the Dolt parts library — can carry a part's footprint + MPN + SPICE model. Add Part.sim (Sim.Device/Name/Library/Pins), parse it in netlist.rs, and have the symbols resolver prefer the part-carried model over reading the shipped symbol (falling back for ideal parts). Model TL072 with the builtin op-amp subckt mapped to its real pinout (1=out 2=in- 3=in+ 4=vee 8=vcc) — an ideal model for now; a real macro-model replaces it under [[legion-of-bom-okm]] (okm.9). Validate: sim gain=10, verify passes, BOM has MPN, board lays out + routes DRC-clean. No generator special-casing (see architecture memory).
close_reason: Real TL072 flows through the whole pipeline (sim 20dB, verify gain 9.995x, BOM MPN, board routes DRC 0/0). Model travels with the part (Sim.* fields -> netlist -> resolver). Removed the is_opamp/is_ideal_opamp device-sniffing anti-pattern: analytic_check is now a registry of self-selecting checks. Added size-aware placement so real ICs don't collide.

title: Layout 6.5a: Router trait + trace routing (first-cut; GND via pour)
description: The routing primitive the iterative loop (j54.6) builds on. A Router trait (the seam, like Placer) that turns placed pads + nets into copper track segments. First impl: route each non-ground net's pads with F.Cu traces (chain/MST); GND (and ground nets) need no traces — the bottom pour (j54.2) handles returns per DESIGN 6.2. Needs absolute pad positions (footprint placement + pad offset; rotation-0 for the grid placer first cut). Emits (segment …). Not obstacle-avoiding yet — direct traces work for simple boards; crossing-avoidance / rip-up-retry is the iterative loop (j54.6), and complex boards may hand off to Freerouting or manual (6.8). DESIGN 6.5.
close_reason: Two-layer obstacle-aware maze router (GridRouter) + Router seam; routes both demo circuits DRC-clean (0 violations, 0 unconnected), incl. vias on the RC ladder

title: Layout 6.9: PanelSpec trait — format-agnostic seam (Eurorack impl only)
description: Same move as the deferred circuit IR (3.3), applied to panels: define a thin PanelSpec trait NOW, implement it fully for EURORACK ONLY (what's shipping), and defer pedal/rack/500-series impls until one is actually being built. Trait shape: dimensions in mm (each format's native units — HP/U, pedal enclosure size class, rack U × 19in-fraction, 500-series fixed slot — translate to mm INSIDE the impl, never exposed as universal concepts to the rest of the pipeline), a mounting-hole list, and a list of anchored cutouts (position, rotation, footprint reference). Section 7 DXF export and Section 6's layout loop both read panels THROUGH this trait, not assuming Eurorack. Rationale for not unifying speculatively: the four formats aren't similar enough, and 500-series is mechanically the odd one out (audio I/O via a card-edge connector into the shared lunchbox bus, not front-panel jacks) — forcing it into the anchored-jack-pot cutout model would be WRONG, not just incomplete. DESIGN.md 6.9; cf. 6.1, 7.1.
acceptance_criteria: a PanelSpec trait (mm dimensions + mounting holes + anchored cutouts) with a complete Eurorack impl; the layout loop + DXF export consume panels only through the trait; no Eurorack-specific concepts (HP/U) leak into pipeline code; other formats unimplemented on purpose

title: Layout 6.6: Board generation — netlist → .kicad_pcb (direct S-expr, headless)
description: The mechanics of driving KiCad pcbnew from legion-of-bom-core to turn the netlist/IR into a .kicad_pcb with footprints placed. Hardened successor to the Phase 0 layout-scaffolding stretch task. DESIGN.md 6.6.
design: DECISION (revises DESIGN 6.6 after de-risk): generate the .kicad_pcb DIRECTLY as S-expression (reuse core::sexpr) rather than via KiCad IPC or kicad-cli — neither can create a board / add footprints / assign nets (see de-risk note). Approach: load footprints from KiCad .kicad_mod libraries (S-expr), place them, embed into a .kicad_pcb with the net table + per-pad net assignments. Headless (no running KiCad), no deprecation risk (unlike SWIG pcbnew), fully under our control. Downstream (gerbers, CPL/position files, DXF, DRC, render) is kicad-cli shell-out once the board exists. Validate generated boards with 'kicad-cli pcb drc' / export.
acceptance_criteria: netlist -> a valid .kicad_pcb with footprints assigned+placed and nets wired; kicad-cli reads it (drc/export succeed); opens in KiCad; deterministic; no running KiCad needed
notes:
DE-RISK FINDING (2026-07-22) — revises DESIGN 6.6: neither the KiCad IPC API (kicad-ipc-rs, verified real+maintained, KiCad 10.0.1) NOR kicad-cli can do the netlist→board CREATION step.
- IPC API is a board EDITING/INSPECTION library: cannot create/open a board (one must already be open in a running KiCad GUI), no documented footprint-ADD, net assignment is READ-ONLY (get_pad_netlist yes, set_net no). It CAN move existing items + run DRC + read back violations.
- kicad-cli pcb = drc | export(gerbers/drill/position(CPL!)/…) | import(foreign PCB formats only) | render | upgrade — no netlist import, no board creation.
So netlist→board needs one of: (A) SWIG pcbnew Python API (deprecated KiCad9, removed KiCad11, but WORKS on KiCad10 now — can create board+add footprints+assign nets); (B) direct .kicad_pcb S-expr generation (future-proof, no dep, more work — reuse core::sexpr); or (C) human does 'Update PCB from Schematic' in KiCad, then we drive placement via IPC + export via kicad-cli. Downstream (gerbers, CPL, DXF, DRC, render) is all kicad-cli regardless. kicad-ipc-rs is the DRC/readback tool for the loop's check step, not the board-creation tool. Decision needed on A/B/C.
DE-RISK VALIDATED (2026-07-22): direct .kicad_pcb generation PROVEN end-to-end via Python prototype. Recipe: (1) parse footprint .kicad_mod (S-expr) from KiCad libs; (2) per instance set lib:name, insert (at x y rot)+(uuid), set Reference=refdes, inject (net N "name")+(uuid) into each connected pad; (3) assemble board = header + 2-layer (layers ...) + minimal (setup) + net table (net 0 "" then one per circuit net) + footprints. kicad-cli READS it: 'pcb drc' runs, 'pcb export gerbers' produced a full gerber set, 'pcb export pos' produced the CPL. Fully headless. Rust build (core::board): add a serializer to core::sexpr, load+transform .kicad_mod, emit board; placement is naive-grid for a first cut (auto-place is the loop's job, j54.6). Blueprint = the validated prototype.
close_reason: Board generation shipped: core::board::generate_board (netlist → valid .kicad_pcb, headless, direct S-expr). Loads .kicad_mod footprints, places (Placer trait — GridPlacer default, loop/PanelSpec placers plug in later) + net-wires them, 2-layer stack + net table. Deterministic UUIDs (sha2) → clean git diffs. core::sexpr rewritten as reader+writer (Sym/Str). 'lob board <circuit>'. Verified: kicad-cli reads it (DRC runs, nets wired) + exports full gerber set. Remaining board completeness is OTHER tasks: routing (j54.6 loop), ground pour (j54.2), board outline (PanelSpec j54.10). 54 core tests.

title: Layout 6.2: 2-layer ground-pour convention
description: Hard v1 constraint: 2 layers. Convention: bottom = solid ground pour, top = signal+power, via stitching to ground as needed. Replaces most manual star-ground work with a low-impedance return 'for free'; critical-net tagging (6.4) is the escape hatch where the pour isn't enough. DESIGN.md 6.2.
acceptance_criteria: board generation applies bottom ground pour + top signal/power + via stitching by default
close_reason: Board outline (Edge.Cuts rect from parts bbox + margin) + bottom-layer ground pour (B.Cu zone flooded to GND, DESIGN 6.2 default). Emitted via the generate_board seam; kicad-cli fills the zone on 'export gerbers --check-zones' (B.Cu gerber 459->965 bytes). Outline took DRC 1->0 violations. BoardOptions.ground_net/outline_margin_mm. Real panel-driven outline comes with PanelSpec (j54.10).

title: Layout 6.1: Format profiles (PanelProfile) with anchored connectors
description: Four v1 form factors — Eurorack, Guitar Pedal, Rack Mount, Desktop — each a PanelProfile: mounting-hole pattern, panel dimension convention (Euro HP / pedal size class / rack U / desktop footprint), and a library of standard connectors with fixed footprints + 3D models. Connectors (jacks, pots, switches) are PLACEMENT-ANCHORED from the panel spec, not placed by the optimizer — this shrinks free placement to just support components and is what makes the loop tractable vs NP-hard. DESIGN.md 6.1.
acceptance_criteria: a PanelProfile type with the 4 profiles; anchored connector positions derived from panel spec and exposed to the layout loop
notes: Refined by 6.9 (legion-of-bom-j54.10): don't design all four format profiles now. 6.1 becomes the EURORACK implementation of the PanelSpec trait (mounting-hole pattern, anchored jack/pot/LED connector library). Other formats' PanelSpec impls are deferred until actually built; 500-series in particular must NOT be forced into the anchored-front-panel-jack model (card-edge bus). Depends on the trait (legion-of-bom-j54.10).

Not general autorouting: constrain the problem to 4 format profiles with placement-ANCHORED connectors, a 2-layer ground-pour convention, and an analog/digital cost function, so a guided place->route->check->repair loop over only the FREE components/nets becomes tractable. title: Firmware/Oopsy board-definition export for carrier profiles
description:
Why this exists: once LOB knows a carrier's SOM pin bindings, firmware needs the same truth: libDaisy/Oopsy board definitions should be generated from the carrier profile instead of hand-copied.

Work: export a firmware-facing pinmap/board definition for Patch SM and Seed2 DFM carrier circuits, including audio, CV, gate, control, and GPIO mappings. Keep it downstream of the carrier netlist/profile work.

Acceptance: a carrier fixture produces a deterministic firmware pinmap artifact that names the SOM profile and every user-facing control binding.

title: Seed2 DFM Eurorack analog-front-end block library
description:
Why this exists: Seed2 DFM is not enough by itself for Eurorack CV/audio carrier boards. The carrier must protect and scale raw Eurorack audio, CV, gates, and outputs before they hit STM32/codec pins.

Work: create reusable circuit blocks for audio input/output conditioning, CV input scaling/clamping/filtering, CV output buffering/scaling, gate input/output conditioning, references/calibration points, and power hygiene.

Acceptance: a Seed2 DFM carrier cannot connect raw panel CV/audio/gate jacks straight to low-voltage pins without either using one of these blocks or emitting a validation failure.

title: Seed2 DFM carrier profile and named pin/capability map
description:
Why this exists: Seed2 DFM is the DFM/productization path for STM32 + codec carrier boards, but unlike Patch SM it exposes lower-level pins and requires the carrier to own more analog/front-end responsibility. LOB has vendored Seed2 DFM footprints but no first-class profile.

Work: add a Seed2 DFM hardware profile under the sub-board primitive with semantic pin aliases, audio/ADC/DAC/GPIO/power capabilities, body/keepout/standoff metadata as available from the footprint/datasheet, and tests for semantic pin resolution.

Acceptance: Seed2 DFM can be referenced through LobModule with named pins/capabilities and unknown names fail clearly.
close_reason: Added Seed2 DFM and Seed2 DFM PTH carrier profiles with named pin aliases, multi-capability pin metadata, body metadata, carrier platform support, and board/profile tests. Validated with cargo fmt --check, cargo test -p legion-of-bom-core, and cargo clippy -p legion-of-bom-core --all-targets -- -D warnings.

title: S-expression parser recurses without a depth bound
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] extra confirmed finding. sexpr.rs recurses without a depth bound, making user-supplied or malformed KiCad-style input capable of stack exhaustion. Fix should add a maximum nesting depth or iterative parser behavior and test excessive nesting fails gracefully.

title: Eagle importer drops nets with one real pin
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] extra confirmed finding. eagle.rs drops nets with <=1 real pin. Single-pin nets can still carry named intent, test points, power flags, or imported schematic information and should not disappear silently. Fix should preserve or explicitly report these nets according to the Circuit model contract.

title: BOM CSV writer emits unquoted fields
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] extra confirmed finding. bom.rs to_csv writes unquoted fields while fab.rs already has a correct CSV escaping helper. Values, MPNs, notes, or designator groups containing commas/quotes can corrupt generated CSV. Fix should reuse a proper CSV writer/escaping path and test comma/quote/newline fields.

title: EasyEDA pricing compares qty-5000 break against Mouser qty-1
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] extra confirmed finding. easyeda.rs takes the qty-5000 price break and ranks it against Mouser quantity-1 prices as cheaper. Fix should compare like quantities or label bulk-price candidates so automated ranking does not mislead sourcing decisions.

title: DIP body length fencepost makes life-size sheets too long
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] extra confirmed finding. package.rs computes DIP-16 body length as 20.92mm versus JEDEC's roughly 18.7-19.7mm range, affecting life-size/package sheets. Fix should correct the DIP body calculation and add representative package-size tests.

title: lob edit panics on inline-table lob.toml accepted by manifest reader
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] finding 11. edit.rs expects repo entries to be Item::Table, but toml_edit represents inline tables as Item::Value(Value::InlineTable). Manifest::from_toml accepts both, so lob edit can panic on a valid manifest. Fix should handle inline tables gracefully, matching find_circuit_mut behavior.

title: Non-USD Mouser prices parse as 100x USD amounts
description: Split from [[legion-of-bom-z8c]] finding 7. mouser.rs parse_price strips everything but ASCII digits and '.', so values like '1,48 EUR' become 148.0 and are later formatted as dollars. PriceBreak.currency is captured but unused. Fix should parse locale/currency safely and avoid aggregating or formatting non-USD prices as USD.

title: Dual: 4 decoupling near-misses survive the layout loop's global trade-off
description:
Residual from [[legion-of-bom-ku4]], filed separately because it is a different mechanism.

decouple::snap now does its job: 6 of 6 caps snapped, 0 skipped, 3.5-7.9mm pad-to-pin, against a
physical floor of ~6.6mm centre-to-centre. But the built board still shows 4 electrical rules
broken by 0.3-1.3mm:

  -1.3mm  C3 is 9.9mm from U2 (max 8.6)
  -0.9mm  C6 is 9.4mm from U3 (max 8.6)
  -0.5mm  C8 is 9.1mm from U2 (max 8.6)
  -0.3mm  C2 is 9.0mm from U1 (max 8.7)

WHY THE PROBE AND THE BOARD DISAGREE: the probe runs snap once over a one-shot EurorackPlacer
placement. A real build runs the layout loop — 6 attempts, snap inside each, legalize after,
and the winner chosen on TOTAL score across wirelength, critical length, vias, copper, unrouted
and rule penalty. An attempt with slightly worse decoupling can win on the other terms. So this
is the loop trading, not the pass failing.

WORTH ASKING BEFORE FIXING:
1. Is the trade correct? A 0.3mm miss on a loop-inductance heuristic may genuinely be worth
   fewer vias. The rule's own text says 'distance stands in for loop inductance' — it is a
   proxy, and proxies should not necessarily win ties.
2. If it is not correct, the lever is the rule penalty weight in the score, not snap.
3. Check whether legalize is moving these caps AFTER snap. It repairs Tier::Physical only, so it
   should not touch an electrical violation — but it can move a cap for an edge or overlap
   reason and land it further from its IC, with nothing re-running snap afterwards. That would
   be a real ordering bug rather than a trade-off, and it is the cheapest thing to check first.

Not urgent: the dual is DRC-clean and fully routed. This is quality, not buildability.

title: Layout mode is a per-invocation flag, not a per-circuit manifest field
description:
Follow-on from [[legion-of-bom-p6m]], which made guide/board/fab able to agree. This makes them agree BY CONSTRUCTION.

Today --mode is passed per command, defaulting to LAYOUT_MODE. Nothing stops someone running
lob fab --mode digital and then lob guide (analog), producing a guide that documents a
different board from the one manufactured. p6m closed the accidental version of that; this is
the deliberate version.

kit and panel already work the right way: declared once per circuit in lob.toml, with an
explicit flag as override. mode should join them — a slew limiter is an analog board as a
property of the circuit, not of the command line.

FIX: add  to the manifest's CircuitEntry (and Defaults), resolve it in resolve_circuit
the way kit already is, and let --mode override. build_one then stops passing a literal at all.

Small, and it removes the last way the two boards can disagree on cost function.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: Typo in the description above: the FIX line should read "add mode to the manifest CircuitEntry (and Defaults)". The field name was eaten by shell backtick expansion when this bead was filed.

title: lob run cannot simulate stereo circuits: phono_preamp and crossfader fail at SimConfig::infer
description:
FOUND WHILE FIXING THE DUAL'S SIMULATE PATH, and pre-existing — not caused by
that work. Two of the three other circuits in ~/src/puget-hardware have NEVER
had a working simulate stage, and neither has ever produced a .cir or .dat in
out/, which is the evidence that this is long-standing rather than new.

MEASURED TODAY:
  lob run circuits/phono_preamp/phono_preamp.py
    -> error: simulate stage failed: simulation needs a net named 'IN'
       (have: ... PHONO_L, PHONO_R, OUT_L, OUT_R, ...)
  lob run circuits/crossfader/crossfader.py
    -> error: simulate stage failed: simulation needs a net named 'IN'
       (have: ... INP_L_A, INP_L_B, INP_R_A, INP_R_B, OUT_L, OUT_R, ...)
  ls out/phono_preamp out/crossfader -> no .cir, no .dat, ever.

WHY. `SimConfig::infer` matches net names against a fixed candidate list
(INPUT_NETS / OUTPUT_NETS in crates/core/src/spice.rs). The dual's problem was
NUMBERED channels (SIG_IN1/SIG_IN2) and that is now handled by `channel_suffix`
/ `channel_nets` / `signal_channels`. These two are the L/R sibling of the same
problem and are NOT handled:
  * `OUT_L` is already in OUTPUT_NETS, so the outputs would resolve.
  * the inputs are `PHONO_L` and `INP_L_A`, which match no candidate at all.
    `IN_L` is in the list; `PHONO_L` and `INP_L_A` are not.

SO THE FIX IS NOT SIMPLY "ADD L/R SUFFIX HANDLING" — a stereo board's input net
can be named after the SOURCE (PHONO) rather than after the signal, and the
crossfader has two inputs per side (A and B) before any channel concept applies.
Worth deciding whether the answer is a wider candidate list, a per-circuit
override in lob.toml, or making the harness's I/O nets declarable by the circuit
itself. Guessing from names has now failed three times in three different ways.

WORTH DOING because it is the same seam that just unblocked the dual: once a
stereo circuit resolves its I/O, `signal_channels()` and the new
`check_channel_crosstalk` gate apply to it unchanged — a stereo preamp has
exactly the same "does L leak into R" question, and the crossfader shares op-amp
packages across channels the same way the dual shares the LM13700.

title: lob init: scaffold a circuits repo's .gitignore and report tracked generated files
description:
DONE 2026-07-28, filed for the record.

Every stage writes artifacts BESIDE its inputs — SKiDL drops .net/.erc/.log/_sklib.py next to the script, lob panel pcb writes a .kicad_pcb and a gerber directory next to the panel spec, ngspice leaves .dat, lob drc leaves -drc.rpt. So a repo accumulates outputs at the top level unless something says otherwise, and puget-hardware had 18 tracked generated files churning every rebuild — 16 of them panel gerbers.

crates/core/src/scaffold.rs holds the canonical list as data (pattern + why), so there is one source of truth rather than a template that drifts. lob init merges it into .gitignore between markers: the author's own rules are never touched, an older managed block is replaced in place so a lob upgrade brings new patterns without hand-merging, and re-running is a no-op. is_generated() answers the same question for tracked files.

It deliberately does NOT run git rm --cached. Untracking is a change to somebody's index; it prints the command and says the files stay on disk.

Verified on puget-hardware: all six output shapes ignored (panel gerbers dir + zip, panel kicad_pcb, -drc.rpt, .dat, out/), all five input shapes still tracked (circuit .py, panel .toml, lob.toml, brand assets, imported fab packages). Three tests: idempotent merge preserving author rules, in-place replacement of an older block, and input-vs-output classification.

FOLLOW-UP: 18 files in puget-hardware are still tracked and generated. The user needs to run the printed git rm -r --cached. Two of them (*:Zone.Identifier) are Windows download cruft rather than lob output, but equally should not be tracked.

title: Placement leaves ~4.6mm of the board's width unused down the right edge
description:
Noticed by the user from the top view, and it holds on the SHIPPING board, not just the ungated one:

  fab/slew_limiter.kicad_pcb   board x 133.26..163.74 (30.48mm, 6.0 HP), rightmost copper 159.11  -> 4.63mm unused
  slew_limiter.kicad_pcb       same outline, rightmost copper 157.78              -> 5.96mm unused

4.63mm is ~0.9 HP on a 6 HP board — about 15% of the width, on a module where width is the scarce resource and where [[legion-of-bom-m1b]] is about the board not fitting its declared 5 HP panel in the first place. If that strip were usable the board might fit the panel it was designed for.

Worth establishing before chasing it: is this the packer failing to use the space, or is it a legitimate consequence of the anchored panel column sitting where it does? The width sweep is suggestive — placement was byte-identical at 6, 8, 10 and 12 HP ([[legion-of-bom-qng]]), which says the packer does not respond to extra width at all. That is either a deliberate pack-from-one-edge strategy or a bug, and nobody has checked which.

Do not tune this before [[legion-of-bom-tsy.1]] lands. Compacting a placement that has no overlap rule just packs the overlaps tighter.

title: Rule constants are uncited magic numbers — trace them to IPC-2221 / Ott / MT-031
description:
The parts library already enforces provenance: PartRecord carries cited_page and a verified_by_human gate, because [[legion-of-bom-okm]] exists to stop numbers being drafted from memory. The layout rules have no equivalent — DECOUPLE_GAP_MM, EDGE_MARGIN_MM, the separation minima and the panel envelopes are constants with prose justifications and no source.

That is the same failure class the design guardrail memory was written about ("legion-of-bom must structurally prevent the LM13700-pinout-from-model-memory mistake"), and it matters more now that rules are about to drive the placer rather than just annotate it.

WANTED: each rule constant carries a citation the way a part does — standard clause or textbook section. Candidate sources, chosen for actually applying to an audio-band +/-12V Eurorack module rather than to GHz digital:

  - IPC-2221 — generic PCB design, the machine-readable one; conductor spacing vs voltage, hole-to-edge, annular ring. Directly sources the Tier::Physical numbers.
  - Henry Ott, Electromagnetic Compatibility Engineering (Wiley 2009) — grounding and plane integrity.
  - Analog Devices MT-031 (Kester/Bryant/Byrne), free PDF — star vs plane grounding for exactly this class of circuit.
  - AD Analog Dialogue decoupling tutorial (2017) — the loop-area argument behind [[legion-of-bom-5kv]].

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: high-speed signal integrity (controlled impedance, return-path discontinuity, stripline geometry). It does not apply at audio band and importing it would produce confident wrong rules. Revisit only when a Daisy lands ([[legion-of-bom-25z]]), where Bogatin becomes relevant.

Not every constant needs a standard — some are our own product decisions (panel finish, silk margins). Those should say so explicitly rather than look like they have a source.

title: Replace summing::snap with a high-impedance-node RULE the optimiser prices
description:
[[legion-of-bom-6yh]] measured summing::snap costing 5 DRC errors and 2 connections, with its original justification no longer reproducing. Deleting it leaves a real objective unrepresented, though: a summing junction is a high-impedance node and wants to be almost no copper. That objective belongs in the score, not in a pass that overrides placement.

WHY A RULE AND NOT A SNAP. The module doc in rules.rs already argues this, from the decoupling case: "Rules that mattered were expressed as weight bonuses inside the greedy placer, which meant they could be, and were, thrown away after the fact... A placement heuristic cannot fix a scoring problem." summing::snap is the same mistake in the other direction — it cannot be traded off at all, so it wins even when it costs five DRC errors.

WANTED: Rule::Proximity (or a node-length variant) from each op-amp inverting input to the passives on that node, Tier::Electrical, priced so it loses to Physical but beats wirelength. The deriver needs the pin-name data summing.rs already reads from the KiCad symbol library (is_amp_input), so the identification logic is reusable even if the placement pass is not.

NAME THE PROXY, per the rules module's standing caution: centre-to-centre millimetres is a stand-in for node capacitance and pickup area, and tightening the number does not straightforwardly buy a quieter node.

BLOCKED ON: deciding 6yh (delete vs guard). Do that first — this is the replacement, and it should be measured against a baseline with the pass already gone.

title: Parts library holds Mouser-shaped part numbers, so a non-Mouser order has nowhere to land
description:
house_parts.csv has one 'mpn' column, and in practice it holds three different kinds of string:

  - real Mouser part numbers with the vendor prefix: 667-ERJ-2RKF1003X, 81-GRM155R61E104KA7D, 604-WP937EGW, 710-61201021621, 612-TL1105SP-250
  - raw LCSC/JLC codes: C21190, C25803, C14663, C234182
  - manufacturer MPNs and outright placeholders: WQP-WQP518MA, RV9012NO-PA25B7.0, EUROPWR-10p (which is a FOOTPRINT name, not an orderable part)

So the column cannot answer 'what do I order, and from whom'. Two consequences seen live on 2026-07-27 sourcing the 2OPFM through-hole set ([[2opfm-50-board-run-jul-2026]]):

1. The user orders a good bit from DigiKey, and NOT ONE DigiKey part number exists anywhere in puget-hardware. That history is simply not captured, so the library keeps steering back to Mouser.
2. J1 (Eurorack power header) had NOTHING orderable behind it. The only 2x5 header in the library carrying a real MPN is Wurth 61201021621 — the shrouded/keyed type the user rejects ([[eurorack-power-header-must-not-be-shrouded]]). Every other row for that part says EUROPWR-10p, a footprint name. The user had to pick the part by search with no help from the tooling.

WANTED: a part record that can carry per-distributor numbers (manufacturer MPN as the key, plus Mouser/DigiKey/LCSC/boutique as separate fields), and a notion of supplier CLASS — catalogue distributor vs boutique/DIY. The 2OPFM THT set splits cleanly along that line: sliders and LEDs are catalogue parts, the Qingpu jacks and the RV9012 trimmer are Thonk-style boutique items that will never match a DigiKey or Mouser upload. Today that split has to be worked out by hand every time.

Relates to [[legion-of-bom-okm]] (parts library + human-verification gate) and [[legion-of-bom-b8c]] (imported BOMs without part numbers).

title: Place and rotate a logical block as a unit
description:
Drag a whole group; the parts keep their relative arrangement. Rotation is the interesting case — a rotated block needs its internal placements rotated about the block centroid, and back-side parts mirrored, which is the same coordinate care board.rs already documents for footprints (flip in the footprint frame first, then rotate; getting it backwards still yields a DRC-clean board that reserves the wrong space).

After the block lands, crate::decouple and crate::summing run as they do now — the pin-level work stays automatic.

title: Derive functional groups by clustering the attractor graph
description:
The netlist has no hierarchy (verified: no sheetpath, no @subcircuit), so groups must be derived. crate::analytical::attractors already builds the weighted graph — nets weighted 1/(k-1), decoupling bonds at 3.0, critical nets 6x. Cluster it and the summing amp {RA,RB,RF,RG,U2} should fall out on its own.

This is a second, uncontested use for analytical.rs: the graph model was never what failed in [[legion-of-bom-10k]] — the placement it produced was. Reuse the graph, not the placer.

Output is a SUGGESTION the author names and corrects, persisted per [[legion-of-bom-cll.1]]'s writer. Judge it on whether the groups match how a person describes the circuit (slew core, CV attenuverter, output buffer), not on a modularity score.

title: [epic] Logical-block placement — group the board internals and place them as units
description:
The other half of the placement split from [[legion-of-bom-cll]]: the user
places the control surface, and the board internals get placed as LOGICAL
BLOCKS rather than as 40 individual passives. Nobody hand-places 0603s, but
"put the summing amp here and the slew core there" is a judgement worth having.

THE PROBLEM THIS HAS TO SOLVE FIRST: there is no hierarchy to group by.
Checked on the real slew limiter — the netlist carries NO sheetpath, and
slew_limiter.py defines no @subcircuit blocks. So functional grouping has to
come from somewhere. Three sources, in the order they should be tried:

  1. DERIVE IT from connectivity. crate::analytical::attractors already builds
     the weighted graph (nets at 1/(k-1), decoupling bonds, critical multiplier)
     — clustering it should fall out as {RA, RB, RF, RG, U2} for the summing
     amp without anyone declaring anything. Available today; analytical.rs is
     in the tree and wired to nothing since [[legion-of-bom-10k]], and this is
     a second use for the part of it that was never in question.
  2. DECLARE IT in the placement file ([[groups]] name + refdes), seeded from
     (1) and then the author's to correct and name. A derived grouping is a
     suggestion; a named one is a decision.
  3. DECLARE IT IN SKIDL with @subcircuit so hierarchy flows from the source and
     the netlist's sheetpath carries it. Best long-term, and it is already
     [[legion-of-bom-tus.4]]. Needs the SKiDL sources rewritten, so not first.

THEN: place and rotate a block as a unit, and auto-place within the block, with
crate::decouple and crate::summing still doing the pin-level work after — those
two are now the measurably good part of the placer ([[legion-of-bom-yck]]).

Sequenced AFTER cll: the control surface is what blocks a shippable board
([[legion-of-bom-qng]]), and grouping is worth much less until a person can
place anything at all.

title: Capture a board's placement back into placement.toml (KiCad round-trip)
description:
The insurance policy, and cheap: capture an existing board's placement INTO a
placement.toml, so a layout done in KiCad round-trips into the format the
pipeline builds from instead of being stranded.

Both halves already exist:
  * guide::placements_from_board reads placements back out of a .kicad_pcb
  * panel::panel_from_board is the exact precedent — capture a shipped board's
    real configuration as a spec, and it is how the slew limiter fixture in
    crates/core/examples/fixtures was made

So this is: read the board, keep the parts with panel cutouts, flip board-frame
Y back to panel space (the inverse of PlacementFile::anchors), and emit
[controls] entries through the writer.

Worth doing even though the editor is the plan, for two reasons: it makes any
KiCad excursion non-destructive, and it gives the editor a realistic starting
file for the flagship board rather than a blank one.

STRETCH, and only if it falls out easily: infer patterns from captured
positions — three parts sharing an x at a constant y-pitch are a column, and
emitting them as one is strictly better than three coordinates. Do not force
it; a wrong inference is worse than none.

title: Live rule feedback while dragging (panel-hardware clearance, with the mm figure)
description:
Show the rules WHILE dragging, not after a rebuild.

rules::assess already returns, per rule, the subject and the margin in mm —
positive is slack, negative is broken. The dashboard already renders "Design
rules — N of M broken" from it. This wires the same call to the drag loop so a
panel-hardware collision is visible as it happens.

The rule that matters most here is the Physical separation between panel parts:
"panel hardware overlaps — knobs and nuts are bigger than the footprints under
them", with a real minimum derived from each part's cutout envelope. A knob
that fouls its neighbour is invisible in a footprint view and obvious in a
rule check, which is exactly the kind of thing a person placing by eye gets
wrong.

  * red/amber/green per selected part, and the offending pair highlighted
  * the mm figure shown, not just a colour — "J1 is 16.0mm from J2 (min 14.4mm)"
    is actionable, a red dot is not
  * evaluate on drag-end at minimum; on drag-move if it is fast enough for the
    part counts involved (5-8 panel parts, so it should be)

Deliberately NOT a gate: this is guidance while placing. The gates stay where
they are — rules::Tier::Physical in `lob fab` ([[legion-of-bom-670]]) and KiCad
DRC.

title: [bug] silkscreen text below JLCPCB's minimum — 0.4mm high, 0.05mm thick
description:
Surfaced by judging a DRC-clean board against JLCPCB capability
([[legion-of-bom-9zc]]). JLCPCB needs silk text >= 1.0mm high and >= 0.15mm
stroke. On out/slew_limiter's board:

    45x  h=1.00mm  thickness=0.15mm   ok (exactly at the limit)
    10x  h=1.27mm  thickness=0.15mm   ok
     1x  h=1.10mm  thickness=0.18mm   ok
     6x  h=0.40mm  thickness=0.060mm  TOO SMALL
     3x  h=0.40mm  thickness=0.051mm  TOO SMALL

which is exactly the 9x text_height + 9x text_thickness warnings KiCad reports
against the JLCPCB rule set.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE MORE THAN USUAL: this project ships hand-assembly build
guides and a kit model where the buyer solders the through-hole panel hardware
themselves, reading refdes off the silkscreen. Silk below the fab's minimum
comes back illegible or simply not printed. It is a warning in KiCad's severity
scheme so no gate refuses it, and nothing would have noticed.

Note the 45 items sitting at EXACTLY 1.00mm/0.15mm are at the limit with zero
margin -- worth nudging up as well, since fab tolerance eats that.

Find where the sub-millimetre text comes from: board.rs writes silk text with
thickness = size/6.0 (board.rs:2320), which at 0.4mm size gives 0.067mm. Check
whether these are our generated labels or reference/value text inherited from
the stock SMD footprints, and clamp to the fab minimum either way.
close_reason: kit-aware silk values (silk_overlap 4->1, silk_over_copper 4->2) + brand/rev/note legend; residual silk-over-pad and refdes auto-placement left open in the notes

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
CORRECTION — I was wrong; this bead's premise is a false positive of my own making. The 9 'undersized silk text' items are on B.Fab (6) and Cmts.User (3), which are documentation layers that are never manufactured. Every VISIBLE silkscreen text on the board is at or above JLCPCB's 1.0mm/0.15mm minimum. The warnings came from my probe .kicad_dru writing text_height/text_thickness with NO layer condition, so they matched Fab and Comments annotations too.

Re-measured with conditions on both sides (A.Layer and B.Layer restricted to F.SilkS/B.SilkS):
    was: 9 text_height + 9 text_thickness + 199 silk_overlap
    is:  0            + 0                + 4

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG WITH THE SILKSCREEN (real, on out/slew_limiter):
    4x silk_overlap, 4x silk_over_copper, 1x silk_edge_clearance
  and THREE of the four overlaps involve a Value field:
    Reference field of C2 || Value field of R4 (51k)
    Reference field of C1 || Value field of C2 (100nF)
    Segment of C2 on B.Silkscreen || Value field of R4 (51k)

  Values like '51k' and '100nF' are wider than the 0603 they label, so on a dense
  board they collide with the neighbours. BoardOptions::silk_values already
  exists and defaults to TRUE. Flipping it to false, measured:
    silk_overlap 4 -> 1, silk_over_copper 4 -> 2, board otherwise identical
    (score 523.8, 0 DRC errors, same placement)

  For this product that is close to free: JLCPCB pre-assembles the SMD parts and
  the buyer only solders THT panel hardware, so a value on a 0603's silk is read
  by nobody. Refdes is what the build guide points at.

The remaining silk_over_copper and the 45 texts sitting at EXACTLY 1.0mm/0.15mm
(zero margin for fab tolerance) are still worth a look — retitle this bead around
those rather than around text size.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
LANDED. Two changes, both in board.rs.

1. SILK VALUES ARE NOW KIT-AWARE. BoardOptions::silk_values went from bool to
   enum SilkValues { All, HandSoldered (default), None }. A part gets its value
   printed only when somebody will actually solder it, decided from the
   footprint itself: any thru_hole/np_thru_hole pad means hand assembly, since
   JLCPCB populates the SMD.

   Measured on the slew limiter, before -> after:
       silk_overlap       4 -> 1
       silk_over_copper   4 -> 2
       silk_edge_clearance 1 -> 1
   Placement, score (523.8) and DRC (0 errors) all unchanged -- this is silk
   only. Three of the four overlaps were a Value field ("51k", "100nF") wider
   than the 0603 it labelled, colliding with the neighbour.

2. SILKSCREEN LEGEND. New SilkLegend { brand, rev, note }, stacked under the
   title at the bottom edge, front silk (the back belongs to the logo). Brand
   and rev share a line; empty/whitespace entries vanish rather than leaving a
   stray separator. Rendered at 1.0mm -- silk_text_on strokes at size/6, so
   0.167mm, clear of JLCPCB's 0.15mm floor.

   Sources: brand from lob.toml [repo] brand (already there); rev and silk_note
   are new per-circuit manifest fields. `lob board` takes a bare path with no
   manifest entry, so it looks the legend up by stem when a lob.toml is
   discoverable and prints nothing when it is not.

   Verified on a real build: "Slew" / "Puget Audio . v1.2" / "VC slew limiter",
   and the legend added ZERO new violations (counts identical to the
   values-off measurement).

Tests: values_go_on_silk_only_for_the_parts_a_person_solders (SMD keeps its
value off silk, the same part as thru_hole keeps it on, both escape hatches
work) and the_legend_joins_brand_and_rev_and_drops_what_is_missing.

STILL OPEN on this board, not addressed here:
  * 2x silk_over_copper -- silk printed across a pad. Needs the silk clipped or
    the refdes nudged.
  * 1x silk_overlap and 1x silk_edge_clearance.
  * 45 silk items sit at EXACTLY 1.0mm/0.15mm, the fab floor with zero margin.
    Worth nudging to ~1.1mm since fab tolerance eats the difference.
  These want auto-placement of the refdes (try N/S/E/W, take the free side),
  which is a bigger piece of work than either change above.

title: layout loop exits on 'clean', so a first-pass-clean placement is never fine-tuned
description:
Noticed while landing [[legion-of-bom-d8t]]. run_layout_loop breaks as soon as
`unrouted == 0 && penalty <= 0.0`:

    // Stop when the board is both routable *and* rule-clean.

Under the greedy placer that almost never fired on attempt 1, so the repair
attempts ran and the loop kept the best of several. Under analytical placement
the slew limiter is clean on attempt 1 -- so the loop exits immediately and the
fine-tuning stage never runs at all.

That is exactly where the remaining gap sits: greedy's second (nudged) attempt
scores 539.1 on the slew board, analytical's first scores 553.4. Analytical wins
the placement and then loses the score because it is not allowed to iterate.

ASK: exit on "no longer improving", not on "clean". Something like -- keep going
while an attempt improves the score by more than some epsilon, with `clean` as
the floor rather than the finish line, and a cap on attempts. Costs routing time
on boards that are already clean, so it wants to be a flag or a budget rather
than unconditional.
close_reason: loop now exits on 'no longer improving' (patience 2); also fixed relax_key ranking an unrouted board above a routable one

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
DONE. run_layout_loop no longer exits on the first clean board; it keeps going
while attempts improve and stops after PATIENCE (2) consecutive ones that do
not, still bounded by max_iters.

A SECOND, WORSE BUG turned up while testing it, and it is the one that actually
mattered. relax_key ranked attempts by (broken tiers, preference cost), and
unrouted nets were priced only inside the preference cost, at 50 each
(CostWeights::unrouted). On daisy_panel_demo the loop compared:

    412.4 with TWO unconnected nets   vs   739.6 fully routed

and returned the broken one, because 2x50 is cheaper than 327mm of wirelength.
The loop was choosing an unfabricable board on purpose. layout.rs's own module
doc claimed "unrouted dominates so a routable board always beats a
tighter-but-broken one" -- it did not. Fixed: unrouted is now a term in
relax_key, above preference and below the rule tiers, so no wirelength buys a
net. Test: no_amount_of_wirelength_buys_an_unrouted_net.

MEASURED (max_iters=6, both placers, all 12 netlists in out/):
  * every board still ends 0-unrouted where it did before
  * daisy_panel_demo 315.3 -> 290.8, vbom 35.1 -> 24.8, rectifier 19.1 -> 17.9
  * most boards now run 3 iterations instead of 1-2 (patience), so a `lob run`
    costs ~2 extra place+route passes. More budget buys nothing: 12 and 20
    iterations score identically to 6 on every board tried.

ALSO TRIED AND REMOVED: a Placer::candidates seam letting the placer offer its
whole spreading trajectory for the loop to route and rank. Sound in principle --
the placer cannot rank its own rounds without routing them -- but measured, it
LOST to simply nudging the first one on 4 of 12 boards and tied on the rest.
The rounds are one solve at six spreading strengths, so they explore far less
than a perturbation does. Reverted; the reasoning is recorded on SeededPlacer::
trajectory so it is not re-attempted blind.

title: placement: daisy_panel_demo scores 23% worse under analytical placement
description:
The one regression from [[legion-of-bom-d8t]]. Single placement pass, no repair:
greedy 257.2 / 0 unrouted, analytical 412.4 / 2 unrouted. Through the full
6-iteration loop the repair recovers routability and both are DRC-clean, but
analytical still scores 315.3 vs 257.2 -- 23% worse.

WHY IT IS PROBABLY THIS BOARD. daisy_panel_demo has NO anchored parts in the
configuration it was measured in (the panel fixture used was opamp's, which has
zero cutouts -- the repo has no real panel spec for this circuit). With nothing
fixed, the analytical stage has no boundary condition and contributes nothing:
every part falls back to its home (an even spread) and the packing decides. The
greedy placer's sequential centroid seeding is a genuinely decent constructive
heuristic in exactly that situation.

CAVEAT ON THE MEASUREMENT: board_preview's own doc warns that made-up panel
configurations mislead placement comparisons, and this is one. Before chasing
this, capture a REAL panel spec for the board (examples/panel_from_pcb) and
re-measure -- it may not reproduce once the parts are anchored.

IF IT DOES REPRODUCE, the honest fix is spreading that does not depend on
anchors: a density/force term (Kraftwerk) rather than the pseudo-anchor walk,
which needs something fixed to walk away from. Gauge-fixing (pin the
most-connected part) was tried and lost on 7 of 10 circuits -- see the d8t
comment; do not re-try it without new evidence.
close_reason: narrowed 23% -> 13% by fixing the loop's ranking (lso); the density theory in the bead was measured and disproved. Residual gap folded into legion-of-bom-x9k

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
NARROWED, NOT ELIMINATED -- and the investigation turned up something bigger
(see [[legion-of-bom-x9k]]).

FIRST, the caveat in this bead is settled: the measurement WAS fair.
daisy_panel_demo has no panel hardware at all -- 8 caps, 4 resistors, one Daisy
Seed module. There is nothing to anchor and no real panel spec to capture, so
the empty-panel configuration is the only one it has.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG. Not the placer. The layout loop's ranking. relax_key
priced unrouted nets at 50 each inside the preference cost, so on this board it
preferred 412.4-with-2-unconnected-nets to 739.6-fully-routed and returned the
broken one. Fixed under [[legion-of-bom-lso]], along with the exit-on-first-clean
rule. daisy_panel_demo: 315.3 -> 290.8, still 0 unrouted.

Remaining gap to greedy on this board: 257.2 vs 290.8, i.e. 13% (was 23%).

WHY THE SPREADING ROUNDS DO NOT EXPLAIN IT -- the theory in this bead was that
an unanchored board needs a density/force spreading term. Measured, and no:
the rounds this board produces all pack to essentially the SAME density (0.72
then 0.89-0.90 for every later round), and yet one routes and another does not.
Two arrangements at identical occupancy, 30% apart in wirelength, and it is the
LONGER one that routes. Density does not separate them, so a density term would
not have chosen between them. Do not build Kraftwerk spreading on this evidence.

Handing the whole trajectory to the loop to route and rank was tried -- see the
lso comment -- and lost. Nudging the placer's first answer explores better.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: Correction: the decision bead is [[legion-of-bom-10k]], not x9k (id guessed before filing).

title: daughterboard on ribbon cable + headers (first case: 3PDT bypass board)
description:
Support a DAUGHTERBOARD attached to a main PCB by ribbon cable and headers, as a first-class thing the pipeline understands: two boards, a connector on each, a cable between them, one BOM, one build guide.

FIRST CONCRETE CASE, from the user: a 3PDT bypass daughterboard for pedals. The 3PDT carries the switching; the daughterboard carries the switch, the LED and the jack wiring, and a ribbon lands it on the main board. That is a real product shape and a good forcing function -- it needs board-to-board connectors, a cable as a BOM line, and a guide that explains which way round the ribbon goes.

DESIGN NOTE captured with it: ground the effect INPUT when bypassed. Cheap, and the usual reason is that a floating input on a high-gain effect picks up hum and lets the bypassed circuit bleed or oscillate into the shared ground.

CAVEAT ON THAT NOTE -- the source says "possible upside, and no downside (that I have ever seen)... it costs nothing, has no tradeoff". Broadly sound but not unconditional, and worth checking per circuit before we bake it into a template:
  * grounding through the input coupling cap changes what that cap is charged to, so re-engaging can thump on circuits with a large cap and a high-impedance bias point. Usually grounding REDUCES pop, occasionally it moves it.
  * effects that need to stay settled while bypassed (long delays/reverbs with feedback, anything with an envelope follower or a bias servo) can behave differently on re-engage.
  * it is wrong for a buffered send where the "effect" is feeding something else downstream.
So: default it ON in any bypass template we ship, make it a switch, and say why.

RELATED: [[legion-of-bom-25z]] is the sub-board/board-to-board header epic (Daisy as a placed module, 2-board stack). This shares the connector and BOM machinery but differs in that the two boards are CABLED rather than stacked, so the mechanical relationship is loose -- no standoff/height checking, but the cable needs a length and an orientation key.

NOT EURORACK: this one is for the pedals side of the repo.

title: panel: toggle cutout is 6.5mm, real sub-mini toggles need 4.95mm
description:
Found while sourcing the RANGE switch for the slew limiter.

TOGGLE_MM = 6.5 (panel.rs:120) drives ControlKind::Switch cutouts. The Dailywell DW5 sub-mini toggle Thonk sells (2MD6T1B1M2QES) specifies a panel hole of:

  diameter  4.95mm  (0.195in)
  with a flat at 4.55mm (0.179in) for anti-rotation
  bushing thread 10-48 UNS-2A

So our hole is 1.55mm oversized. A switch in a hole that loose sits crooked and the nut has to do all the work -- and the D-flat that stops it rotating is missing entirely, so it WILL rotate in use.

FIX: TOGGLE_MM -> 4.95, and consider a D-shaped cutout (CutoutShape has RoundedRect; a circle-with-flat is a new shape, or approximate). Check the Alpha/other toggles Thonk sells before settling on one number -- the DWB "mini" range is a different size to the DW "sub-mini" range, so the vocabulary may need both.

Same class of error as [[legion-of-bom-3s8]] (1U hole inset unverified): panel geometry taken from a plausible number rather than a datasheet.
notes:
REFRAMED after sourcing two real candidates. There is no single correct number -- the hole follows the part:

  Dailywell 2MD6T1B1M2QES (Thonk DW5)   4.95mm dia + 4.55mm flat, 10-48 UNS bushing
  E-Switch 100DP6T1B1M1QEH               6.35mm dia, 1/4-40 bushing

Our TOGGLE_MM = 6.5 is badly wrong for the Dailywell (1.55mm oversize) and very nearly right for the E-Switch (0.15mm over). So the bug is not "6.5 is the wrong constant", it is "a single constant cannot be right" -- BuiltinCutouts needs per-part cutout geometry keyed off the MPN, which is what CutoutSource::cutout(mpn, footprint) already takes an mpn for but never uses.

That also makes this a parts-library question: the cutout dimensions belong WITH the part, same standing rule as [[legion-of-bom-okm]]. Until then, at minimum add a second toggle entry so both bushing sizes are expressible.

Anti-rotation flat: the Dailywell needs a D-shaped hole. CutoutShape has no such variant.

title: panel: no slide/fader cutout type
description:
From puget-hardware/lob-gaps.md B3 (medium).

Cutout vocabulary is rotary (Alpha9mm), Thonkiconn, LED and toggle only. A slide pot -- the crossfader fader, Bourns PTA -- gets mapped to a 9mm ROUND HOLE, which is not a hole you can fit a fader through. Repro: crossfader_panel.toml has RV1 anchored as Alpha9mm with a warning comment.

ASK: a slot/slide cutout type carrying length plus orientation. CutoutShape already has RoundedRect, so the shape exists; what is missing is a ControlKind + BuiltinCutouts entry and an envelope, plus a footprint mapping so footprint_shape resolves a slide pot to it.

Blocks the crossfader, which is a confirmed 1U design using a real slide pot.

title: route: autorouter leaves nets unrouted on dense 2-layer boards
description:
From puget-hardware/lob-gaps.md C1 (medium). The user notes this is expected of a simple router and files it for a rip-up/retry pass or a documented handoff.

The seeded router plateaus and hands nets off "for manual routing", after which DRC blocks fab. Repro: crossfader, 44 parts -- 6 nets unrouted at 6 iterations, still 5 at 40. DRC 6 errors, all unconnected_items, and lob fab refuses.

ASK: either a rip-up-and-retry pass, or -- more honestly for now -- a documented manual-routing handoff so a board with known-unrouted nets can still reach fab with the user having explicitly accepted them. Today the pipeline just stops.
notes:
DIAGNOSED, and it is mostly NOT the router. Attempted fix made it worse and was reverted.

WHAT ACTUALLY FAILS. On the 8 HP slew limiter the router leaves exactly ONE real unconnected net: CTRL_FB between RG.1 and U2.13. (GND also reports unresolved but the pour covers it, so it is not a DRC error once zones are filled.)

WHY. CTRL_FB, CTRL_SUM and friends are the summing amps feedback network -- four resistors that belong against U2 pins 12/13/14. SeededPlacer seeds each free part at the CENTROID of its nets, and RA touches RATE_CV (at RV1, top of board) as well as CTRL_SUM (at U2), so its centroid is halfway between. Measured distance from U2:

   RA 45.45mm   RB 21.71mm   RF 21.49mm   RG 11.33mm

A feedback resistor 45mm from its op-amp on a two-layer board is not a routing problem. It is also electrically wrong: an inverting input is a virtual-ground summing node, high impedance, and a long trace there is an antenna.

WHAT I TRIED. A feedback_bonus mirroring decoupling_bonus -- strong attractor edges between a passive and the IC on any net touching <= 3 parts. REVERTED: it went 5 errors -> 7 and broke a CRITICAL net (SLEW_NODE could not reach U1.7). The rule is too broad. SLEW_NODE, IABC and others all match "small net touching an IC", so the greedy placer ends up with a dozen competing max-strength pulls and satisfies none.

WHAT WOULD WORK. Pin-level knowledge, not net-size heuristics: pull a passive to the specific PIN it connects to, and only for genuinely high-impedance nodes -- an op-amps inverting input. We can now identify those: SymbolGraphics::pin_names carries the "-" name (from [[legion-of-bom-sto]]), and PartFacts::pin_offsets carries the geometry (from [[legion-of-bom-22c]]). So the ingredients exist; it wants a snap pass like crate::decouple rather than an adjacency weight, because "against this pin" is a position, not a pull.

Router improvements that ARE still worth doing, separately: the rip-up loop only permutes net ORDER (topo constraints), it never changes the cost landscape. Negotiated congestion (PathFinder: allow overlap at a penalty, accumulate history cost per cell, rip up and re-route) is the standard answer and would help the genuinely congested cases. But it would not have fixed this one.
close_reason: crate::summing landed: CTRL_FB and CTRL_SUM route at every width; unconnected 4->1 at 10 HP. Tight-board packing tradeoff noted for follow-up

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
BUILT — crate::summing, landed in c93bab4. This is the pass this bead specified:
pin-level, position not pull, shaped like crate::decouple.

Pins come from the SYMBOL as this bead predicted: read_symbol_graphics gives
Amplifier_Operational:TL074 pin 13 = "-", pin 12 = "+", LM13700 pins 4/13 = "-".
PartFacts::pin_offsets supplies the geometry. Both ingredients were exactly
where this bead said they would be.

Measured on the real puget-hardware netlist, unconnected nets before -> after:
     6 HP   9 -> 5
     8 HP   4 -> 2
    10 HP   4 -> 1     (total DRC errors 4 -> 1)

CTRL_FB and CTRL_SUM — the two connections that failed at EVERY width and
blocked [[legion-of-bom-qng]] — now route.

The prediction in this bead that turned out to matter most: "it wants a snap
pass like crate::decouple rather than an adjacency weight, because 'against this
pin' is a position, not a pull." Correct, and the reason is now measurable:
at 8 HP and 10 HP the placer produced IDENTICAL placements with RA 43.5mm from
U2, because RA is tied to RATE_CV at an anchored pot and to CTRL_SUM at U2 — its
optimum is the midpoint of two fixed points. No weight moves a midpoint.

THREE WAYS THE PASS WAS INITIALLY TOO BROAD, all guarded now, all worth
remembering because they are the same failure this bead's history keeps hitting:
  1. GND is an op-amp input net (U2 pin 10 = +inC on a unity-gain stage), so the
     first version dragged every cap on GND onto one pin and undid decouple.
     Supply rails excluded.
  2. A node with a crowd on it is a bus. Capped at 3 movable passives.
  3. A pin on a package's outward face near the board edge points OFF the board;
     stepping out from it put parts in space, 3e6 of physical penalty at 6 HP.
     Now outline-bounded, and a part that will not fit is left alone + reported.

STILL OPEN: at 6 and 8 HP the pass trades unconnected nets for physical DRC
(clearance, courtyard overlap, mask bridge) because it packs hard against the IC
on a board with no spare room. The queue geometry (PAD_GAP_MM 1.2, parts stacked
outward from the pin) wants tuning against the legalizer.

title: sim: single IN/OUT convention cannot express stereo or control sweeps
description:
From puget-hardware/lob-gaps.md A4 (medium).

Two-channel boards (phono, crossfader) have no single IN. And the crossfaders real test is a DC SWEEP OF THE FADE CONTROL against output, not a signal pass-through -- a different analysis shape entirely. Repro: crossfader_control.cir (DC sweep) plus crossfader_signalpath.cir are hand decks for exactly this.

ASK: mostly falls out of the [circuit.sim] table in [[legion-of-bom-A3]]. Also consider emitting the circuit as a reusable .subckt so an external harness can wrap the GENERATED topology -- that kills topology drift even for analyses lob does not own.
notes: The [circuit.sim] table referenced above is [[legion-of-bom-5j6]].

title: pot swap to RV9012NO-PA25B7.0: value and footprint both change
description:
User picked RV9012NO-PA25B7.0 for the attenuverter pot, from the SuperSynthesis fab packages. Two things to settle before swapping, because neither is a like-for-like substitution:

1. VALUE. The SuperSynthesis BOMs describe it as "Tall Trimmer 10k". RV2 is currently 100k, and the circuit comment says why: "high enough not to load the CV source". A 10k pot across a CV input is a 10k load, which will sag another modules output. If the swap goes ahead at 10k that is a deliberate loading choice, not a detail.

2. FOOTPRINT. RV1/RV2 are on Potentiometer_THT:Potentiometer_Alpha_RD901F-40-00D_Single_Vertical. RV9012 is a different body and pinout, so this changes the board footprint AND the panel cutout envelope (BuiltinCutouts Alpha9mm), which feeds min_panel_hp and every derived panel.

3. It is listed against R-designators under JLC assembly in 2opfm/eg/tvca, which is what a trimmer looks like in a BOM, not a panel control. Worth confirming this is really the panel pot SuperSynthesis fit rather than their onboard trim.

Where the MPN goes: slew_limiter.py Part() carries no mpn field today, so this needs either the SKiDL part to declare one or a parts-library record -- the latter matches the standing rule that a components data travels with the component. See [[legion-of-bom-okm]].
notes:
VALUE CONCERN WITHDRAWN. Asked whether 10k works with the op-amp attenuverter: yes, and it is the better choice.

In the passive circuit the wiper feeds R5 directly, so the pots own output impedance (up to R/4 = 25k at mid-rotation for 100k) sits in series with R5 and makes CV depth interact with knob position -- which is why 100k was chosen. In the op-amp topology the wiper drives a high-Z non-inverting input, so that interaction vanishes and the op-amp output drives R5 stiffly. Depth becomes linear.

Gain is set by the two resistors, not the pot: Vout = W(1 + R2/R1) - CV(R2/R1), and with R1 = R2 that is 2W - CV, sweeping -CV / 0 / +CV. Pot value is independent of them. 10k gives lower Johnson noise and less leakage sensitivity than 100k.

Only consequence is a 10k load on the patched CV source, which any buffered Eurorack output drives without trouble.

STILL OPEN on this bead: whether RV9012NO-PA25B7.0 is a panel control at all (listed as a trimmer against R-designators under JLC assembly) and the footprint/cutout change. Those are mechanical, not electrical.

title: lob panel derive: width from minimum_hp but positions from the built board
description:
Found while checking the new panel art on puget slew_limiter.

`lob panel derive slew_limiter.py` prints:
  auto width: minimum 5 HP
  from the built board (out/slew_limiter/slew_limiter.kicad_pcb) - 5 cutout(s) at their real positions

It takes the WIDTH from minimum_hp (5 HP) and the POSITIONS from a board that was laid out against an 8 HP panel. The two disagree, and the result has overlapping hardware: RV2 lands at y=73.9 and J1 at y=67.0, 6.9mm apart, where a 9mm pot needs ~14mm and a jack ~9mm. Rendered the panel PCB and the IN jack sits inside the CV AMT pot cutout.

Either the width should come from the board too (it is the master, per bjd), or positions should be re-derived when the width changes. Silently mixing the two produces a spec that cannot be built.

Repro: cd puget-hardware && lob panel derive slew_limiter.py, then lob panel pcb on the result and look at it.
close_reason:
Fixed, but the filed diagnosis was wrong on both counts. The board IS 5.00 HP so width and positions agreed, and the 6.9mm reading was pin-1-to-jack rather than shaft-to-jack.

REAL FAULT: guide::parse_board documents cx/cy as "board-space centre" and sets them to the footprint ORIGIN. An Alpha pots origin is pin 1, so panel_from_board drilled pot holes off the shaft -- RV1/RV2 landed at x=10.2 on a panel whose jacks were at 12.7, i.e. 2.5mm left of centre. And the reverse path (cutout -> placement) already subtracts the offset, so board -> panel -> board drifted a part by one offset per trip. The round-trip test passed because both ends were consistently wrong.

panel_from_board now maps the courtyard bbox centre. Re-derived on puget slew_limiter: all cutouts centre on 12.7, spacing 20 / 18.4 / 16 / 16mm, panel PCB renders with no overlapping holes.

ALSO LANDED: Rule::Separation (panel hardware judged on panel envelopes, Physical tier), and Placer::anchored() + legalize_pinning so legalization can never slide a panel control off its cutout -- it reports instead. Tests for both.

title: IC pin names: KiCad leaves the most useful ones unnamed (IABC, OUT)
description:
Fallout from sto. The schematic now shows every pin name KiCad declares, but KiCad declares fewer than the bead assumed.

Ground truth, read from Amplifier_Operational.kicad_sym: LM13700 names pins 2/15 DIODE_BIAS, 3/14 +, 4/13 -, 6 V-, 11 V+. Pins 1, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 16 are named ~ (KiCad explicit no-name).

So the two pins stos headline example wanted are the two we cannot get: pin 1 IABC (the bias input the RATE pot drives) and pin 5 (the OTA output). On slew_limiter U1 now reads 3 +, 4 -, and 1 / 5 / 7 / 8 stay bare. Half the topology is legible, the interesting half is not.

The names exist in the datasheet, not the symbol, so the source has to be a parts library carrying verified pinouts per MPN -- which is the Dolt parts library seam, and matches the standing rule that a components data travels WITH the component rather than being special-cased. See [[legion-of-bom-okm]].

WORK: resolve pin function names through the parts library, falling back to the KiCad symbol. Then a boxed IC can read 1 IABC / 5 OUT.

title: harness: examples/board_preview is unrepresentative for DRC-level conclusions
description:
It derives its own panel with derive_panel, which stacks every control in one idealised centred column. Its boards carry ~69 DRC errors (24 tracks_crossing, 25 unconnected_items, 13 solder_mask_bridge) where the SHIPPED slew_limiter board carries 5, all unconnected_items.

So it is fine for placement-level A/B against itself — same harness before and after a change — and useless for judging whether a board is buildable or how many DRC errors a width really has. It has now misled me twice: once by passing no anchors at all (fixed), and once by making 4 HP vs 5 HP DRC comparisons look meaningful when the router was flailing at both widths for unrelated reasons.

FIX: build the harness against a real declared panel spec. slew_limiter's lives in the circuits repo, not here, so this probably means either checking in a representative panel spec as a fixture or pointing the harness at a circuits-repo path. Until then, put a warning at the top of the example saying what it is and is not good for.
close_reason:
Fixed. Three things were wrong, in increasing order of impact:

1. It passed no anchors (fixed earlier).
2. It derived its own idealised panel. Now it builds against a real declared spec, defaulting to examples/fixtures/slew_limiter_panel.toml, captured off the SHIPPED board via the new panel_from_pcb example. That revealed the shipped board is 8 HP -- every 4 vs 5 HP DRC comparison I had been drawing was at a width nothing ships at.
3. It overrode the router with MstRouter. BoardOptions::new defaults to GridRouter and the CLI never overrides it, so the harness was measuring a router that ships nowhere. This was most of the gap: 16 tracks_crossing and 25 unconnected_items were the MST connector, not placement.

Harness now reports DRC: 0 errors, against the shipped board 5. It is representative and can be trusted for DRC-level conclusions -- which unblocks t5t (minimum_hp routability), the whole point of the bead.

title: rules: the decoupling rule measures distance, but the objective is loop inductance
notes:
FIRST SLICE DONE (commit f35644b): the rule now names itself a proxy. DECOUPLE_GAP_MM's docs state the objective is loop inductance and that distance is a stand-in, with an explicit 'do not tighten this number expecting better decoupling'; the rule's own 'why' text says the same, so it reaches the guide and the dashboard panel. The rules module doc generalises it — every electrical rule will have this gap between what a placement can see and what matters, and each should name its proxy.

The two better versions remain open, unchanged: cap-to-POWER-PIN rather than cap-to-centre (blocked on per-pad net in PartFacts), and true loop area (needs the routed board, probably not worth it).
PARTLY ADDRESSED by legion-of-bom-22c: crate::decouple::snap now PLACES each bypass cap against the power pin it bypasses (pad-to-pin 10.0mm -> 4.5mm on slew_limiter), so the physical objective is met by construction rather than by scoring.

What remains here is exactly the framing this bead was filed for: the RULE still measures cap-centre to IC-centre. It now passes comfortably, which is worse than failing -- a regression in the snap pass would hide behind a green rule. Making Proximity measure pad-to-pin (PartFacts::pin_offsets now carries the geometry needed) changes thresholds and the layout loop scoring, so it was deliberately not bundled into the fix.

title: photos: add Thonk as a product-photo source for DIY-domain parts
description: LCSC/EasyEDA pictures catalog electronics well and DIY panel hardware badly (a Thonkiconn jack, an Alpha 9mm pot, jack nuts). Thonk is our supplier and runs WooCommerce: GET /wp-json/wp/v2/product?search=X&per_page=N&_embed=wp:featuredmedia returns titles, product links and featured images with a sizes map (woocommerce_thumbnail 700x700). Verified 2026-07-26. Search is fuzzy — LM13700 returns an unrelated VCA kit — so it needs a relevance guard on the title before a photo is accepted.

Verified live: real photos for the Thonkiconn jacks, Alpha 9mm T18 pot, shrouded 2x5 power header and the jack nuts bag. title_matches guards against the fuzzy search — needs two thirds of the meaningful query words in the title, which is what stops 'eurorack power header shrouded' from returning a photo of power CABLES and LM13700 from returning an unrelated VCA kit. examples/thonk_probe.rs re-checks the supplier API on demand.

title: viewer: Flip duplicates Top/Bottom on renders and is the only mirror on gerbers
description: hasSide is true only for subject=pcb AND mode=render, so a photoreal board has both Top/Bottom and Flip (redundant), while gerber and board-layout have only Flip. Unify on one Side control across every pcb view: on a render it selects the rendered side; on layout/gerber it mirrors the composite (which is what viewing from the bottom means). Delete Flip.
close_reason: Side now applies to every pcb view: on a render the server draws that face, on layout/gerber the composite is mirrored (which is what viewing from the bottom means). Flip deleted.

title: viewer: board renders take ~4.7s because kicad-cli runs at --quality high
description: Measured on slew_limiter, 1600x1200: --quality high 4.74s, --quality basic 0.92s (5.1x). render_board_png hardcodes high. The printed guide wants high; the interactive viewer does not. Make quality a parameter and let the web viewer ask for basic.
close_reason: render_board_png takes a Quality; the web viewer asks for Basic (0.69s measured) and the printed guide keeps High (4.69s). Quality is in the scratch filename so a dashboard render and a build render can't clobber each other.

title: viewer: SMD toggle silently does nothing when the visible side has no SMD parts
description: Diagnosed: the plumbing is correct end to end. strip_smd drops 14 footprints to 6 on slew_limiter, the ?smd=0 query reaches render_view, the cache key differs, and the bottom render visibly loses every SMD pad. The failure is UX: slew_limiter's SMD is all on the BACK, and the viewer opens on board-top, so toggling the box changes nothing visible and reads as broken.
