title: Imported BOMs without part numbers: suggest MPNs from value + package
description:
Measured across the five SuperSynthesis packages: only 2OPFM fills its distributor column (20/24 lines). PHRSR, SCANNER, TVCA and EG leave it blank entirely, so their BOMs cannot be priced or ordered as imported — 20, 15, 16 and 32 lines respectively with nothing to look up.

Everything needed already exists: [[legion-of-bom-lrr]] built suggest_mpns(part) which turns value + footprint into ranked candidates via Mouser keyword search, and an imported BOM line carries exactly that (value "10uF 50v", footprint "CAP_1206"). So: for an imported circuit with blank part numbers, run the same suggestion path, and — per the okm human-verification gate — SUGGEST rather than assign. Surface candidates in the Visual BOM so the builder confirms one, and write the confirmed choice back to the package or a sidecar.

Package strings need a little normalising first: these are "0603 CAP", "CAP_1206", "SOD-323", not clean footprint names — import::package_size_mm and package_is_through_hole already read them, so the same vocabulary can feed the query builder. Follows [[legion-of-bom-u7p]].
notes:
CLI SHIPPED: lob import repair <package> [--search] [--limit N]. core/bom_repair.rs classifies the comment column into Mpn / Value / Label, which is the crux — the column does three jobs at once. Ordering rules earned against real data: (1) FIRST TOKEN decides (authors append ratings/tolerance/notes: '10uF 50v', '10k 0603 1%'); (2) value tested BEFORE mpn ('10uF' satisfies both heuristics, only one is true); (3) mpn tested BEFORE the connector rule (else a jack with a real MPN, WQP-WQP518MA, is thrown away as a signal label). Wrong order gave 28/111 unsourceable; right order gives 12, and those 12 genuinely are (DNP + jacks named CV/OUT/TRIG). Across the 5 packages: 63 lines carry an MPN in the comment, 36 are searchable, 12 not. PHRSR alone: 0 -> 12 recovered outright (STM32F334K8, TL072D, AMS1117-3.3, 1N4148WS, WQP-WQP518MA...) + 8 searchable. sourcing::suggest_by_keyword added so an imported line can reuse the lrr search without a Part. 10 unit tests. Gates: 253 core + 11 web, fmt/clippy clean.

HONEST LIMIT — the --search path is wired and returns results, but the RESULTS ARE POOR for generic passives: '10uF capacitor 1206' returns Visaton speaker caps, '100k resistor 0603' returns MOX power resistors, all 0 stock. This is the keyword-noise limitation lrr already documented; it needs the value-parse tightening noted there (compare parsed ohms/farads against each candidate, and filter by package) before it is trustworthy. Comment RECOVERY is solid and is where the value is today.

NOT DONE: (a) no UI surface — the user asked for UI and CLI; the dashboard BOM does not yet show recovered/suggested MPNs or let you confirm one; (b) nothing writes the confirmed MPN back to the package or a sidecar; (c) the okm verification gate is not applied to a recovered number.

title: Dashboard: rebuild button (run lob build from the UI)
description:
User: "we do not have a rebuild button in the UI." The workspace polls and shows a rebuild within ~2.5s, but you still have to go to a terminal to trigger one. Add a button that runs the build for the circuit being viewed and streams or reports its result.

Notes: the server already shells out for renders, so running a build is the same shape, but it is longer (SKiDL + KiCad + DRC) and mutates out/, so it needs progress rather than a spinner, and must not run twice concurrently for one circuit. Errors matter here — a failed build (DRC errors, missing tool) is the normal case while iterating, so surface the message rather than a bare failure. For an imported circuit there is nothing to build; the button should not appear. Discovered from [[legion-of-bom-awu]].
close_reason: Closed

title: THT drill clearance: are footprint drills big enough for the real part?
description:
User: "I do not think the pot holes (not the pins) but the holders are drilled big enough."

WHAT I VERIFIED (so this is not the pipeline): our gerbers faithfully reproduce the KiCad footprint. Potentiometer_Alpha_RD901F-40-00D_Single_Vertical declares the two mounting lugs as (drill oval 1.1 1.8) and pins 1-3 as (drill 1). Our Excellon emits exactly that: tool T3 = 1.1mm routed 0.7mm via G85, giving a 1.1 x 1.8mm slot, four of them (2 pots x 2 lugs). Nothing is dropped or shrunk.

SO THE QUESTION IS UPSTREAM: is the KiCad footprint tight for the physical Alpha 9mm pot? Needs a caliper on the real part (lug cross-section) and on a fab-house sample, which is exactly the verified mechanical data the parts library is meant to carry — see [[legion-of-bom-okm]].

LIKELY REAL FIX, once measured, is a DFM rule rather than a per-footprint edit: a drill-oversize allowance on through-hole pads (fab houses typically want lead diameter + 0.2-0.3mm, and plating shrinks a hole further). That belongs in the declarative rule work [[legion-of-bom-avg]] as a physical-tier constraint, applied at fab export so it cannot be forgotten, and reported so the builder sees what was widened and why. Also worth a DFM check that no slot is below the house minimum. Related: [[legion-of-bom-j54.7]].

title: Eagle import (.brd/.sch) — Mutable Instruments and friends
description:
User: "Maybe eagle_brd from Mutables." Eagle is a much better import target than DipTrace: since v6 .brd/.sch are XML with a published DTD, so components, nets, footprints and placement are all directly readable — meaning a real netlist, and therefore schematic view, ERC and simulation, not just layout re-use.

TWO ROUTES: (a) parse the XML ourselves into the Circuit model — no new dependency, full control, and it fits the CircuitSource seam; (b) shell out to KiCad, which ships an Eagle importer, then read the resulting .kicad_pcb/.kicad_sch with the parsers we already have. (b) is less code and reuses proven conversion, but adds a kicad-cli dependency for import and must degrade gracefully when absent.

Mutable Instruments hardware is open (cc-by-sa) and Eagle-based, so this unlocks a well-known body of designs. Distinct from [[legion-of-bom-u7p]] (fab-package import, layout only, no nets).
notes:
SHIPPED (first slice): lob import eagle <sch> [--board <brd>] [--skidl <out>]. core/eagle.rs — hand-rolled XML scanner (handles '>' inside quoted attrs), parse_schematic -> real Circuit with nets from <net>/<segment>/<pinref>, parts from <part> resolved to a package via the file's own library/deviceset/device chain; parse_board -> EaglePlacement (x/y/rot, 'MR90' = mirrored to back); to_skidl -> a runnable-looking SKiDL script so an import becomes an editable definition. Judgement calls: (1) schematic symbols with no package (frames, GND/supply markers) are NOT components — skipped, counted, and their pins excluded since a GND symbol's pin IS the net; (2) unknown packages pass through as 'eagle:<name>' and are reported, never guessed — but AMBIGUOUS ones (Eagle names passives by bare size, '0603') are settled by the refdes, since R14/C9 say what the package doesn't. VERIFIED on Mutable Instruments: grids 106 parts/70 nets/108 placements, peaks 90/69, ripples 105/63, tides 139/98; generated SKiDL for grids is 514 lines with real per-pin nets. Gates: 238 core + 11 web, fmt/clippy clean, 5 unit tests. NOT DONE: (a) symbol library is GUESSED from refdes prefix (Device:R/C/L/D/Q, else REVIEW_ME) — Eagle records the package, not the KiCad schematic symbol, so generated Part() lines need review; (b) 17 unmapped packages on grids alone (HC49UP, LQFP48, ALPS_POT_VERTICAL_PS, SOIC16N...) — the footprint map covers common passives/SOT/SOIC only; (c) placements parsed but not yet fed into a board, so 'import to layout' is read-only; (d) no manifest integration — an Eagle circuit cannot yet be declared in lob.toml the way [[legion-of-bom-u7p]] fab packages can; (e) multi-sheet schematics untested.
2026-08-18 stale in-progress cleanup: removed from active work. Keep open because the bead is broader than the shipped slice or still has unresolved scope in the existing notes.

title: Schematic: split multi-unit symbols (op-amps) into their units
description:
Multi-unit parts still fall back to a labelled box: read_symbol_graphics reports units>1 and the renderer declines. On puget slew_limiter that is U1 (LM13700, units=5) and U2 (TL072, units=3) — the two parts that ARE the circuit.

WORK: a real schematic places unit A and unit B as separate symbol instances, each wired to its own nets, with the power unit drawn once (or as rail stubs). So: (1) map pin -> unit from the sub-symbol that declares it (pins live in <NAME>_<unit>_<style> blocks, already parsed); (2) group a component instance role by unit and emit one placed instance per unit that is actually used, labelled U2A / U2B; (3) draw unit 0 (common graphics) with each; (4) route each unit only to the nets its pins touch. Layout/ranking must treat each unit as its own node. Follows [[legion-of-bom-n5l]] and [[legion-of-bom-agr]].

title: Schematic: draw real KiCad component symbols instead of boxes
description:
User: "why cannot we get kicad component symbols?" Answer: we can — the current box rendering was a shortcut, not a limitation. Everything needed is already present and verified:
- Part.library_part is already parsed from the netlist libsource, e.g. (libsource (lib "Device") (part "C")) -> "Device:C" (crates/core/src/netlist.rs).
- 223 .kicad_sym libraries are installed and we ALREADY read them: crates/core/src/symbols.rs resolves SPICE models out of them and skidl::kicad_symbol_dir() locates the dir.
- Symbol bodies carry real graphic primitives — rectangle / polyline / circle / arc with stroke and fill, in mm (e.g. Device:R body unit R_0_1 is a rectangle -1.016,-2.54 to 1.016,2.54).
- Pins carry position, angle, length, number and name: (pin passive line (at 0 3.81 270) (length 1.27)) — so wires can terminate at REAL pins instead of the box edge, which also improves the routing.
- crates/core/src/sexpr.rs already parses this format.

WORK:
1. Resolve the symbol: library_part -> <lib>.kicad_sym -> symbol block, following (extends "...") inheritance (verified: TL072 extends LM2904).
2. Emit body primitives as SVG. KiCad symbol space is mm with Y up; the sheet is Y down, so flip. Honour stroke width and fill type.
3. Anchor net wires at real pin endpoints (pin at + angle + length gives the wire attach point) instead of the box edge.
4. Cache parsed symbols per (lib, part) — a circuit reuses the same few.
5. Fall back to the current box when the symbol or the symbol dir is missing (KiCad may not be installed) — same graceful-degradation rule as every other external dependency here.

HARD PART — multi-unit symbols: LM2904 has sub-units LM2904_1_1, _2_1, _3_1 (two op-amps plus the power unit) but the netlist has ONE component U2 for the whole chip. A real schematic places unit A and unit B separately, each wired to its own nets, with power drawn once. So pins must be grouped by unit and each unit placed as its own graphical instance — real schematic-capture logic. Passives/diodes/jacks/pots/headers are single-unit and straightforward; do those first and let multi-unit parts fall back to a box until the unit splitting lands. Follows [[legion-of-bom-agr]].
close_reason: Real KiCad symbols now drawn in the schematic view. symbols::read_symbol_graphics() parses a symbol body (rectangle/polyline/circle/arc) + pins from <lib>.kicad_sym, follows (extends) inheritance (TL072 -> LM2904), and reports unit count; resolved from Part.library_part which the netlist parser already recorded, cached per lib:part. Wires now attach at the REAL pin tip (the netlist names the pin per connection) instead of a box edge. KiCad's three fill modes modelled as SymFill — outline=solid ink, background=sheet colour (occludes without going black), none=open; collapsing them to a bool had rendered audio jacks as black blobs. Verified on puget slew_limiter: 12/14 parts as real symbols (resistor rectangles, cap plates, pot wiper arrows, jack switched-tip contacts), U1/U2 boxed. Gates: 217 core + 11 web, fmt/clippy clean; 4 offline tests using synthetic .kicad_sym fixtures (fill modes, extends, multi-unit, missing lib). DEFERRED: multi-unit parts (op-amps) still fall back to a box — drawing them means splitting pins across separately-placed units, real schematic-capture work; also no symbol rotation/mirroring for tidier wiring, and no pin-name labels.

title: Dashboard: toggle SMD parts on/off in the board view
description: User: "Toggling on SMD or not would be great in legion-of-bom view." In the PCB viewer, let the user show/hide SMD parts (and by extension see the THT-only picture a hand-builder cares about, since puget kits are mixed: SMD pre-assembled by JLCPCB + THT panel hardware soldered by the builder). Implementation options: (a) cheapest — the board render is generated by render_board_png/export_board_svg via kicad-cli, so a toggle needs either a second board file with SMD footprints stripped, or (b) render the 2D layout ourselves from the placements so layers/part-classes can be toggled client-side, or (c) overlay: keep the KiCad render and draw part outlines from the placement data with a class filter. Part class is already known — PartFacts.tht_pads distinguishes THT from SMD, and Part.side gives front/back. Pairs naturally with a front/back toggle (already present) and with the build-guide highlight work [[legion-of-bom-fsn]]. Discovered from the dashboard epic p58.
close_reason: SMD on/off shipped. ?smd=0 on board-top/board-bottom/board-layout renders a through-hole-only board; PCB viewer gets an SMD checkbox beside the view segments (board views only). fab::strip_smd() drops footprints with no thru_hole/np_thru_hole pads — same classification board.rs uses — with a paren-balanced, string-aware block scan so a paren inside a footprint name can't desync it; copper/zones/outline untouched. Filtered variant is a separate render cache key. Verified on puget slew_limiter: 14 parts -> 6 (J1-J4, RV1, RV2 — exactly the panel hardware a mixed-kit builder solders; all 0603/0805/SOIC stripped). 2 unit tests. Gates: 213 core + 11 web, fmt/clippy clean.

title: Dashboard: render the schematic in the UI
description: User: "I would like a nice rendering of the schematic in the legion-of-bom UI if possible." Show the circuit schematic alongside the PCB/panel in the circuit workspace. Investigate the cheapest faithful path: (a) SKiDL can emit a KiCad schematic/netlist — if a .kicad_sch is produced, kicad-cli sch export svg renders it (same shell-out pattern as export_board_svg / render_board_png in fab.rs, with the same graceful ToolNotFound handling); (b) if no .kicad_sch exists, draw our own schematic-style graph from the Circuit model (parts + nets) with a symbol-per-part-kind and simple net routing — full control, no KiCad dependency, but real work; (c) an interim netlist/graph view. Wire into the existing render endpoint as view=schematic (crates/web/src/render.rs already caches by source mtime and maps missing-tool to 503), then add it to the Renders section next to the PCB viewer. Discovered from the dashboard epic p58.
close_reason: Schematic view shipped: GET /render?view=schematic + a 'Schematic' segment in the PCB viewer. Drawn in core (crates/core/src/schematic.rs, schematic_to_svg) from CircuitSource — NOT shelled out, because SKiDL's own generator is experimental and netlistsvg/graphviz are absent here; model-driven keeps it DSL-agnostic and always-available like panel_to_svg. Layout: parts ranked left->right by BFS hops from the input net over SIGNAL nets only (power rails would collapse everything into one column), stacked in columns; signal nets route vertical trunks with per-column lane assignment so parallel nets don't stack on one line or collide labels; power drawn as rail bars, ground as triangles, per part. Values ellipsized to fit boxes. Verified on puget slew_limiter: all 14 parts, readable signal flow, no overlaps. 4 unit tests. title: Rotate anchored landscape controls (pots) to horizontal pins — needs placer/router support

So anchored 90-deg controls need real placer/router support: rotated-footprint keepout+mating (keepout_at_rot exists), edge-clearance for the wider rotated body, and route re-flow. control_rotation reverted to the safe pin-span heuristic (pots stay rot=0, DRC-clean 5HP). close_reason: Pots now sit pins-horizontal, DRC-clean, and routing IMPROVED. control_rotation decides on body_extent (courtyard) not the lug-inflated keep-out. Root cause of the old breakage found + fixed: the placer rotated a part's body box but NOT its THT keep-outs (tht_pads_at had no rotation param), so a rotated pot's mounting lugs were reserved in the wrong place and a back-side SMD pad got packed onto one (clearance 0.1895<0.2mm). tht_pads_at now takes rotation; keepout_at_rot now carries the origin offset around the turn. Both use KiCad's sense (x,y)->(y,-x) at +90 — the opposite sense is still DRC-clean but reserves wrong squares and degrades routing (HPWL 358 vs 227), so a regression test pins it. Also connect_pads yes (solid zone connect) to kill starved_thermal on edge-hugging THT GND pads. title: Routability-aware auto-sizing: minimum_hp must account for routing, not just placement

Options: (a) route+DRC per HP candidate and pick the smallest that's clean (expensive but correct); (b) a routability buffer (min-HP + N) until the router improves; (c) gate auto-derive-default behind clean routing. Blocked-by router improvement + design-rule placement (siblings) — those shrink the true routable HP.
notes: PARTIAL fix shipped: minimum_hp now returns place-min + 1 HP (a routability margin) — the parts PLACE at the min but the crude router needs ~1 HP more room to route DRC-clean. title: Orientation-aware anchored placement: rotate controls + align mount point to cutout
description: EurorackPlacer::place (board.rs) places every part at rotation_deg=0.0 and puts the footprint ORIGIN at the cutout center. Two bugs: (1) POTS render 90-deg wrong (Alpha9mm native orientation = pins in a horizontal row → landscape); anchored controls need a rotation so pins face INTO the board. (2) JACKS don't line up with panel holes: the panel-mount point (jack barrel / pot bushing center) isn't the footprint origin, and nothing offsets for it — align the mechanical mount point to the cutout, not the origin. Needs per-control orientation + mount-point-offset data (extend BuiltinCutouts/CutoutSpec or PartFacts). Verify by regenerating slew_limiter board+panel and checking barrel↔hole concentricity.
close_reason: Orientation + mount-point alignment landed in both placers (EurorackPlacer + SeededPlacer, board.rs). ROOT CAUSE found via the Alpha RD901F pot footprint: origin is at pad 1, but the shaft/courtyard-centre is offset +(5.72,2.5)mm — so anchoring the ORIGIN at the cutout put the shaft ~5.7mm off the panel hole (same for jacks in y). FIX: align the mount point (PartFacts.origin_offset ≈ courtyard centre ≈ shaft/barrel) to the cutout — place the footprint origin at cutout - rotate_offset(offset, rot), keep-out re-centred on the cutout. VERIFIED on slew_limiter: RV1/RV2 origins shifted to x=9.9 so shafts land at x=15.2 (panel hole); jacks' y-offset applied so barrels hit the holes. Also added control_rotation (stands a control on end when its through-hole PIN ROW is horizontal — pad_span, not courtyard) + rotate_offset; the Alpha pot's pins are a vertical column so it correctly stays rot=0 (the 'wider than tall' look is the body shape; a pins-down rotation is a possible refinement, noted). 3 new unit tests. NOTE: keepout_at_rot approximates the offset for rot≠0 (fine — controls ~never rotate).

This is the seam DESIGN 2.2 requires: web + CLI read the same struct.

title: Repo-aware pipeline + CLI: multi-circuit, manifest-driven build
description: Make lob operate on a REPO, not a lone .py: discover circuits from the manifest; build/run/guide/fab one circuit or all; consistent out/<circuit>/ layout; a single 'lob build' that produces the full artifact set per circuit. This is the 'Hugo' — a repo->artifacts builder. Composes the existing stage functions; no core rewrite. Foundation the dashboard renders from.

Outputs keyed by circuit NAME (ResolvedCircuit.name -> out/<name>/, threaded through guide/bom/fab). Verified: 'lob build slew_limiter' on puget-hardware -> guide+bom+fab, DRC-clean. title: Repo-aware circuits builder + project-management CLI (the local 'Hugo' layer)
description: Crystallizes the direction in DESIGN 2.2/2.4/2.5: lob becomes a Git-backed circuits-repo tool, not a single-file runner. title: Path B: cross-engine harness — run pedalkernel process, diff vs ngspice simulate_tran
description: The differential-validation loop: (1) emit .pedal (ef4.3) + a step/sequence stimulus WAV; (2) run 'pedalkernel process <pedal> <in.wav> <out.wav>' (WDF/MNA); (3) read out.wav, measure slew rate / step response; (4) compare to our ngspice simulate_tran result, PASS/FAIL within tolerance. Two independent engines agreeing = high-confidence functional validation. Needs the pedalkernel binary available (cd pedalkernel && cargo build -p pedalkernel --bin pedalkernel, ~22s) or the optional-dep path (ef4.1). Build pedalkernel binary discovery like kicad-cli (lob doctor).

title: Slew validation gate: step-sequence + CV stimulus + slew-rate/CV verify check
description: Builds on tus.10 (transient wired into lob run). Add: (1) a step-SEQUENCE stimulus (multi-step, like a sequencer) not just one step; (2) a CV input driven during the transient so the sim exercises the rate modulation; (3) a self-selecting verify CHECK (like check_rc_cutoff/gain) that gates: output slews toward each step (settles), and slew rate scales ~linearly with CV/IABC. Reference envelope from the competitive analysis (A-170 etc.): flag builds landing outside expected V/ms. Hand-proven already (scratchpad/slew_val.cir + artifact): base 2.13, CV+5V 4.21 V/ms (1.98x).

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
PARTLY DONE, 2026-07-28 — via the dual slew limiter's channel-independence work
([[legion-of-bom-9wh.1]], machinery in [[legion-of-bom-9wh.2]]). Two of this
bead's three asks are now built and running in `lob run`; the third is NOT and
this bead should stay open for it.

DONE — ask (1), step-SEQUENCE stimulus, not a single edge.
  `step_sequence()` in crates/cli/src/main.rs builds a multi-step PWL (0, +2,
  -2, +1, 0 V, 150 ms dwell each, 0.1 ms edges) so the stimulus demands far more
  slew rate than the circuit can deliver and the output is genuinely
  rate-limited rather than following the input. Feeds the new crosstalk stage.

DONE — ask (2), extra nets driven during the transient.
  `TranDrive.cv` is used to hold every non-driven channel's input at 0 V. The
  mechanism this bead wanted for CV is in place and exercised; it is just
  pointed at channel inputs rather than at a RATE_CV net so far.

DONE, and beyond the original scope — a self-selecting verify check does now
exist for a multi-channel time-domain property: `check_channel_crosstalk` in
crates/core/src/verify.rs, gating at -60 dB, self-selecting on >= 2 signal
channels exactly the way check_rc_cutoff / check_noninverting_gain self-select
on topology. Measured on the real dual: 0.000000 Vpp leaked against 4.000 Vpp
driven; and proven to bite by mutation (a copied dual with one shared net object
fails at 0.0 dB, pipeline 2 of 8 stages failed).

STILL OPEN — ask (3), the actual SLEW-RATE check, and it is the heart of this
bead:
  * "output slews toward each step (settles)" — nothing checks this. The
    step-sequence stimulus is built and run, but no check asserts that the
    output actually reached each level before the next step.
  * "slew rate scales ~linearly with CV/IABC" — nothing checks this. This needs
    two or more driven runs at different CV/RATE settings and a linearity
    assertion across them, which the current single-shot stage shape does not
    express.
  * "reference envelope from the competitive analysis (A-170 etc.) — flag builds
    landing outside expected V/ms" — nothing checks this either.

USEFUL NUMBER FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP, measured today rather than assumed. The
transient stage reports peak slew 41 V/s on both the mono and the dual, which is
the pot at its default 50 % wiper: Vctrl = +1.0 V, IABC = (1.0 + 10.6)/620k =
18.7 uA, SR = IABC/C1 = 18.7 uA / 470 nF = 39.8 V/s predicted. Measured 41.
And at the ends of the knob the standalone deck measures 78.45 V/s at Vctrl
= +12 V against 77.6 V/s predicted. So the analytic model to check against —
SR = (Vctrl - V_BIAS)/(R3*C1), V_BIAS ~= -10.6 V — is confirmed to about 1 % and
is a sound basis for the check this bead is asking for.

BLOCKER REMOVED: this bead was previously unimplementable on the real board
anyway, because `lob run`'s simulate stage FAILED on the slew limiter ("no SPICE
model or primitive mapping for: SW1, U2"). That is fixed in 9wh.2. The mono
board now completes 7 stages and the dual 8.

title: Router can't fan out to fine-pitch SMD sub-board pads (Seed2 DFM 1.27mm)
description: The Seed2 DFM's 50 SMD pads at 1.27mm pitch: the router leaves inner/boxed-in pads unrouted (unused neighbour pads seeded as obstacles + their clearance halos box in the target at 0.2mm grid). Seed2 DFM demo: 3 nets unrouted (M1.A10, R1.1, M1.A4), 2 unconnected DRC errors. Footprint is correct (real Electrosmith); needs finer routing grid near fine-pitch SMD and/or pad fanout (short escape stubs). Patch SM (THT) is unaffected (0 errors).
close_reason: Root cause was NOT a router fanout gap — footprint_pads ignored per-pad rotation. The Seed2 DFM's SMD pads are rotated 90/270 with size (1.98 0.65); read as 1.98mm WIDE (not tall), so at 1.27mm pitch the painted pads overlapped into one solid unroutable blob. Fix: read the pad's rotation (at x y ROT) and swap w/h for odd multiples of 90. Seed2 DFM demo: 2 errors/3 unrouted -> 0 errors, 0 unconnected; inner fine-pitch pads (A3-A8 etc.) now route. General correctness fix for any rotated non-square pad. Patch SM + 8HP slew unchanged (0 errors). Unit test footprint_pads_swaps_wh_for_rotated_pads + inner-pad integration route; 146 tests, clippy/fmt clean.

title: Placer: pack short parts into the standoff space under a sub-board (collision check gates tall ones)
description: Today the placer treats a sub-board's courtyard as full keep-out, so the space under a stacked Daisy (its ~11mm standoff) is wasted and the 25z.4 collision check never fires in practice. Let the placer place SHORT parts (height < standoff) under the sub-board body, using part_height_mm; the collision check then actively guards against tall parts slipping under. This is the vertical-space efficiency (a 3U board has room) and makes 25z.4 live.
close_reason: Real, general packing under stacked sub-boards. (1) Region-based side+THT-aware placement: PartFacts now carries height_mm, standoff_mm, and tht_pads (through-hole pad keep-outs); placement_clear enforces — bodies clash only same-side and only when neither passes under the other (standoff vs height); through-hole pins are both-side hard keep-outs every body avoids; a candidate's own pins may pass over a standoff but not into a surface part. (2) Sub-board courtyard = per-header-row rects (general from spec.rows), not the full body, so KiCad stops false-flagging same-side parts in the open centre. Nothing Daisy-hardcoded (driven by pad layers + standoff + rows). Verified real KiCad: 8HP slew limiter 0 errors (side-aware placement, no regression); daisy_demo 0 errors; daisy_panel_demo 0 errors with 6/12 support parts packed UNDER the Daisy in the clear centre (was 25 errors with naive packing). Tall parts kept out (height gate); 25z.4 collision check remains the backstop. 144 tests (placement_clear rules + pack-under/tall-out).

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
Attempted naive packing (let a short part's placement overlap the sub-board's courtyard via a height-aware nearest_clear_spot). REVERTED — it is not DRC-clean, for two reasons found via real KiCad DRC on a Daisy 8HP panel demo (Daisy + 12 short 0603 parts netted to it):

1) Parts land ON the sub-board's header pads → clearance / shorting_items / pth_inside_courtyard (the header pins are real copper on the main board). Needs PAD-AWARE placement: the sub-board's header-pad regions must stay hard keep-outs while only the clear interior is soft.

2) MORE fundamental: KiCad courtyards_overlap fires on ANY 2D courtyard overlap regardless of Z clearance. So even perfect pad-aware placement (parts in the clear centre strip) still trips 9x courtyards_overlap against the Daisy body courtyard. To be DRC-clean the sub-board's COURTYARD must be modelled to exclude the usable under-space (courtyard = header/pad regions only, not the full 18x51 body).

Measured: naive packing = 25 DRC errors (9 courtyards_overlap, 4 pth_inside_courtyard, clearance/shorting on header pins, silk). Same board with parts placed AROUND the Daisy (no packing) = 0 errors, 0 unconnected.

Re-scope: (a) sub-board courtyard covers only its pads/edges (not the body interior) + (b) pad-aware placement. Both required. PartFacts already has the height data path from 25z.4. Not started beyond this investigation.

title: Height/collision awareness: parts under a stacked sub-board must clear its standoff (DESIGN 6.7)
description: A sub-board (Daisy) mounts on headers at a standoff height above the main board; components under its body on the same side must be shorter than that standoff or they collide. Add height data (sub-board standoff height + part heights) and a collision check that surfaces parts under a sub-board taller than its clearance. First cut of DESIGN 6.7 mechanical/3D collision, scoped to sub-board stacks.
close_reason: Height/collision check (DESIGN 6.7): part_height_mm heuristic by footprint family + SubboardSpec.standoff_mm (Daisy 11mm); detect_collisions flags same-side parts whose keep-out overlaps a sub-board body and exceed its standoff. Wired through BoardArtifacts.collisions + LayoutReport.collisions + findings; lob board prints 'mechanical clearance issue(s)'. Unit-tested (tall-under vs short/back/clear-of). Daisy demo + slew limiter: 0 false collisions, still DRC-clean. NOTE: with the current placer keeping parts out of the sub-board courtyard, this is a safety net; it fires once a placer packs under sub-boards (filed follow-up). 142 tests (2 new), clippy/fmt clean.

title: Ground pour fragments around a sub-board's dense THT header grid -> starved_thermal
description: A sub-board's header (e.g. Daisy's 40 THT pads) punches a dense grid of holes through the ground pour, splitting it into islands; a GND pad's thermal spokes then land on an isolated island (KiCad starved_thermal). Seen on the daisy_demo board (1 error: pad 20 [GND] of A1, B.Cu island). Inherent to placing dense THT headers on a poured board. Fix options: stitching vias between F/B pours near the header, or pour-aware GND pad handling. Relates to j54.17 (back-side pour). Not a footprint defect (footprint places+routes clean).
close_reason: ground_stitching_vias places a GND via just off each through-hole ground pad, tying the F.Cu/B.Cu pours together locally so a pour island fenced off by a dense THT header grid reconnects to the intact pour on the other layer. Placed inside the board edge and clear of all other-net copper (pads/tracks/vias); a boxed-in pad is skipped, not forced. Daisy demo: 1 starved_thermal -> 0 DRC errors (1 stitch added). 8HP slew limiter unchanged: 0 errors (7 stitches added, improves the ground plane). 2 unit tests + 137 total, clippy/fmt clean.

title: 4HP: back-side SOIC U2 adjacent pads short on B.Cu (real narrow-module blocker, NOT a space issue)
description: Reframes 3jh: at 4HP the slew limiter's DRC errors are NOT physical infeasibility (14x128mm 3U has ample area to stack parts vertically). They cluster on ONE part: U2, a back-side SOIC on B.Cu, whose adjacent pads short (pads 2-3,3-4,5-6,7-8: shorting_items + solder_mask_bridge, different nets). Likely the B.Cu ground pour / routing interacting with the fine-pitch (1.27mm) SOIC after the back-flip. Fixing this (plus better vertical stacking) should make single-board narrow modules route clean, per user: rotate/stack in the tall 3U rather than pack horizontally. Found while scoping 3jh.
notes:
2026-07-28: root cause found (KiCad .kicad_pcb pad `at` angles are ABSOLUTE
board orientation, not footprint-relative) and fixed in board.rs
`turn_pad_with_footprint`. Measured: a 90-turned SOIC-14 on the real slew
limiter went 10 shorting_items + 10 solder_mask_bridge -> 0. The placer's
"never turn an SMD part" band-aid is retired: it now PREFERS not to turn SMD
and falls back to the other quarter turn only when the preferred pose fits
nowhere. See the comment thread and [[legion-of-bom-unc]].
close_reason: Stale in-progress cleanup: implementation notes show this work was completed and verified; leaving any follow-up work to separate beads.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED, 2026-07-28, with KiCad as the oracle. The open
question in the note — "understand WHY rotated pads 0.67mm apart read as
shorting (likely the rotated+mirrored back-footprint pad/mask emission in
board.rs vs KiCad)" — is answered, and the guess was right.

IN A .kicad_pcb A FOOTPRINT PAD'S `at` ANGLE IS ABSOLUTE BOARD ORIENTATION,
not an angle relative to its footprint. Rotating a footprint turns its pad
POSITIONS (KiCad does that from the footprint's own `(at x y rot)`) and carries
the same turn into every pad's own `at`. board.rs copied library pads verbatim,
so the positions turned and the pad SHAPES did not: a SOIC-14's 1.95 x 0.6mm
pads end up lying broadside across a 1.27mm pitch and overlap every neighbour.

MEASURED, on out/slew_limiter/slew_limiter.kicad_pcb with U2 turned to 90 and
nothing else changed:
  pads copied verbatim (what we shipped):  10 pad-to-pad shorting_items
                                         + 10 solder_mask_bridge, inside U2
                                           (pairs 2-3, 3-4, 4-5, 5-6, 8-9,
                                            9-10, 10-11, 11-12, 12-13, 13-14)
  +90 added to each pad's `at` angle:       0 and 0
Same board, same router, same everything else.

FIX: crates/core/src/board.rs `turn_pad_with_footprint`, called from
transform_footprint after the back-flip (which already reverses handedness).
Unit test board::tests::a_rotated_footprints_pads_carry_the_rotation covers
front, back and a non-zero library pad angle.

THIS WAS NOT ONLY AN SMD PROBLEM. Every rotated footprint on every board this
project has shipped was affected. On the dual slew limiter the four Alpha pots
are rotated 90 and their library pads carry angle 90, so their 2.72 x 3.24mm
OVAL MOUNTING LUGS — with 1.1 x 1.8mm slot drills — were emitted at 90 instead
of the true 180, i.e. with the slot turned a quarter turn. Correcting it
exposes one real `clearance` error KiCad previously could not see (a track
routed through where a mounting lug actually is): dual route_bench goes 15 DRC
-> 16. That is the tool becoming honest, not a regression.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PLACER, which is the reason this bead mattered: the
"partial fix" recorded here — never turn a fine-pitch SMD IC — was a band-aid
over this, and it is what made a 4 HP module impossible, because the only pose
a SOIC fits a 20.32mm-wide board in is sideways. SeededPlacer may now turn a
part either way (it still PREFERS not to turn SMD — fanout — and only falls
back when the preferred pose fits nowhere). See [[legion-of-bom-unc]] for what
that did and did not buy at 4 HP.

title: Placement: free parts land within edge clearance of the board edge on narrow HP (unroutable + copper_edge_clearance)
description: Surfaced by j54.23: on a 6HP slew-limiter variant the CV jack J4 (a free/auto-placed part, not a panel cutout) is placed hard against the board edge — its GND PTH pad trips copper_edge_clearance and 3 nets to J4 are left unrouted because the router (correctly, post-j54.23) won't route into the edge band to reach it. The placer must keep every part's courtyard an edge-clearance (~0.5mm) inside the board outline. Pre-existing (the pad-edge error predates j54.23; that fix just unmasked the unroutable connections). Related to 3jh (dense narrow modules). The real 8HP board is unaffected (0 errors).
close_reason: overflow_drop() stacks unfittable free parts in an off-board lane 2mm below the bottom edge instead of straddling it at y1+2 (~1mm inside), so an overflowed part no longer trips copper_edge_clearance — the failure surfaces honestly as unrouted nets. Fixed in both SeededPlacer and EurorackPlacer. 8HP slew limiter unchanged (0 DRC errors); 6HP CV jack J4 drops 3.9mm below the edge, 3 nets unconnected (J4 unfittable on 30mm = 3jh, not this bug). Regression test overflow_parts_drop_clear_below_the_board_edge; 131 tests, clippy/fmt clean.

title: Dense narrow modules (<=4HP): controls eat the board -> offset-column or 2-board stack
description: At 4HP a centered jack/pot courtyard (~13mm) spans nearly the whole 14mm usable width, so anchored panel controls leave no room for components on the same PCB (103 DRC errors even SMD+double-sided). Real fix is architectural: (a) offset the control column to one side to clear a component strip, or (b) a 2-board stack (controls PCB + main PCB + board-to-board header). Neither exists yet; needed for auto-layout of dense <=4HP modules.
notes: 2026-08-18 stale in-progress cleanup: removed from active work. Keep open because the bead is broader than the shipped slice or still has unresolved scope in the existing notes.

title: Router: rip-up-and-retry to resolve the last unrouted nets (8HP=4, 6HP=6 left)
description: With A* fast enough to iterate, the remaining gap to clean boards is the router giving up on nets blocked by already-committed copper. Add rip-up: when a net can't route, rip up the blocking net(s) and re-route in a better order. DESIGN 6.5 names this as the loop's job. Would take 8HP/6HP from ~10-13 errors toward clean.
close_reason: Rip-up-and-reroute landed: route_pass reports blame (nets whose committed copper boxes in an unreachable pad); route() forces those blockers to route after the victim via accumulating ordering constraints + topo-sort (cycles dropped). Combined with A* + a conservative rotation heuristic (only rotate parts too wide for the board), the CV-added SMD PCBA slew limiter now routes 6HP AND 8HP fully DRC-clean (0 errors, was 10-13). 4HP 103->46 (still architectural, see 3jh). 128 tests pass.

title: Panel mounting holes: oval (slotted) vs round option + placement pattern (diagonal L/R 2-hole, or all 4)
description: Eurorack panels use oval/slotted mounting holes so horizontal position adjusts in the rack. Add: hole shape (oval slot | round) and placement pattern (diagonal top-left+bottom-right 2-hole | all 4 | left 2). Wire into panel spec TOML + PCB Edge.Cuts + DXF rendering. Real-Eurorack default: oval, diagonal.

title: Layout: HP-minimizing mode — find the smallest HP the module fits in (controls + board)
description: A mode where layout optimizes for minimum HP: try successively narrower HP widths, place+route the board and fit the panel controls, pick the smallest HP where everything fits without overflow/unroutable criticals. Ties into derive-panel (auto-choose HP) and the iterative layout loop (j54.6).
notes: UPDATE: the +1-HP routability band-aid noted earlier is REMOVED. It was compensating for the j54.25 rotation-short (place-min 4 with a rotated SOIC didn't route). With j54.25's partial fix (SMD ICs no longer rotate), place-min=5 for slew_limiter ROUTES DRC-clean, so minimum_hp now honestly returns place-min (no buffer) → default 5HP clean. True route-aware sizing (route+DRC per candidate) still the real thing for the general case.

title: Panel silk (labels/title/logo) collides with cutouts — 'writing hitting a jack'
description: Derived/rendered panel places the title (vertical, centre) and per-cutout labels and the logo without checking against cutout positions, so text lands on a jack/pot hole. Placement of title/labels/logo must avoid the cutouts (and mounting holes).

title: Circuits: tag critical nets in slew_limiter.py (SLEW_NODE feedback, output path) via net.netclass=NetClass('Critical')
description: The layout loop now reads (class "Critical") and weights those nets in analog mode, but no net in the puget-hardware circuits is tagged yet (loop reports 'critical 0mm'). Tagging SLEW_NODE (high-Z OTA feedback) and the output path would (a) protect them in placement and (b) recover the SIG_OUT regression (16->30mm) seen when U2 pulled toward its higher-fanout neighbours. One-line change per net in the separate ~/src/puget-hardware repo.
close_reason: Tagged SLEW_NODE (high-Z OTA feedback), SIG_IN + SIG_OUT (panel audio I/O) via a critical() helper (net.netclasses=NetClass('Critical')) in slew_limiter.py. Verified end-to-end: netlist emits (class 'Default,Critical'); is_critical() now parses comma-joined classes; analog loop reports critical 53mm and drives SLEW_NODE 86->8.6mm, SIG_IN 32->14mm. DRC-clean. Fab regenerated.

title: Panel PCB: per-cutout silk labels (IN/OUT/RATE) + derive panel from circuit
description: panel_to_kicad_pcb emits only a title. Add per-cutout silkscreen labels (IN/OUT/RATE/etc.) and nicer artwork. Cutout struct needs a label field. Ideally derive the panel spec from the circuit's panel-facing parts (jacks/pots) + net names rather than a hand-written TOML.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: Per-cutout silk labels DONE: Cutout.label field (+ TOML), rendered as horizontal gr_text above each cutout in panel_to_kicad_pcb; slew panel now shows RATE/IN/OUT + prettified title. Board silk also gained title + component values (transform_footprint). Remaining part of this bead: derive-panel-from-circuit (auto-place cutouts from the circuit's jacks/pots) — not done.

title: Transient (time-domain) simulation for slew/VCA circuits — not just AC sweep
description: lob run's simulate stage hardcodes an ngspice AC sweep on nets named IN/OUT. The slew limiter needs TRANSIENT analysis (slew-rate response to a step), and uses SIG_IN/SIG_OUT. Predicted in slew-limiter-circuit.md ('first circuit where ngspice checks behavior over time... transient, not AC sweep'). Add a transient sim path + configurable stimulus/probe nets so lob run works on time-domain circuits. Maps to tus.3.
close_reason: Transient sim capability delivered: TranAnalysis + generate_tran_deck (PWL step) + simulate_tran + slew/rise metrics, shared body-emission with the AC path. Validated end-to-end on an RC step response (ngspice). Slew-limiter values (R3=47k, C1=47nF) confirmed via a datasheet-behavioural OTA core: 10.23 V/ms = IABC/C1, 10V in ~1ms. Full LM13700-part pipeline run still needs the cited SPICE model (okm.9).

title: GridRouter leaves nets unrouted on denser boards (slew limiter: SIG_IN->U2.3)
description: The slew limiter (11 parts, 2-layer) left 1 net unrouted (SIG_IN to U2 pin 3). The maze router's completion rate drops on denser real boards vs the trivial Phase 0 demos. Needs ripup-and-retry / ordering heuristics / more layers, or at least a clear manual-route handoff. Feeds the iterative-layout loop (j54).
close_reason: Added rip-up-free retry to GridRouter: failed nets get grid priority on the next pass so their blockers reroute around them (route_pass + priority loop, <=6 rounds, deterministic). Slew limiter SIG_IN now routes: 1 unrouted -> 0. Existing routing/determinism tests unchanged. Fuller routing exposed a separate GND-pour-island bug (new bead).

title: Access-aware assembly sequencing (spatial), beyond height heuristic
description: Current ordering is a good heuristic: back side first, then low-to-high by type (R,D,Q,U,C,SW,pots,jacks), panel hardware last. But true physical-access sequencing needs spatial reasoning — a placed tall part must not block iron/tweezer access to a shorter neighbour soldered later, and clearance between adjacent parts matters. Consider per-part height (from footprint courtyard/3D or a height table) + neighbour-proximity to refine order within a kind group. User feedback 2026-07-23.

title: Double-sided guide: render bottom side for back-mounted steps
description: Back-mounted parts are currently overlaid on the TOP photoreal render at their board-mm position, but they physically mount on the bottom (mirror). A step containing back parts should show a 'pcb render --side bottom' render (mirrored mapping) so overlays land on the real bottom pads. Front steps keep the top render. The BACK caution already warns; this makes the diagram match. Same-side boards (Puget/Mutable) unaffected.
close_reason: dqk.4: prep/sort sheet + per-step progress + BACK-side badges; assembly reordered per user feedback (type groups low->high, back side first, panel hardware last). dqk.5: back-side steps render on pcb render --side bottom with mirror_part_x so overlays land on real bottom pads (multi-image PDF).

title: Richer, genuinely helpful step content (quantities, orientation, tools, progress, visual-BOM sort sheet)
description: Beyond bare minimum: per-step quantities + running progress, explicit orientation guidance for polarized parts, a component sorting/visual-BOM sheet (place-all-resistors style), and clear 'what you need' framing. DESIGN 7.6/7.8.
close_reason: dqk.4: prep/sort sheet + per-step progress + BACK-side badges; assembly reordered per user feedback (type groups low->high, back side first, panel hardware last). dqk.5: back-side steps render on pcb render --side bottom with mirror_part_x so overlays land on real bottom pads (multi-image PDF).

title: Multi-component grouping in guide steps — verify + regression test
description: A step highlights ALL same-type parts at once (all resistors, then all caps). Verify grouping renders correctly with several parts and lock with a test (rc_ladder: 2R+2C).
close_reason: Photoreal unpopulated pcb render + analytic overlay mapping (f=0.70, centered, W/H from PNG header) shipped for HTML+PDF; markers upgraded to amber/red boxes + chip labels + polarity dots; multi-component grouping verified (R1+R2 in one step) and tested.

title: Improved highlight markers on photoreal board (high-contrast box, refdes chip, polarity)
description: Replace the flat red rects with markers that read well over a green board: high-contrast outline + translucent fill, a refdes chip label, and polarity/pin-1 callouts. PDF translucency needs an ExtGState alpha (/ca).
close_reason: Photoreal unpopulated pcb render + analytic overlay mapping (f=0.70, centered, W/H from PNG header) shipped for HTML+PDF; markers upgraded to amber/red boxes + chip labels + polarity dots; multi-component grouping verified (R1+R2 in one step) and tested.

title: Build guide: step-by-step visual assembly guide (DESIGN 7.6/7.8)
description: Generate a step-by-step assembly guide from a placed board. Group components into low-profile-first build steps (resistors -> diodes/LEDs -> sockets/connectors -> caps -> ICs -> tall parts, DESIGN 7.8), and render a self-contained HTML page: each step shows a top-down board diagram with THAT step's components highlighted (red boxes over all resistors, then caps, etc. — the human's visual hint), a sorted parts list (value -> designators, qty), and polarity/pin-1 callouts for polarized parts (diodes, electrolytics, ICs). Also the 7.6 visual-BOM/component-sorting view. Parses the generated .kicad_pcb for positions (decoupled, like drc/fab); values/types from the circuit. First cut: schematic top-down SVG (accurate boxes, no render/camera dependency); overlaying on a real render is a later refinement.
notes: HTML guide now uses the REAL KiCad board layout (user: 'photo real kicad with real layout'). fab::export_board_svg runs kicad-cli export svg (F.Cu,B.Cu,F.Silkscreen,F.Fab,Edge.Cuts, no fit -> true board mm coords). guide_to_html(guide, Option<real_svg>): retargets the KiCad SVG viewBox to crop to the board outline and overlays translucent-red highlight boxes + K/+/pin-1 markers at true board coords (pixel-accurate, verified: kicad paths + overlays share the 93-128mm range). Falls back to schematic top-down if kicad-cli absent. Note: PDF still uses the schematic top-down (embedding the KiCad plot in the native PDF needs image/SVG support) — follow-up.
close_reason: lob guide: step-by-step visual assembly guide (HTML). core::guide parses the generated board for positions, groups parts into low-profile-first steps (resistors->diodes->connectors->switches->caps->transistors->ICs), renders a self-contained HTML page with a top-down SVG per step (current step's parts highlighted red, others greyed) + sorted parts list + polarity/pin-1 callouts + back-side notes. First cut = schematic top-down (accurate, no render dependency). Validated on opamp + double_sided.

title: CPL/Gerber origin alignment (drill/place-file origin at board corner)
description: lob fab's CPL had page-space coordinates (negative Y). Anchor the board's aux/drill-place-file origin at the outline's bottom-left corner in generate_board, and export CPL (pos), gerbers, and drill with --use-drill-file-origin / --drill-origin plot so all three share that origin. CPL coords are now small + positive from the board corner (JLC convention).
close_reason: Done: aux_axis_origin at outline bottom-left; --use-drill-file-origin on pos+gerbers, --drill-origin plot on drill. Verified: opamp CPL R1 at (6.425, 7.205) instead of (100, -100).

title: Router: THT-aware layer transitions (no redundant vias on through-hole pads)
description: On a double-sided board the maze router drops a via essentially on top of a through-hole pad (DRC hole_to_hole warning: two drilled holes too close). A through-hole pad already connects both copper layers, so the router should treat reaching a Both-layer pad as a FREE layer transition and never place a via on/adjacent to one. Fix: mark through-hole pad cells as owned-by-net on BOTH layers (connection points on either side), and forbid via placement within a through-hole pad's keep-out. Exposed by the double_sided.py demo (SMD front + THT header back); currently a warning, not an error.
close_reason: Router now treats through-hole pads as free layer transitions (PadLayer::layers): a pad is a source/target on every layer it touches, so the router meets a through-hole pad on whichever side the net is already on instead of vias-ing onto its hole. double_sided.py hole_to_hole warnings 4->0; all boards 0 errors.

title: Reconcile back-side ground pour with back-side components (DESIGN 6.2)
description: The 'bottom = pure ground, no components' mental model earlier drafts implicitly carried is WRONG for Eurorack (stays true for THT-pedal single-sided). A solid ground pour on the back copper AND components mounted on that same physical side are NOT mutually exclusive: SMD parts sit on a mostly-ground-poured layer, routed around, with the pour knocked out around their pads/traces. Update the pour generation + routing so back-side components coexist with the back-copper GND pour. DESIGN says: worth a closer pass once double-sided placement logic is actually being built, not before — so this follows the side-aware placement work.
notes:
Considered as a design-rule variant (legion-of-bom-avg) and REJECTED, twice over:

1. What this bead actually asks for — a back-copper GND pour coexisting with back-side components, knocked out around their pads, plus via-stitching the pour to GND pads — is board GENERATION work on copper geometry produced after placement. The rule system evaluates placements. Forcing it in would be the wrong shape.

2. The placement-shaped version cannot fire. For the pour to flow between two parts the gap must exceed 2*clearance + min_thickness = 2(0.2) + 0.25 = 0.65mm, but the placer already enforces PLACE_CLEARANCE_MM = 1.5mm between keep-outs. The rule is satisfied by construction and would never report anything — which is the anti-pattern recorded on avg: a rule nobody can fail reads as a guarantee we never checked.

So this stays generation work. The tractable first slice is the concrete instance already in the notes: via-stitch the pour to GND pads, which fixes the isolated_copper warning when a GND net's only pad is on the opposite layer. Roughly the size of the power-header silkscreen work.

title: silkscreen_collision violation type in DRC-readback (DESIGN 6.10)
description: Add a silkscreen_collision violation type to the DRC-readback check step (6.5). Silkscreen-over-pad or silkscreen-over-silkscreen is NOT an electrical DRC violation, so it passes the existing copper/electrical check silently — the layout loop's check step must surface it explicitly. Depends on the silkscreen actually being generated (6.10 gen) and on the IPC DRC + violation readback plumbing (j54.11).
close_reason: DrcViolation::is_silkscreen_collision + DrcReport::silkscreen_collisions/count classify KiCad silk keys (silk_overlap/silk_over_copper) by 'silk' substring; CLI drc report surfaces them in a dedicated section with locations, separate from electrical warnings. Verified against a real colliding board (3 flagged) and clean boards (0). Not gated on is_clean (warnings, not electrical).

title: Silkscreen generation v0 — refdes/polarity/pin-1, KiCad defaults (DESIGN 6.10)
description: Silkscreen (reference designators, polarity marks, pin-1 indicators) is a distinct KiCad layer the sexp-gen/DRC copper work (6.6) never touched. v0 scope: ACCEPT KiCad's default reference-designator auto-placement rather than building custom placement logic — real auto-arrangement of silkscreen text to avoid overlaps is its own hard label-placement problem, not worth solving before a single real board ships. Ensure refdes + polarity marks + pin-1 indicators render on F.SilkS/B.SilkS in the generated .kicad_pcb. Matters directly (not cosmetic) for THT hand-assembly from a BOM: polarity marks in particular must be correct and visible — wrong-polarity assembly (diodes, electrolytics, ICs) is a common DIY failure mode. Feeds 7.8 build-guide rendering (the populated-board render needs accurate silkscreen, not just accurate copper). THT's low part count + 0.1in grid makes collisions rare, so defaults are a forgiving first cut.
close_reason: Silk (refdes+polarity+pin-1) renders via wholesale footprint placement; added Reference-unhide for guaranteed visibility + 2 regression tests. Front on F.SilkS, back mirrored to B.SilkS. DRC clean.

title: Compatible-substitute suggestions at BOM time (DESIGN 9.6)
description: Advisory only, NEVER automatic. At generate_bom time, if a primary MPN has low/zero stock, pull every part sharing its pin_compatible_groups entry and check each LIVE against the SUBCIRCUIT'S declared requires block (3.4) using the stored part_ratings (3.5) — not a hardcoded 'part X substitutes for Y' fact, which would ignore that the same swap can be fine in one role (buffer) and wrong in another (noise-sensitive signal path). Passing candidates are surfaced to the human for approval at BOM time; nothing swaps automatically. Depends on: pin_compatible_groups table, subcircuit role-requirements, okm part_ratings + verified gate, and a live stock signal (zya.2 Mouser).

title: pin_compatible_groups table (DESIGN 9.6)
description: A small, hand-maintained table of physically drop-in part families (op-amp pinout-compatible groups, etc.), each row (group_id, mpn, package, verified_by_human). This is the only genuinely stable fact worth caching — footprint/pinout compatibility doesn't change — so it's a cached relation, unlike the live requirement check. verified_by_human gated like the rest of the parts library (okm.4). Schema per DESIGN 9.6: CREATE TABLE pin_compatible_groups (group_id INT, mpn VARCHAR(64), package VARCHAR(32), verified_by_human BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE).

title: Layout: IPC DRC + violation readback via kicad-ipc-rs (loop check step)
description: What survives of the kicad-ipc-rs plan after de-risk: it's an EDITING/INSPECTION library (can't create boards / add footprints / assign nets — that's direct-gen's job now), but it CAN move existing footprints, run DRC, and read back violations against a board open in a running KiCad. That's exactly the layout loop's CHECK step (6.5 step 3): read DRC/critical-net violations to drive repairs. Requires KiCad running + IPC enabled (Preferences → Plugins). Targets KiCad 10.0.1. Optional for a first non-iterative board; needed for the iterative loop.
acceptance_criteria: connect to a running KiCad, run DRC on the open board, read back violations as structured data the layout loop consumes
close_reason: DRC readback via headless kicad-cli (not IPC — same de-risk as direct-gen). core::drc: run_drc shells kicad-cli pcb drc --format json --refill-zones, parses into DrcReport {violations/unconnected/parity} with severity helpers (errors/warnings/is_clean). CLI: lob drc <board> reports + exits non-zero on errors. This is the layout loop's check step (6.5 step 3). Surfaced a real latent issue (isolated GND pour -> j54.17 stitching).

title: Parts: PDF datasheet fallback extraction (cited_page)
description: The trust-order fallback tier of fetch_datasheet: when structured CAD/distributor sources are incomplete (e.g. the KiCad LM13700 symbol leaves bias/output/buffer pins UNNAMED), extract pin tables + absolute-max ratings from the datasheet PDF and populate cited_page with the real page number. Sourced only from a distributor-API datasheet URL (which okm.3 now captures). Completes the pin-name gaps the CAD sources leave. DESIGN.md 3.5, MCP.md 1.
acceptance_criteria: given a part with a datasheet URL, extract pin names/numbers + abs-max ratings with cited_page; fills the gaps the KiCad symbol left for LM13700

title: P3: Panel order tracking (panel_orders Dolt table; lob panel status/mark-ordered)
description: DESIGN.md 7.5: neither SendCutSend nor OSH Cut exposes a public order API (upload-to-web-app only, unlike JLCPCB/Mouser/DigiKey) — so panel ORDERING stays manual (human uploads the generated DXF + places the order). What's automatable is TRACKING that manual step so it isn't lost. panel_orders table in the same Dolt store as inventory (module, dxf_path/commit ref, vendor, status: not_ordered|ordered|shipped|received, ordered_at, tracking_ref, notes). CLI: 'lob panel status <module>' reads state; 'lob panel mark-ordered <module> --vendor oshcut --tracking <ref>' updates it. Deferred-not-designed-away: if a vendor adds an API, mark-ordered becomes an API call updating the same table — no schema change.
acceptance_criteria: panel_orders table in Dolt; lob panel status + mark-ordered work; status transitions tracked; DXF path/commit recorded per order

title: Parts: license handling policy (metadata, not a pipeline gate)
description: Per LIBRARIES.md: a library's license is INFORMATIONAL metadata surfaced to the user, NOT a pipeline gate — legion-of-bom doesn't police how end users use a library in their own designs. The one real exposure is if legion-of-bom itself bundles/redistributes library files in its own repo (CC-BY-SA 'collection' clause → same-license + attribution retained). Open item: before we VOUCH for any 'license not confirmed' source (KiCad official is confirmed CC-BY-SA 4.0; DigiKey/JLCPCB/SnapEDA/Eurorack repos are unconfirmed) in docs or tooling defaults, do a real license check. See LIBRARIES.md.
acceptance_criteria: a decided policy: license as surfaced metadata not a gate; redistribution handled if we bundle; a checklist for confirming a source before it becomes a recommended default
close_reason: Policy decided (LIBRARIES.md): a library's license is informational metadata surfaced to the user, NOT a pipeline gate — legion-of-bom doesn't police end-user usage. Only exposure is redistribution (CC-BY-SA 'collection' clause if we bundle library files). Verify a source before vouching (KiCad official confirmed CC-BY-SA 4.0). No license enforcement in the pipeline.

title: BOM: accuracy/verification — airtight before ordering
description: BOM correctness must be airtight before any real order: right part, right qty, right footprint, cross-checked against the verified parts library. Supersedes the old Phase 4 'BOM accuracy hardening' task now that BOM is its own epic. DESIGN.md 9.4.
acceptance_criteria: BOM verified against the parts library; qty/footprint/MPN mismatches flagged; blocks nothing at Phase 0 but gates real ordering

title: MCP: submit_for_approval (human touchpoint); NO place_order tool
description: submit_for_approval packages design+BOM+cost+sourcing into a human-reviewable summary. CRITICAL: place_order is NOT agent-callable — no such MCP tool exists at all; ordering is a manual human action outside the MCP surface. Building one later is a deliberate separate decision, never a default the surface grows into. MCP.md 2.1.

title: MCP: gated tools — layout, generate_bom (inherit core verification gate)
description: layout (iterative loop, DESIGN.md 6) and generate_bom (live pricing/stock from JLCPCB/Mouser/DigiKey) are gated: require open-questions checklist clear + all used parts verified_by_human=TRUE. Gate is core-enforced (same as CLI), tool just inherits it and returns blocking items on failure. MCP.md 2, 2.2.

title: MCP: ungated tools — create_project, research_topology, search_part, fetch_datasheet, define_circuit
description: create_project (scaffold repo from PanelProfile), research_topology (real reference circuits + citations), search_part (distributor records incl datasheet URL), fetch_datasheet (into global parts library), define_circuit (SKiDL vs verified data). MCP.md 2.

title: MCP: pipeline tools — validate, simulate (reuse Phase 0 stages)
description: Expose the existing core validate + simulate stages as MCP tools. These already exist from Phase 0; this is the MCP wrapping. MCP.md 2.

title: MCP: server scaffold (crates/mcp) over legion-of-bom-core
description: Stand up the local MCP server crate wrapping the core library; nothing MCP-only, everything delegates to core (DESIGN.md 2.2). MCP.md 2.

title: Epic: MCP agent interface (crates/mcp)
description: Agent-facing MCP server over the SAME legion-of-bom-core (local-first, not hosted SaaS). Lets an agent go prompt -> research -> define -> simulate -> layout -> BOM autonomously, but NEVER place a real order (no place_order tool exists — human-only, outside the MCP surface). Nothing may look verified without being verified: gated tools inherit the core parts-verification gate. Full spec in MCP.md. Supersedes the thin Phase 2 'expose over MCP' stub.

title: Parts: human verification workflow (confirm extraction once per part)
description: Lightweight review that sets verified_by_human: present extracted pinout/ratings table + citation/link, human confirms or corrects once per PART (not per circuit — global reuse). Same shape as the slew-limiter open-questions checklist, tool-enforced instead of doc-enforced. MCP.md 3.
close_reason: Human verification workflow: 'lob parts show <mpn>' presents extracted pins/ratings/datasheet + status; 'lob parts verify <mpn> --by' confirms ONCE per part (global, reused across projects). Tool-enforced version of the slew-limiter open-questions checklist.

title: Parts: cross-check safety/money data (pins, abs-max) from 2 independent sources
description: For pin assignments and absolute-max ratings specifically (error -> physical damage / bad respin), fetch from two independent sources where possible (distributor CAD lib + manufacturer PDF) and FLAG mismatches rather than silently picking one. title: Layout: decide 3D model library sourcing for connectors + collision checks

title: layout: replace HPWL with Steiner-tree wirelength in the placement score
description:
layout::measure computes signal_hpwl_mm (half-perimeter wirelength) and score() weights it. The routability-driven placement literature is clear that Steiner-tree wirelength (StWL) correlates with actual routed wirelength substantially better than HPWL, and that wirelength alone does not capture local congestion at all — see the two estimation papers in [[legion-of-bom-REFS]].

DELIBERATELY DEFERRED. It improves the weakest term in the score, but that term is not currently causing trouble: since the tiered rules landed (legion-of-bom-avg), rule violations dominate attempt selection and HPWL only breaks ties. Worth doing when either (a) rule-clean boards start differing only by wirelength and the choices look wrong, or (b) we add congestion/routability to the score, at which point HPWL's blindness to congestion becomes the limiting factor.

Cheapest version: rectilinear minimum spanning tree as a Steiner approximation over each net's placed pads — no router involvement, same shape as the current per-net loop in measure().

title: refs: academic grounding for layout automation (constraint-driven, PCB placement, PDN)
description:
Verified 2026-07-26. Cite these rather than re-deriving; where marked ABSTRACT ONLY the body was not read (ACM DL 403).

CONSTRAINT-DRIVEN LAYOUT — the lineage crates/core/src/rules.rs sits in:
- Malavasi, Charbon, Felt, Sangiovanni-Vincentelli, 'Automation of IC layout with analog constraints', IEEE TCAD 15(8):923-941, 1996. Foundational formulation.
- Chang et al., 'A Top-Down, Constraint-Driven Design Methodology for Analog Integrated Circuits' (Berkeley). https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-1-4757-2233-8_13
- ALIGN: Dhar, Kunal, Li, Madhusudan, Poojary, Sharma, Xu, Burns, Harjani, Hu, Kirkpatrick, Mukherjee, Sapatnekar, Yaldiz. IEEE Design & Test 38(2):8-18, 2021. https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.10682 — derives constraints hierarchically FROM THE NETLIST rather than hand annotation, which is what decoupling_pairs does in miniature.
- MAGICAL: automatic constraint extraction from an unannotated netlist. https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/dc7241bb084c979aec6e1dd8cbf8f09b39fbc12b

PCB-SPECIFIC (closest to our problem; IC literature does not transfer cleanly):
- Liu, Agnesina, Ren, 'Challenges for Automating PCB Layout', ISPD 2024. https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3626184.3635285 — ABSTRACT ONLY.
- Tsou, Lin, Hung, Chang, 'Modern Automatic PCB Placement with Complex Constraints', DAC 2024. https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3649329.3663495 — ABSTRACT ONLY. Journal extension: https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/11195800/
- 'Constraint Graph-Based PCB Legalization Considering Dense, Heterogeneous, Irregular-Shaped, and Any-Oriented Components', DAC 2025. https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1109/DAC63849.2025.11133304 — irregular shapes and arbitrary orientation, i.e. exactly our rotated-header problem.
- 'An analytical approach and fine-tuning strategy for PCB placement optimization'. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S016792602500224X — the three-stage architecture (global -> legalization -> fine-tuning) we are missing a stage of.

PLACEMENT OBJECTIVE:
- 'Wirelength and congestion estimation for routability-driven placement' https://www.researchgate.net/publication/221031529
- 'Fast and Accurate Routing Demand Estimation' https://www.researchgate.net/publication/221339455
  Both: wirelength alone does not capture congestion; Steiner-tree WL correlates with routed WL far better than HPWL.

POWER INTEGRITY:
- Altium PDN decoupling: https://resources.altium.com/p/decoupling-strategies-for-pdn — proximity is a PROXY; the objective is loop inductance. A cap 2mm away with poor vias can beat one 5mm away with good vias.
- 'Hierarchical Decoupling Capacitor Optimization for PDN of 2.5D ICs', arXiv 2407.04737 — RL over frequency/time-domain co-analysis. Far beyond us, but confirms the objective is impedance, not millimetres.

title: DipTrace native import (.dch/.dip) — blocked on a proprietary binary format
description:
To get connectivity (a netlist, hence schematic/ERC/simulation) out of the SuperSynthesis modules, not just their layout, we would need the DipTrace source.

BLOCKER, verified: .dch and .dip are proprietary BINARY files — a .dch starts with magic \\x07DTSCHEM followed by length-prefixed UTF-16LE strings and undocumented records. There is no public spec. Reverse-engineering it is a large, fragile job that breaks on any DipTrace version bump.

BETTER PATHS, in order:
1. Export from DipTrace itself to an interchange format (it can write netlists, PADS/P-CAD/Eagle, Specctra DSN). Needs a DipTrace licence + a manual step per module, but is reliable and gives real connectivity. If the upstream project will publish an exported netlist alongside the binaries, that is the cheapest fix of all.
2. Recover connectivity from the gerbers by tracing copper and matching pads to the CPL. Doable in principle, genuinely hard, and produces nets with no names or intent.
3. Reverse-engineer the binary. Last resort.

Until one of those lands, [[legion-of-bom-u7p]] gets the layout, BOM and placement from the fab package, which covers re-use and ordering; only schematic/ERC/simulation are missing.

title: Schematic: draw feedback paths as loops, not another vertical trunk
description: Layout ranks parts left-to-right by BFS hops from the input, so a feedback net (slew_limiter: SLEW_NODE back to the OTA inverting input) is drawn as just another vertical trunk. An experienced reader looks for the feedback topology around the active device and will not see it. Genuinely hard — it needs loop detection in the net graph plus a routing style that carries the return path over or under the forward path. Low priority; the diagram is readable without it once [[legion-of-bom-sto]] (pin names) and [[legion-of-bom-373]] (multi-unit split) land.

The local 'Forestry' head shipped: crate legion-of-bom-web (crates/web) — an axum 0.8 + Preact/Vite SPA dashboard (Understory stack) wrapping the SAME core (DESIGN 2.2), localhost + no auth (DESIGN 2.5), run via 'lob serve'. p58.1 shared read model core::project::ProjectView (CLI status/circuits refactored onto it — nothing web-only). p58.2 axum skeleton + SPA embed (rust-embed 'embed-assets', CLI feature → self-contained binary). p58.3 read API (repo/circuits/detail/bom-from-cached-netlist/orders) + traversal-guarded /artifacts serving. p58.4 read-only Preact browser (project list → circuit detail: renders/guide/vbom embedded, BOM table w/ live-pricing toggle, order status). p58.5 metadata-only editing: POST /api/edit → toml_edit format-preserving write of brand+build-copy+kit → git STAGE (never commit, per user + conservative profile), UI editors + StagedNote. ACCEPTANCE MET: renders projects+artifacts read-only from the same core; editing limited to metadata w/ a git round-trip; no auth/remote/topology-editing. Follow-ups (own beads): panel-labels + deeper part/order editing (round 2). Note: brand+build-copy edits verified; UI not visually rendered (no headless browser) — open http://127.0.0.1:8080. title: Expose OTA IABC as a pedalkernel control so the VC/CV slew sweep cross-checks too
description: Nuance found: pedalkernel's OTA (ca3080) IABC is a fixed MODEL parameter, so cross-engine validation (ef4.4) checks slew at a FIXED bias only — the VC/CV rate sweep stays ngspice-side. To cross-check the voltage-controlled behaviour, pedalkernel would need to expose IABC (the OTA bias) as a knob/control driven by a CV input in the .pedal DSL. Upstream change in pedalkernel (~/src/pedalkernel/pedalkernel). Lower priority; the fixed-rate slew cross-check (ef4.4) is already strong.

title: Eurorack panel: rail-aligned mounting slots (not 2 left holes)
description: EurorackPanel default mounting holes are 2 round holes on the left (4 for >=8HP). Real Eurorack panels use oval slots at top+bottom aligned to the rack rails for adjustability. Improve the default hole/slot pattern per the Doepfer mechanical spec.

title: Generated footprints trigger lib_footprint_mismatch (cosmetic) — suppress/reconcile
description: kicad-cli DRC warns lib_footprint_mismatch on generated boards because our placed footprint instance (flipped, nets injected, pad uuids added) doesn't byte-match the library master it references. Cosmetic — doesn't affect gerbers/manufacturing — but noisy. Options: carry a proper 'footprint changed from library' marker, or emit a footprint id that doesn't claim library parity, or accept it. Low priority; investigate the least-surprising option once more boards exist.

title: Parametric brand identity — curated brand kit (DESIGN 7.9)
description: Boards/panels should read as designed products, not raw pipeline output — even the fully-automatic ones. Same automatable/curated split as 7.8: (1) Automatable parametric layer — a small fixed set of house-style rules: consistent silkscreen typography, logo placement as a FUNCTION of panel dimensions (e.g. bottom-center, N% of panel width, M mm from edge) not a fixed pixel position, consistent border/frame, defined finish/color palette per product line — applied programmatically to every board via the same PanelSpec/silkscreen (6.10) path. (2) Stays manual/curated — illustration, one-off artwork, genuine creative choices. The risk this names: a system that INVENTS its own placement/spacing heuristics reads as generated no matter how correct; 'curated, not generated' comes from the rules being designed ONCE by a human and applied consistently, not from clever automation. Practical shape: a small brand kit (logo as scalable vector so it holds across HP widths / enclosure sizes, legend typography, the placement-rule set) stored ONCE as a shared asset referenced by every PanelSpec (Eurorack, Guitar Pedal, ...), not duplicated per product line. It's cross-project brand identity, so it likely belongs with the other shared/global concerns (parts library, panel-order tracking), not inside a per-circuit repo — storage mechanism (Dolt vs a brand/ dir in legion-of-bom) is an open detail, not resolved in DESIGN.
